lines.text: ut haec trementi questus ore constitit
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="11">ut haec trementi questus ore constitit</l>
<l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="12">insignibus raptis puer,</l>
<l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="13">inpube corpus, quale posset inpia</l>
<l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="14">mollire Thracum pectora:</l>
<l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="15">Canidia, brevibus illigata viperis</l>
<l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="16">crinis et incomptum caput,</l>
<l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="17">iubet sepulcris caprificos erutas,</l>
<l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="18">iubet cupressos funebris</l>

lines.text: et uncta turpis ova ranae Sanguine
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="19">et uncta turpis ova ranae Sanguine</l>
<l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="20">plumamque nocturnae strigis</l>
<l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="21">herbasque, quas Iolcos atque Hiberia</l>
<l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="22">mittit venenorum ferax,</l>

lines.text: et ossa ab ore rapta ieiunae canis
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="23">et ossa ab ore rapta ieiunae canis</l>
<l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="24">flammis aduri Colchicis.</l>

lines.text: at expedita Sagana, per totam domum
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="25">at expedita Sagana, per totam domum</l>
<l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="26">spargens Avernalis aquas,</l>
<l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="27">horret capillis ut marinus asperis</l>
<l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="28">echinus aut Laurens aper.</l>
<l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="29">abacta nulla Veia conscientia</l>
<l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="30">ligonibus duris humum</l>
<l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="31">exhauriebat, ingemens laboribus,</l>
<l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="32">quo posset infossus puer</l>

lines.text: longo die bis terque mutatae dapis
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="33">longo die bis terque mutatae dapis</l>
<l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="34">inemori spectaculo,</l>

lines.text: cum promineret ore, quantum exstant aqua
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="35">cum promineret ore, quantum exstant aqua</l>
<l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="36">suspensa mento corpora;</l>

lines.text: exsucta uti medulla et aridum iecur
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="37">exsucta uti medulla et aridum iecur</l>
<l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="38">amoris esset poculum,</l>
<l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="39">interminato cum semel fixae cibo</l>
<l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="40">intabuissent pupulae.</l>
<l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="41">non defuisse masculae libidinis</l>
<l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="42">Ariminensem Foliam</l>
<l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="43">et otiosa credidit Neapolis</l>
<l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="44">et omne vicinum oppidum,</l>
<l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="45">quae sidera excantata voce Thessala</l>
<l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="46">lunamque caelo deripit.</l>
<l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="47">hic inresectum saeva dente livido</l>
<l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="48">Canidia rodens pollicem</l>

lines.text: quid dixit aut quid tacuit? “o rebus meis
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="49">quid dixit aut quid tacuit? “o rebus meis</l>
<l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="50">non infideles arbitrae,</l>

lines.text: Nox et Diana, quae silentium regis,
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="51">Nox et Diana, quae silentium regis,</l>
<l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="52">arcana cum fiunt sacra,</l>

lines.text: nunc, nunc adeste, nunc in hostilis domos
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="53">nunc, nunc adeste, nunc in hostilis domos</l>
<l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="54">iram atque numen vertite.</l>
<l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="55">formidulosis cum latent silvis ferae</l>
<l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="56">dulci sopore languidae,</l>
<l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="57">senem, quod omnes rideant, adulterum</l>
<l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="58">latrent Suburanae canes</l>
<l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="59">nardo perunctum, quale non perfectius</l>
<l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="60">meae laborarint manus.</l>

lines.text: quid accidit? cur dira barbarae minus
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="61">quid accidit? cur dira barbarae minus</l>
<l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="62">venena Medeae valent,</l>
<l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="63">quibus Superbam fugit ulta paelicem,</l>
<l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="64">magni Creontis filiam,</l>

lines.text: cum palla, tabo munus imbutum, novam
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="65">cum palla, tabo munus imbutum, novam</l>
<l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="66">incendio nuptam abstulit?</l>

lines.text: atqui nec herba nec latens in asperis
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="67">atqui nec herba nec latens in asperis</l>
<l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="68">radix fefellit me locis.</l>
<l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="69">indormit unctis omnium cubilibus</l>
<l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="70">oblivione paelicum?</l>
<l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="71">a, a, solutus ambulat veneficae</l>
<l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="72">scientioris carmine.</l>
<l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="73">non usitatis, Vare, potionibus,</l>
<l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="74">o multa fleturum caput,</l>

lines.text: ad me recurres nec vocata mens tua
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="75">ad me recurres nec vocata mens tua</l>
<l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="76">Marsis redibit vocibus.</l>
<l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="77">maius parabo, maius infundam tibi</l>
<l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="78">fastidienti poculum</l>
<l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="79">priusque caelum Sidet inferius mari</l>
<l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="80">tellure porrecta super</l>

lines.text: quam non amore sic meo flagres uti
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="81">quam non amore sic meo flagres uti</l>
<l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="82">bitumen atris ignibus.”</l>

lines.text: sub haec puer iam non, ut ante, mollibus
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="83">sub haec puer iam non, ut ante, mollibus</l>
<l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="84">lenire verbis inpias,</l>
<l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="85">sed dubius unde rumperet silentium,</l>
<l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="86">misit Thyesteas preces:</l>

lines.text: “venena maga non fas nefasque, non valent
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="87">“venena maga non fas nefasque, non valent</l>
<l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="88">convertere humanam vicem.</l>
<l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="89">diris agam vos: dira detestatio</l>
<l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="90">nulla expiatur victima.</l>
<l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="91">quin, ubi perire iussus exspiravero,</l>
<l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="92">nocturnus occurram Furor</l>
<l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="93">petamque voltus umbra curvis unguibus,</l>
<l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="94">quae vis deorum est Manium,</l>
<l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="95">et inquietis adsidens praecordiis</l>
<l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="96">pavore somnos auferam.</l>

lines.text: vos turba vicatim hinc et hinc saxis petens
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="97">vos turba vicatim hinc et hinc saxis petens</l>
<l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="98">contundet obscaenas anus;</l>
<l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="99">post insepulta membra different lupi</l>
<l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="100">et Esquilinae alites</l>

lines.text: neque hoc parentes, heu mihi superstites,
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="101">neque hoc parentes, heu mihi superstites,</l>
<l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="102">effugerit spectaculum.”</l>

edition: Friedrich Vollmer; Teubner, Leipzig 1912

lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="1">Quid inmerentis hospites vexas, canis</l>
<l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="2">ignavos adversum lupos?</l>

lines.text: quin huc inanis, si potes, vertis minas
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="3">quin huc inanis, si potes, vertis minas</l>
<l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="4">et me remorsurum petis?</l>

lines.text: nam qualis aut Molossus aut fulvos Lacon,
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="5">nam qualis aut Molossus aut fulvos Lacon,</l>
<l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="6">amica vis pastoribus,</l>

lines.text: agam per altas aure sublata nivis
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="7">agam per altas aure sublata nivis</l>
<l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="8">quaecumque praecedet fera;</l>

lines.text: tu, cum timenda voce complesti nemus,
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="9">tu, cum timenda voce complesti nemus,</l>
<l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="10">proiectum odoraris cibum.</l>

lines.text: cave, cave, namque in malos asperrimus
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="11">cave, cave, namque in malos asperrimus</l>
<l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="12">parata tollo cornua,</l>
<l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="13">qualis Lycambae spretus infido gener</l>
<l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="14">aut acer hostis Bupalo.</l>

lines.text: an si quis atro dente me petiverit,
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="15">an si quis atro dente me petiverit,</l>
<l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="16">inultus ut flebo puer?</l>

edition: Friedrich Vollmer; Teubner, Leipzig 1912

lines.text: Quo, quo scelesti ruitis? aut cur dexteris
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="1">Quo, quo scelesti ruitis? aut cur dexteris</l>
<l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="2">aptantur enses conditi?</l>
<l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="3">parumne campis atque Neptuno super</l>
<l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="4">fusum est Latini sanguinis,</l>
<l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="5">non ut superbas invidae Karthaginis</l>
<l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="6">Romanus arces ureret,</l>
<l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="7">intactus aut Britannus ut descenderet</l>
<l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="8">sacra catenatus via,</l>

lines.text: sed ut Secundum vota Parthorum sua
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="9">sed ut Secundum vota Parthorum sua</l>
<l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="10">Vrbs haec periret dextera?</l>

lines.text: neque hic lupis mos nec fuit leonibus
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="11">neque hic lupis mos nec fuit leonibus</l>
<l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="12">umquam nisi in dispar feris.</l>

lines.text: furorne caecos an rapit vis acrior
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="13">furorne caecos an rapit vis acrior</l>
<l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="14">an culpa? responsum date.</l>

lines.text: tacent et albus ora pallor inficit
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="15">tacent et albus ora pallor inficit</l>
<l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="16">mentesque perculsae Stupent.</l>

lines.text: sic est: acerba fata Romanos agunt
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="17">sic est: acerba fata Romanos agunt</l>
<l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="18">scelusque fraternae necis,</l>

lines.text: ut inmerentis fluxit in terram Remi
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="19">ut inmerentis fluxit in terram Remi</l>
<l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="20">sacer nepotibus cruor.</l>

edition: Friedrich Vollmer; Teubner, Leipzig 1912

lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="1">Rogare longo putidam te saeculo,</l>
<l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="2">viris quid enervet meas,</l>

lines.text: cum sit tibi dens ater et rugis vetus
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="3">cum sit tibi dens ater et rugis vetus</l>
<l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="4">frontem senectus exaret</l>
<l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="5">hietque turpis inter aridas natis</l>
<l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="6">podex velut crudae bovis.</l>

lines.text: sed incitat me pectus et mammae putres
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="7">sed incitat me pectus et mammae putres</l>
<l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="8">equina quales ubera</l>
<l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="9">venterque mollis et femur tumentibus</l>
<l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="10">exile suris additum.</l>
<l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="11">esto beata, funus atque imagines</l>
<l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="12">ducant triumphales tuom</l>
<l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="13">nec sit marita, quae rotundioribus</l>
<l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="14">onusta bacis ambulet.</l>

lines.text: quid? quod libelli Stoici inter Sericos
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="15">quid? quod libelli Stoici inter Sericos</l>
<l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="16">iacere pulvillos amant,</l>
<l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="17">inlitterati num minus nervi rigent</l>
<l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="18">minusve languet fascinum?</l>

lines.text: quod ut superbo provoces ab inguine,
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="19">quod ut superbo <corr>provoces</corr> ab inguine,</l>
<l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="20">ore adlaborandum est tibi.</l>

edition: Friedrich Vollmer; Teubner, Leipzig 1912

lines.text: Quando repositum Caecubum ad festas dapes
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="1">Quando repositum Caecubum ad festas dapes</l>
<l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="2">victore laetus Caesare</l>
<l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="3">tecum sub alta—sic Iovi gratum—domo,</l>
<l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="4">beate Maecenas, bibam</l>
<l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="5">sonante mixtum tibiis carmen lyra,</l>
<l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="6">hac Dorium, illis barbarum?</l>

lines.text: ut nuper, actus cum freto Neptunius
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="7">ut nuper, actus cum freto Neptunius</l>
<l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="8">dux fugit ustis navibus</l>
<l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="9">minatus Vrbi vincla, quae detraxerat</l>
<l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="10">servis amicus perfidis.</l>
<l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="11">Romanus eheu—posteri negabitis—</l>
<l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="12">emancipatus feminae</l>

lines.text: fert vallum et arma miles et spadonibus
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="13">fert vallum et arma miles et spadonibus</l>
<l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="14">servire rugosis potest</l>
<l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="15">interque signa turpe militaria</l>
<l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="16">sol adspicit conopium.</l>

lines.text: ad hunc frementis verterunt bis mille equos
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="17">ad hunc frementis verterunt bis mille equos</l>
<l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="18">Galli canentes Caesarem</l>
<l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="19">hostiliumque navium portu latent</l>
<l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="20">puppes sinistrorsum citae.</l>
<l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="21">io Triumphe, tu moraris aureos</l>
<l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="22">currus et intactas boves?</l>
<l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="23">io Triumphe, nec Iugurthino parem</l>
<l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="24">bello reportasti ducem</l>
<l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="25">neque Africanum, cui super Karthaginem</l>
<l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="26">virtus Sepulcrum condidit.</l>
<l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="27">terra marique victus hostis Punico</l>

lines.text: By proffer'd wealth to tempt Myrtoan seas,
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="13">By proffer'd wealth to tempt Myrtoan seas,</l>

lines.text: The timorous captain of a Cyprian bark.
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="14">The timorous captain of a Cyprian bark.</l>

lines.text: The winds that make Icarian billows dark
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="15">The winds that make Icarian billows dark</l>

lines.text: The merchant fears, and hugs the rural ease
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="16">The merchant fears, and hugs the rural ease</l>

lines.text: Of his own village home; but soon, ashamed
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="17">Of his own village home; but soon, ashamed</l>

lines.text: Of penury, he refits his batter'd craft.
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="18">Of penury, he refits his batter'd craft.</l>

lines.text: There is, who thinks no scorn of Massic draught,
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="19">There is, who thinks no scorn of Massic draught,</l>

lines.text: Who robs the daylight of an hour unblamed,
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="20">Who robs the daylight of an hour unblamed,</l>

lines.text: Now stretch'd beneath the arbute on the sward,
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="21">Now stretch'd beneath the arbute on the sward,</l>

lines.text: Now by some gentle river's sacred spring;
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="22">Now by some gentle river's sacred spring;</l>

lines.text: Some love the camp, the clarion's joyous ring,
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="23">Some love the camp, the clarion's joyous ring,</l>

lines.text: And battle, by the mother's soul abhorr'd.
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="24">And battle, by the mother's soul abhorr'd.</l>

lines.text: See, patient waiting in the clear keen air,
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="25">See, patient waiting in the clear keen air,</l>

lines.text: The hunter, thoughtless of his delicate bride,
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="26">The hunter, thoughtless of his delicate bride,</l>

lines.text: Whether the trusty hounds a stag have eyed,
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="27">Whether the trusty hounds a stag have eyed,</l>

lines.text: Or the fierce Marsian boar has burst the snare.
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="28">Or the fierce Marsian boar has burst the snare.</l>

lines.text: To me the artist's meed, the ivy wreath
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="29">To me the artist's meed, the ivy wreath</l>

lines.text: Is very heaven: me the sweet cool of woods,
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="30">Is very heaven: me the sweet cool of woods,</l>

lines.text: Where Satyrs frolic with the Nymphs, secludes
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="31">Where Satyrs frolic with the Nymphs, secludes</l>

lines.text: From rabble rout, so but Euterpe's breath
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="32">From rabble rout, so but Euterpe's breath</l>

lines.text: Fail not the flute, nor Polyhymnia fly
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="33">Fail not the flute, nor Polyhymnia fly</l>

lines.text: Averse from stringing new the Lesbian lyre.
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="34">Averse from stringing new the Lesbian lyre.</l>

lines.text: O, write my name among that minstrel choir,
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="35">O, write my name among that minstrel choir,</l>

lines.text: And my proud head shall strike upon the sky!
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="36">And my proud head shall strike upon the sky!</l>

edition: John Conington; George Bell and Sons, London 1882

lines.text: Enough of snow and hail at last
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="1">Enough of snow and hail at last</l>

lines.text: The sire has sent in vengeance down:
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="2">The sire has sent in vengeance down:</l>

lines.text: His bolts, at his own temple cast,
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="3">His bolts, at his own temple cast,</l>
<l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="4">Appall'd the town,</l>

lines.text: Appall'd the lands, lest Pyrrha's time
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="5">Appall'd the lands, lest <placeName key="perseus,Pyrrha">Pyrrha</placeName>'s time</l>

lines.text: Return, with all its monstrous sights,
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="6">Return, with all its monstrous sights,</l>

lines.text: When Proteus led his flocks to climb
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="7">When Proteus led his flocks to climb</l>
<l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="8">The flatten'd heights,</l>

lines.text: When fish were in the elm-tops caught,
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="9">When fish were in the elm-tops caught,</l>

lines.text: Where once the stock-dove wont to bide,
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="10">Where once the stock-dove wont to bide,</l>

lines.text: And does were floating, all distraught,
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="11">And does were floating, all distraught,</l>
<l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="12">Adown the tide.</l>

lines.text: Old Tiber, hurl'd in tumult back
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="13">Old <placeName key="tgn,1130786">Tiber</placeName>, hurl'd in tumult back</l>

lines.text: From mingling with the Etruscan main,
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="14">From mingling with the Etruscan main,</l>

lines.text: Has threaten'd Numa's court with wrack
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="15">Has threaten'd Numa's court with wrack</l>
<l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="16">And Vesta's fane.</l>

lines.text: Roused by his Ilia's plaintive woes,
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="17">Roused by his <placeName key="tgn,5001986">Ilia</placeName>'s plaintive woes,</l>

lines.text: He vows revenge for guiltless blood,
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="18">He vows revenge for guiltless blood,</l>

lines.text: And, spite of Jove, his banks o'erflows,
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="19">And, spite of Jove, his banks o'erflows,</l>
<l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="20">Uxorious flood.</l>

lines.text: Yes, Fame shall tell of civic steel
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="21">Yes, Fame shall tell of civic steel</l>

lines.text: That better Persian lives had spilt,
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="22">That better Persian lives had spilt,</l>

lines.text: To youths, whose minish'd numbers feel
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="23">To youths, whose minish'd numbers feel</l>
<l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="24">Their parents' guilt.</l>

lines.text: What god shall Rome invoke to stay
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="25">What god shall <placeName key="perseus,Rome">Rome</placeName> invoke to stay</l>
<l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="26">Her fall? Can suppliance overbear</l>

lines.text: The ear of Vesta, turn'd away
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="27">The ear of Vesta, turn'd away</l>
<l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="28">From chant and prayer?</l>
<l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="29">Who comes, commission'd to atone</l>

lines.text: For crime like ours? at length appear,
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="30">For crime like ours? at length appear,</l>

lines.text: A cloud round thy bright shoulders thrown,
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="31">A cloud round thy bright shoulders thrown,</l>
<l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="32">Apollo seer!</l>
<l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="33">Or Venus, laughter-loving dame,</l>

lines.text: Round whom gay Loves and Pleasures fly;
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="34">Round whom gay Loves and Pleasures fly;</l>

lines.text: Or thou, if slighted sons may claim
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="35">Or thou, if slighted sons may claim</l>
<l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="36">A parent's eye,</l>

lines.text: O weary with thy long, long game,
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="37">O weary with thy long, long game,</l>

lines.text: Who lov'st fierce shouts and helmets bright,
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="38">Who lov'st fierce shouts and helmets bright,</l>

lines.text: And Moorish warrior's glance of flame
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="39">And Moorish warrior's glance of flame</l>
<l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="40">Or e'er he smite!</l>

lines.text: Or Maia's son, if now awhile
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="41">Or <placeName key="tgn,1049816">Maia</placeName>'s son, if now awhile</l>

lines.text: In youthful guise we see thee here,
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="42">In youthful guise we see thee here,</l>
<l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="43">Caesar's avenger—such the style</l>
<l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="44">Thou deign'st to bear;</l>

lines.text: Late be thy journey home, and long
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="45">Late be thy journey home, and long</l>
<l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="46">Thy sojourn with <placeName key="perseus,Rome">Rome</placeName>'s family;</l>

lines.text: Nor let thy wrath at our great wrong
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="47">Nor let thy wrath at our great wrong</l>
<l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="48">Lend wings to fly.</l>

lines.text: Here take our homage, Chief and Sire;
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="49">Here take our homage, Chief and Sire;</l>

lines.text: Here wreathe with bay thy conquering brow,
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="50">Here wreathe with bay thy conquering brow,</l>

lines.text: And bid the prancing Mede retire,
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="51">And bid the prancing <placeName key="tgn,1045322">Mede</placeName> retire,</l>
<l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="52">Our Caesar thou!</l>

edition: John Conington; George Bell and Sons, London 1882

lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="1">Thus may <placeName key="tgn,1000112">Cyprus</placeName>' heavenly queen,</l>

lines.text: Thus Helen's brethren, stars of brightest sheen,
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="2">Thus Helen's brethren, stars of brightest sheen,</l>

lines.text: Guide thee! May the sire of wind
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="3">Guide thee!  May the sire of wind</l>

lines.text: Each truant gale, save only Zephyr, bind!
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="4">Each truant gale, save only Zephyr, bind!</l>

lines.text: So do thou, fair ship, that ow'st
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="5">So do thou, fair ship, that ow'st</l>

lines.text: Virgil, thy precious freight, to Attic coast,
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="6">Virgil, thy precious freight, to Attic coast,</l>

lines.text: Safe restore thy loan and whole,
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="7">Safe restore thy loan and whole,</l>

lines.text: And save from death the partner of my soul!
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="8">And save from death the partner of my soul!</l>

lines.text: Oak and brass of triple fold
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="9">Oak and brass of triple fold</l>

lines.text: Encompass'd sure that heart, which first made bold
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="10">Encompass'd sure that heart, which first made bold</l>

lines.text: To the raging sea to trust
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="11">To the raging sea to trust</l>

lines.text: A fragile bark, nor fear'd the Afric gust
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="12">A fragile bark, nor fear'd the Afric gust</l>

lines.text: With its Northern mates at strife,
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="13">With its Northern mates at strife,</l>

lines.text: Nor Hyads' frown, nor South-wind fury-rife,
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="14">Nor Hyads' frown, nor South-wind fury-rife,</l>
<l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="15">Mightiest power that <placeName key="perseus,Hadria">Hadria</placeName> knows,</l>

lines.text: Wills he the waves to madden or compose.
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="16">Wills he the waves to madden or compose.</l>

lines.text: What had Death in store to awe
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="17">What had Death in store to awe</l>

lines.text: Those eyes, that huge sea-beasts unmelting saw,
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="18">Those eyes, that huge sea-beasts unmelting saw,</l>

lines.text: Saw the swelling of the surge,
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="19">Saw the swelling of the surge,</l>

lines.text: And high Ceraunian cliffs, the seaman's scourge?
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="20">And high Ceraunian cliffs, the seaman's scourge?</l>
<l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="21">Heaven's high providence in vain</l>

lines.text: Has sever'd countries with the estranging main,
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="22">Has sever'd countries with the estranging main,</l>
<l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="23">If our vessels ne'ertheless</l>

lines.text: With reckless plunge that sacred bar transgress.
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="24">With reckless plunge that sacred bar transgress.</l>

lines.text: Daring all, their goal to win,
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="25">Daring all, their goal to win,</l>

lines.text: Men tread forbidden ground, and rush on sin:
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="26">Men tread forbidden ground, and rush on sin:</l>
<l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="27">Daring all, Prometheus play'd</l>

lines.text: His wily game, and fire to man convey'd;
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="28">His wily game, and fire to man convey'd;</l>

lines.text: Soon as fire was stolen away,
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="29">Soon as fire was stolen away,</l>

lines.text: Pale Fever's stranger host and wan Decay
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="30">Pale Fever's stranger host and wan Decay</l>
<l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="31">Swept o'er earth's polluted face,</l>

lines.text: And slow Fate quicken'd Death's once halting pace.
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="32">And slow Fate quicken'd Death's once halting pace.</l>
<l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="33">Daedalus the void air tried</l>

lines.text: On wings, to humankind by Heaven denied;
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="34">On wings, to humankind by Heaven denied;</l>

lines.text: Acheron's bar gave way with ease
lines.xml:
<l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="35">
                        <placeName key="tgn,1120946">Acheron</placeName>'s bar gave way with ease</l>

lines.text: Before the arm of labouring Hercules.
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="36">Before the arm of labouring Hercules.</l>

lines.text: Nought is there for man too high;
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="37">Nought is there for man too high;</l>

lines.text: Our impious folly e'en would climb the sky,
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="38">Our impious folly e'en would climb the sky,</l>

lines.text: Braves the dweller on the steep,
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="39">Braves the dweller on the steep,</l>

lines.text: Nor lets the bolts of heavenly vengeance sleep.
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="40">Nor lets the bolts of heavenly vengeance sleep.</l>

edition: John Conington; George Bell and Sons, London 1882

lines.text: The touch of Zephyr and of Spring has loosen'd Winter's thrall;
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="1">The touch of Zephyr and of Spring has loosen'd Winter's thrall;</l>

lines.text: The well-dried keels are wheel'd again to sea:
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="2">The well-dried keels are wheel'd again to sea:</l>

lines.text: The ploughman cares not for his fire, nor cattle for their stall,
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="3">The ploughman cares not for his fire, nor cattle for their stall,</l>

lines.text: And frost no more is whitening all the lea.
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="4">And frost no more is whitening all the lea.</l>

lines.text: Now Cytherea leads the dance, the bright moon overhead;
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="5">Now Cytherea leads the dance, the bright moon overhead;</l>

lines.text: The Graces and the Nymphs, together knit,
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="6">The Graces and the Nymphs, together knit,</l>

lines.text: With rhythmic feet the meadow beat, while Vulcan, fiery red,
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="7">With rhythmic feet the meadow beat, while <placeName key="tgn,1050339">Vulcan</placeName>, fiery red,</l>

lines.text: Heats the Cyclopian forge in Aetna's pit.
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="8">Heats the Cyclopian forge in <placeName key="tgn,7003867">Aetna</placeName>'s pit.</l>

lines.text: 'Tis now the time to wreathe the brow with branch of myrtle green,
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="9">'Tis now the time to wreathe the brow with branch of myrtle green,</l>

lines.text: Or flowers, just opening to the vernal breeze;
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="10">Or flowers, just opening to the vernal breeze;</l>

lines.text: Now Faunus claims his sacrifice among the shady treen,
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="11">Now Faunus claims his sacrifice among the shady treen,</l>

lines.text: Lambkin or kidling, which soe'er he please.
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="12">Lambkin or kidling, which soe'er he please.</l>

lines.text: Pale Death, impartial, walks his round: he knocks at cottage-gate
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="13">Pale Death, impartial, walks his round: he knocks at cottage-gate</l>

lines.text: And palace-portal. Sestius, child of bliss!
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="14">And palace-portal.  Sestius, child of bliss!</l>

lines.text: How should a mortal's hopes be long, when short his being's date?
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="15">How should a mortal's hopes be long, when short his being's date?</l>

lines.text: Lo here! the fabulous ghosts, the dark abyss,
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="16">Lo here! the fabulous ghosts, the dark abyss,</l>

lines.text: The void of the Plutonian hall, where soon as e'er you go,
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="17">The void of the Plutonian hall, where soon as e'er you go,</l>

lines.text: No more for you shall leap the auspicious die
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="18">No more for you shall leap the auspicious die</l>

lines.text: To seat you on the throne of wine; no more your breast shall glow
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="19">To seat you on the throne of wine; no more your breast shall glow</l>

lines.text: For Lycidas, the star of every eye.
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="20">For Lycidas, the star of every eye.</l>

edition: John Conington; George Bell and Sons, London 1882

lines.text: What slender youth, besprinkled with perfume,
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="1">What slender youth, besprinkled with perfume,</l>

lines.text: Courts you on roses in some grotto's shade?
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="2">Courts you on roses in some grotto's shade?</l>
<l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="3">Fair <placeName key="perseus,Pyrrha">Pyrrha</placeName>, say, for whom</l>
<l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="4">Your yellow hair you braid,</l>

lines.text: So trim, so simple! Ah! how oft shall he
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="5">So trim, so simple! Ah! how oft shall he</l>

lines.text: Lament that faith can fail, that gods can change,
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="6">Lament that faith can fail, that gods can change,</l>
<l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="7">Viewing the rough black sea</l>
<l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="8">With eyes to tempests strange,</l>

lines.text: Who now is basking in your golden smile,
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="9">Who now is basking in your golden smile,</l>

lines.text: And dreams of you still fancy-free, still kind,
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="10">And dreams of you still fancy-free, still kind,</l>

lines.text: Poor fool, nor knows the guile
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="11">Poor fool, nor knows the guile</l>
<l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="12">Of the deceitful wind!</l>

lines.text: Woe to the eyes you dazzle without cloud
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="13">Woe to the eyes you dazzle without cloud</l>

lines.text: Untried! For me, they show in yonder fane
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="14">Untried! For me, they show in yonder fane</l>
<l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="15">My dripping garments, vow'd</l>

lines.text: To Him who curbs the main.
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="16">To Him who curbs the main.</l>

edition: John Conington; George Bell and Sons, London 1882

lines.text: Not I, but Varius:—he, of Homer's brood
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="1">Not I, but Varius:—he, of Homer's brood</l>

lines.text: A tuneful swan, shall bear you on his wing,
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="2">A tuneful swan, shall bear you on his wing,</l>

lines.text: Your tale of trophies, won by field or flood,
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="3">Your tale of trophies, won by field or flood,</l>
<l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="4">Mighty alike to sing.</l>

lines.text: Not mine such themes, Agrippa; no, nor mine
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="5">Not mine such themes, Agrippa; no, nor mine</l>

lines.text: To chant the Wrath that fill'd Pelides' breast,
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="6">To chant the Wrath that fill'd Pelides' breast,</l>

lines.text: Nor dark Ulysses' wanderings o'er the brine,
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="7">Nor dark Ulysses' wanderings o'er the brine,</l>
<l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="8">Nor Pelops' house unblest.</l>

lines.text: Vast were the task, I feeble; inborn shame,
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="9">Vast were the task, I feeble; inborn shame,</l>

lines.text: And she, who makes the peaceful lyre submit,
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="10">And she, who makes the peaceful lyre submit,</l>

lines.text: Forbid me to impair great Caesar's fame
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="11">Forbid me to impair great Caesar's fame</l>

lines.text: And yours by my weak wit.
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="12">And yours by my weak wit.</l>

lines.text: But who may fitly sing of Mars array'd
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="13">But who may fitly sing of Mars array'd</l>

lines.text: In adamant mail, or Merion, black with dust
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="14">In adamant mail, or Merion, black with dust</l>

lines.text: Of Troy, or Tydeus' son by Pallas' aid
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="15">Of <placeName key="tgn,7014164">Troy</placeName>, or Tydeus' son by <placeName key="tgn,2565867">Pallas</placeName>' aid</l>
<l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="16">Strong against gods to thrust?</l>

lines.text: Feasts are my theme, my warriors maidens fair,
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="17">Feasts are my theme, my warriors maidens fair,</l>

lines.text: Who with pared nails encounter youths in fight;
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="18">Who with pared nails encounter youths in fight;</l>

lines.text: Be Fancy free or caught in Cupid's snare,
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="19">Be Fancy free or caught in Cupid's snare,</l>
<l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="20">Her temper still is light.</l>

edition: John Conington; George Bell and Sons, London 1882

lines.text: Let others Rhodes or Mytilene sing,
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="1">Let others <placeName key="tgn,2616128">Rhodes</placeName> or <placeName key="tgn,7002672">Mytilene</placeName> sing,</l>

lines.text: Or Ephesus, or Corinth, set between
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="2">Or <placeName key="tgn,7002499">Ephesus</placeName>, or <placeName key="tgn,7010734">Corinth</placeName>, set between</l>

lines.text: Two seas, or Thebes, or Delphi, for its king
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="3">Two seas, or <placeName key="perseus,Thebes">Thebes</placeName>, or <placeName key="perseus,Delphi">Delphi</placeName>, for its king</l>

lines.text: Each famous, or Thessalian Tempe green;
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="4">Each famous, or Thessalian Tempe green;</l>

lines.text: There are who make chaste Pallas' virgin tower
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="5">There are who make chaste Pallas' virgin tower</l>

lines.text: The daily burden of unending song,
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="6">The daily burden of unending song,</l>

lines.text: And search for wreaths the olive's rifled bower:
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="7">And search for wreaths the olive's rifled bower:</l>

lines.text: The praise of Juno sounds from many a tongue,
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="8">The praise of Juno sounds from many a tongue,</l>

lines.text: Telling of Argos' steeds, Mycenae's gold.
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="9">Telling of <placeName key="perseus,Argos">Argos</placeName>' steeds, <placeName key="perseus,Mycenae">Mycenae</placeName>'s gold.</l>

lines.text: For me stern Sparta forges no such spell,
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="10">For me stern <placeName key="perseus,Sparta">Sparta</placeName> forges no such spell,</l>

lines.text: No, nor Larissa's plain of richest mould,
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="11">No, nor Larissa's plain of richest mould,</l>

lines.text: As bright Albunea echoing from her cell.
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="12">As bright Albunea echoing from her cell.</l>

lines.text: O headlong Anio! O Tiburnian groves,
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="13">O headlong Anio!  O Tiburnian groves,</l>

lines.text: And orchards saturate with shifting streams!
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="14">And orchards saturate with shifting streams!</l>

lines.text: Look how the clear fresh south from heaven removes
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="15">Look how the clear fresh south from heaven removes</l>

lines.text: The tempest, nor with rain perpetual teems!
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="16">The tempest, nor with rain perpetual teems!</l>

lines.text: You too be wise, my Plancus: life's worst cloud
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="17">You too be wise, my Plancus: life's worst cloud</l>

lines.text: Will melt in air, by mellow wine allay'd,
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="18">Will melt in air, by mellow wine allay'd,</l>

lines.text: Dwell you in camps, with glittering banners proud,
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="19">Dwell you in camps, with glittering banners proud,</l>

lines.text: Or 'neath your Tibur's canopy of shade.
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="20">Or 'neath your <placeName key="perseus,Tibur">Tibur</placeName>'s canopy of shade.</l>

lines.text: When Teucer fled before his father's frown
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="21">When Teucer fled before his father's frown</l>

lines.text: From Salamis, they say his temples deep
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="22">From <placeName key="tgn,7002340">Salamis</placeName>, they say his temples deep</l>

lines.text: He dipp'd in wine, then wreath'd with poplar crown,
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="23">He dipp'd in wine, then wreath'd with poplar crown,</l>

lines.text: And bade his comrades lay their grief to sleep:
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="24">And bade his comrades lay their grief to sleep:</l>

lines.text: “Where Fortune bears us, than my sire more kind,
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="25">“Where Fortune bears us, than my sire more kind,</l>

lines.text: There let us go, my own, my gallant crew.
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="26">There let us go, my own, my gallant crew.</l>

lines.text: 'Tis Teucer leads, 'tis Teucer breathes the wind;
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="27">'Tis Teucer leads, 'tis Teucer breathes the wind;</l>

lines.text: No more despair; Apollo's word is true.
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="28">No more despair; Apollo's word is true.</l>
<l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="29">Another <placeName key="tgn,7002340">Salamis</placeName> in kindlier air</l>

lines.text: Shall yet arise. Hearts, that have borne with me
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="30">Shall yet arise.  Hearts, that have borne with me</l>

lines.text: Worse buffets! drown today in wine your care;
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="31">Worse buffets! drown today in wine your care;</l>

lines.text: To-morrow we recross the wide, wide sea!”
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="32">To-morrow we recross the wide, wide sea!”</l>

edition: John Conington; George Bell and Sons, London 1882

lines.xml:
<l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="1">
                        <placeName key="tgn,7016631">Lydia</placeName>, by all above,</l>

lines.text: Why bear so hard on Sybaris, to ruin him with love?
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="2">Why bear so hard on <placeName key="perseus,Sybaris">Sybaris</placeName>, to ruin him with love?</l>

lines.text: What change has made him shun
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="3">What change has made him shun</l>

lines.text: The playing-ground, who once so well could bear the dust and sun?
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="4">The playing-ground, who once so well could bear the dust and sun?</l>
<l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="5">Why does he never sit</l>

lines.text: On horseback in his company, nor with uneven bit
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="6">On horseback in his company, nor with uneven bit</l>
<l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="7">His Gallic courser tame?</l>

lines.text: Why dreads he yellow Tiber, as 'twould sully that fair frame?
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="8">Why dreads he yellow <placeName key="tgn,1130786">Tiber</placeName>, as 'twould sully that fair frame?</l>
<l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="9">Like poison loathes the oil,</l>

lines.text: His arms no longer black and blue with honourable toil,
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="10">His arms no longer black and blue with honourable toil,</l>
<l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="11">He who erewhile was known</l>

lines.text: For quoit or javelin oft and oft beyond the limit thrown?
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="12">For quoit or javelin oft and oft beyond the limit thrown?</l>

lines.text: Why skulks he, as they say
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="13">Why skulks he, as they say</l>

lines.text: Did Thetis' son before the dawn of Ilion's fatal day,
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="14">Did Thetis' son before the dawn of <placeName key="tgn,7002329">Ilion</placeName>'s fatal day,</l>
<l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="15">For fear the manly dress</l>

lines.text: Should fling him into danger's arms, amid the
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="16">Should fling him into danger's arms, amid the</l>
<l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="17">Lycian press?</l>

edition: John Conington; George Bell and Sons, London 1882

lines.text: See, how it stands, one pile of snow,
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="1">See, how it stands, one pile of snow,</l>
<l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="2">Soracte! 'neath the pressure yield</l>

lines.text: Its groaning woods; the torrents' flow
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="3">Its groaning woods; the torrents' flow</l>

lines.text: With clear sharp ice is all congeal'd.
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="4">With clear sharp ice is all congeal'd.</l>

lines.text: Heap high the logs, and melt the cold,
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="5">Heap high the logs, and melt the cold,</l>

lines.text: Good Thaliarch; draw the wine we ask,
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="6">Good Thaliarch; draw the wine we ask,</l>
<l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="7">That mellower vintage, four-year-old,</l>

lines.text: From out the cellar'd Sabine cask.
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="8">From out the cellar'd <placeName key="tgn,7021127">Sabine</placeName> cask.</l>

lines.text: The future trust with Jove; when he
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="9">The future trust with Jove; when he</l>

lines.text: Has still'd the warring tempests' roar
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="10">Has still'd the warring tempests' roar</l>

lines.text: On the vex'd deep, the cypress-tree
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="11">On the vex'd deep, the cypress-tree</l>

lines.text: And aged ash are rock'd no more.
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="12">And aged ash are rock'd no more.</l>

lines.text: O, ask not what the morn will bring,
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="13">O, ask not what the morn will bring,</l>

lines.text: But count as gain each day that chance
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="14">But count as gain each day that chance</l>

lines.text: May give you; sport in life's young spring,
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="15">May give you; sport in life's young spring,</l>

lines.text: Nor scorn sweet love, nor merry dance,
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="16">Nor scorn sweet love, nor merry dance,</l>

lines.text: While years are green, while sullen eld
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="17">While years are green, while sullen eld</l>

lines.text: Is distant. Now the walk, the game,
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="18">Is distant.  Now the walk, the game,</l>

lines.text: The whisper'd talk at sunset held,
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="19">The whisper'd talk at sunset held,</l>

lines.text: Each in its hour, prefer their claim.
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="20">Each in its hour, prefer their claim.</l>

lines.text: Sweet too the laugh, whose feign'd alarm
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="21">Sweet too the laugh, whose feign'd alarm</l>
<l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="22">The hiding-place of beauty tells,</l>

lines.text: The token, ravish'd from the arm
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="23">The token, ravish'd from the arm</l>

lines.text: Or finger, that but ill rebels.
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="24">Or finger, that but ill rebels.</l>

edition: John Conington; George Bell and Sons, London 1882

lines.text: Grandson of Atlas, wise of tongue,
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="1">Grandson of Atlas, wise of tongue,</l>

lines.text: O Mercury, whose wit could tame
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="2">O Mercury, whose wit could tame</l>

lines.text: Man's savage youth by power of song
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="3">Man's savage youth by power of song</l>
<l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="4">And plastic game!</l>

lines.text: Thee sing I, herald of the sky,
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="5">Thee sing I, herald of the sky,</l>

lines.text: Who gav'st the lyre its music sweet,
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="6">Who gav'st the lyre its music sweet,</l>

lines.text: Hiding whate'er might please thine eye
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="7">Hiding whate'er might please thine eye</l>
<l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="8">In frolic cheat.</l>

lines.text: See, threatening thee, poor guileless child,
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="9">See, threatening thee, poor guileless child,</l>
<l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="10">Apollo claims, in angry tone,</l>

lines.text: His cattle;—all at once he smiled,
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="11">His cattle;—all at once he smiled,</l>
<l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="12">His quiver gone.</l>

lines.text: Strong in thy guidance, Hector's sire
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="13">Strong in thy guidance, Hector's sire</l>
<l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="14">Escaped the Atridae, pass'd between</l>
<l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="15">Thessalian tents and warders' fire,</l>
<l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="16">Of all unseen,</l>

lines.text: Thou lay'st unspotted souls to rest;
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="17">Thou lay'st unspotted souls to rest;</l>

lines.text: Thy golden rod pale spectres know;
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="18">Thy golden rod pale spectres know;</l>

lines.text: Blest power! by all thy brethren blest,
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="19">Blest power! by all thy brethren blest,</l>
<l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="20">Above, below!</l>

edition: John Conington; George Bell and Sons, London 1882

lines.text: Ask not ('tis forbidden knowledge), what our destined term of years,
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="1">Ask not ('tis forbidden knowledge), what our destined term of years,</l>

lines.text: Mine and yours; nor scan the tables of your Babylonish seers.
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="2">Mine and yours; nor scan the tables of your Babylonish seers.</l>

lines.text: Better far to bear the future, my Leuconoe, like the past,
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="3">Better far to bear the future, my Leuconoe, like the past,</l>

lines.text: Whether Jove has many winters yet to give, or this our last;
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="4">Whether Jove has many winters yet to give, or this our last;</l>

lines.text: This, that makes the Tyrrhene billows spend their strength against the shore.
lines.xml:
<l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="5">
                        <emph>This</emph>, that makes the Tyrrhene billows spend their strength against the shore.</l>

lines.text: Strain your wine and prove your wisdom; life is short; should hope be more?
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="6">Strain your wine and prove your wisdom; life is short; should hope be more?</l>

lines.text: In the moment of our talking, envious time has ebb'd away.
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="7">In the moment of our talking, envious time has ebb'd away.</l>

lines.text: Seize the present; trust tomorrow e'en as little as you may.
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="8">Seize the present; trust tomorrow e'en as little as you may.</l>

edition: John Conington; George Bell and Sons, London 1882

lines.text: What man, what hero, Clio sweet,
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="1">What man, what hero, <placeName key="tgn,2244631">Clio</placeName> sweet,</l>

lines.text: On harp or flute wilt thou proclaim?
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="2">On harp or flute wilt thou proclaim?</l>

lines.text: What god shall echo's voice repeat
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="3">What god shall echo's voice repeat</l>
<l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="4">In mocking game</l>
<l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="5">To <placeName key="tgn,2003822">Helicon</placeName>'s sequester'd shade,</l>

lines.text: Or Pindus, or on Haemus chill,
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="6">Or Pindus, or on <placeName key="tgn,7011635">Haemus</placeName> chill,</l>

lines.text: Where once the hurrying woods obey'd
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="7">Where once the hurrying woods obey'd</l>
<l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="8">The minstrel's will,</l>

lines.text: Who, by his mother's gift of song,
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="9">Who, by his mother's gift of song,</l>

lines.text: Held the fleet stream, the rapid breeze,
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="10">Held the fleet stream, the rapid breeze,</l>
<l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="11">And led with blandishment along</l>
<l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="12">The listening trees?</l>

lines.text: Whom praise we first? the sire on high,
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="13">Whom praise we first? the sire on high,</l>

lines.text: Who gods and men unerring guides,
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="14">Who gods and men unerring guides,</l>

lines.text: Who rules the sea, the earth, the sky,
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="15">Who rules the sea, the earth, the sky,</l>
<l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="16">Their times and tides.</l>

lines.text: No mightier birth may he beget;
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="17">No mightier birth may he beget;</l>

lines.text: No like, no second has he known;
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="18">No like, no second has he known;</l>

lines.text: Yet nearest to her sire's is set
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="19">Yet nearest to her sire's is set</l>

<l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="20">
                        <placeName key="tgn,2070580">Minerva</placeName>'s throne.</l>

lines.text: Nor yet shall Bacchus pass unsaid,
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="21">Nor yet shall <placeName key="tgn,2097807">Bacchus</placeName> pass unsaid,</l>

lines.text: Bold warrior, nor the virgin foe
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="22">Bold warrior, nor the virgin foe</l>

lines.text: Of savage beasts, nor Phoebus, dread
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="23">Of savage beasts, nor Phoebus, dread</l>
<l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="24">With deadly bow.</l>

lines.text: Alcides too shall be my theme,
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="25">Alcides too shall be my theme,</l>

lines.text: And Leda's twins, for horses he,
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="26">And Leda's twins, for horses he,</l>

lines.text: He famed for boxing; soon as gleam
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="27">He famed for boxing; soon as gleam</l>
<l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="28">Their stars at sea,</l>

lines.text: The lash'd spray trickles from the steep,
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="29">The lash'd spray trickles from the steep,</l>

lines.text: The wind sinks down, the storm-cloud flies,
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="30">The wind sinks down, the storm-cloud flies,</l>

lines.text: The threatening billow on the deep
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="31">The threatening billow on the deep</l>
<l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="32">Obedient lies.</l>

lines.text: Shall now Quirinus take his turn,
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="33">Shall now Quirinus take his turn,</l>

lines.text: Or quiet Numa, or the state
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="34">Or quiet <placeName key="tgn,2033144">Numa</placeName>, or the state</l>

lines.text: Proud Tarquin held, or Cato stern,
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="35">Proud Tarquin held, or <placeName key="tgn,2226609">Cato</placeName> stern,</l>
<l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="36">By death made great?</l>

lines.text: Ay, Regulus and the Scaurian name,
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="37">Ay, Regulus and the Scaurian name,</l>

lines.text: And Paullus, who at Cannae gave
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="38">And Paullus, who at <placeName key="tgn,7009090">Cannae</placeName> gave</l>

lines.text: His glorious soul, fair record claim,
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="39">His glorious soul, fair record claim,</l>
<l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="40">For all were brave.</l>
<l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="41">Thee, Furius, and Fabricius, thee,</l>

lines.text: Rough Curius too, with untrimm'd beard,
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="42">Rough Curius too, with untrimm'd beard,</l>
<l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="43">Your sires' transmitted poverty</l>
<l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="44">To conquest rear'd.</l>

<l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="45">
                        <placeName key="tgn,7013998">Marcellus</placeName>' fame, its up-growth hid,</l>

lines.text: Springs like a tree; great Julius' light
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="46">Springs like a tree; great <placeName key="tgn,2008628">Julius</placeName>' light</l>

lines.text: Shines, like the radiant moon amid
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="47">Shines, like the radiant moon amid</l>
<l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="48">The lamps of night.</l>

lines.text: Dread Sire and Guardian of man's race,
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="49">Dread Sire and Guardian of man's race,</l>

lines.text: To thee, O Jove, the Fates assign
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="50">To thee, O Jove, the Fates assign</l>

lines.text: Our Caesar's charge; his power and place
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="51">Our Caesar's charge; his power and place</l>
<l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="52">Be next to thine.</l>
<l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="53">Whether the Parthian, threatening <placeName key="tgn,7013962">Rome</placeName>,</l>

lines.text: His eagles scatter to the wind.
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="54">His eagles scatter to the wind.</l>

lines.text: Or follow to their eastern home
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="55">Or follow to their eastern home</l>
<l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="56">Cathay and Ind,</l>

lines.text: Thy second let him rule below
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="57">Thy second let him rule below</l>

lines.text: Thy car shall shake the realms above;
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="58">Thy car shall shake the realms above;</l>
<l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="59">Thy vengeful bolts shall overthrow</l>
<l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="60">Each guilty grove.</l>

edition: John Conington; George Bell and Sons, London 1882

lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="1">Telephus—you praise him still,</l>

lines.text: His waxen arms, his rosy-tinted neck;
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="2">His waxen arms, his rosy-tinted neck;</l>

lines.text: Ah! and all the while I thrill
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="3">Ah! and all the while I thrill</l>

lines.text: With jealous pangs I cannot, cannot check
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="4">With jealous pangs I cannot, cannot check</l>

lines.text: See, my colour comes and goes,
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="5">See, my colour comes and goes,</l>

lines.text: My poor heart flutters, Lydia, and the dew,
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="6">My poor heart flutters, <placeName key="tgn,7016631">Lydia</placeName>, and the dew,</l>

lines.text: Down my cheek soft stealing, shows
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="7">Down my cheek soft stealing, shows</l>

lines.text: What lingering torments rack me through and through.
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="8">What lingering torments rack me through and through.</l>
<l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="9">Oh, 'tis agony te see</l>

lines.text: Those snowwhite shoulders scarr'd in drunken fray,
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="10">Those snowwhite shoulders scarr'd in drunken fray,</l>

lines.text: Or those ruby lips, where he
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="11">Or those ruby lips, where he</l>

lines.text: Has left strange marks, that show how rough his play!
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="12">Has left strange marks, that show how rough his play!</l>
<l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="13">Never, never look to find</l>

lines.text: A faithful heart in him whose rage can harm
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="14">A faithful heart in him whose rage can harm</l>
<l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="15">Sweetest lips, which <placeName key="tgn,2094077">Venus</placeName> kind</l>

lines.text: Has tinctured with her quintessential charm.
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="16">Has tinctured with her quintessential charm.</l>
<l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="17">Happy, happy; happy they</l>

lines.text: Whose living love, untroubled by all strife,
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="18">Whose living love, untroubled by all strife,</l>

lines.text: Binds them till the last sad day,
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="19">Binds them till the last sad day,</l>

lines.text: Nor parts asunder but with parting life!
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="20">Nor parts asunder but with parting life!</l>

edition: John Conington; George Bell and Sons, London 1882

lines.text: O luckless bark! new waves will force you back
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="1">O luckless bark! new waves will force you back</l>

lines.text: To sea. O, haste to make the haven yours!
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="2">To sea.  O, haste to make the haven yours!</l>
<l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="3">E'en now, a helpless wrack,</l>
<l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="4">You drift, despoil'd of oars;</l>

lines.text: The Afric gale has dealt your mast a wound;
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="5">The Afric gale has dealt your mast a wound;</l>

lines.text: Your sailyards groan, nor can your keel sustain,
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="6">Your sailyards groan, nor can your keel sustain,</l>
<l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="7">Till lash'd with cables round,</l>
<l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="8">A more imperious main.</l>

lines.text: Your canvass hangs in ribbons, rent and torn;
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="9">Your canvass hangs in ribbons, rent and torn;</l>

lines.text: No gods are left to pray to in fresh need.
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="10">No gods are left to pray to in fresh need.</l>
<l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="11">A pine of <placeName key="tgn,7016619">Pontus</placeName> born</l>
<l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="12">Of noble forest breed,</l>

lines.text: You boast your name and lineage—madly blind
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="13">You boast your name and lineage—madly blind</l>

lines.text: Can painted timbers quell a seaman's fear?
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="14">Can painted timbers quell a seaman's fear?</l>
<l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="15">Beware! or else the wind</l>

lines.text: Makes you its mock and jeer.
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="16">Makes you its mock and jeer.</l>

lines.text: Your trouble late made sick this heart of mine,
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="17">Your trouble late made sick this heart of mine,</l>

lines.text: And still I love you, still am ill at ease.
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="18">And still I love you, still am ill at ease.</l>

lines.text: O, shun the sea, where shine
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="19">O, shun the sea, where shine</l>
<l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="20">The thick-sown <placeName key="tgn,7011270">Cyclades</placeName>!</l>

edition: John Conington; George Bell and Sons, London 1882

lines.text: When the false swain was hurrying o'er the deep
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="1">When the false swain was hurrying o'er the deep</l>

lines.text: His Spartan hostess in the Idaean bark,
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="2">His Spartan hostess in the Idaean bark,</l>

lines.text: Old Nereus laid the unwilling winds asleep,
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="3">Old Nereus laid the unwilling winds asleep,</l>

lines.text: That all to Fate might hark,
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="4">That all to Fate might hark,</l>

lines.text: Speaking through him:—“Home in ill hour you take
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="5">Speaking through him:—“Home in ill hour you take</l>

lines.text: A prize whom Greece shall claim with troops untold,
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="6">A prize whom <placeName key="tgn,1000074">Greece</placeName> shall claim with troops untold,</l>

lines.text: Leagued by an oath your marriage tie to break
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="7">Leagued by an oath your marriage tie to break</l>
<l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="8">And Priam's kingdom old.</l>

lines.text: Alas! what deaths you launch on Dardan realm!
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="9">Alas! what deaths you launch on Dardan realm!</l>

lines.text: What tolls are waiting, man and horse to tire!
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="10">What tolls are waiting, man and horse to tire!</l>

lines.text: See! Pallas trims her aegis and her helm,
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="11">See! Pallas trims her aegis and her helm,</l>
<l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="12">Her chariot and her ire.</l>

lines.text: Vainly shall you; in Venus' favour strong,
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="13">Vainly shall you; in Venus' favour strong,</l>

lines.text: Your tresses comb, and for your dames divide
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="14">Your tresses comb, and for your dames divide</l>

lines.text: On peaceful lyre the several parts of song;
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="15">On peaceful lyre the several parts of song;</l>
<l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="16">Vainly in chamber hide</l>

lines.text: From spears and Gnossian arrows, barb'd with fate,
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="17">From spears and Gnossian arrows, barb'd with fate,</l>

lines.text: And battle's din, and Ajax in the chase
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="18">And battle's din, and Ajax in the chase</l>

lines.text: Unconquer'd; those adulterous locks, though late,
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="19">Unconquer'd; those adulterous locks, though late,</l>
<l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="20">Shall gory dust deface.</l>

lines.text: Hark! 'tis the death-cry of your race! look back!
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="21">Hark! 'tis the death-cry of your race! look back!</l>

lines.text: Ulysses comes, and Pylian Nestor grey;
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="22">Ulysses comes, and Pylian Nestor grey;</l>

lines.text: See! Salaminian Teucer on your track,
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="23">See! Salaminian Teucer on your track,</l>
<l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="24">And Sthenelus, in the fray</l>

lines.text: Versed, or with whip and rein, should need require,
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="25">Versed, or with whip and rein, should need require,</l>

lines.text: No laggard. Merion too your eyes shall know
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="26">No laggard.  Merion too your eyes shall know</l>

lines.text: From far. Tydides, fiercer than his sire,
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="27">From far. Tydides, fiercer than his sire,</l>
<l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="28">Pursues you, all aglow;</l>

lines.text: Him, as the stag forgets to graze for fright,
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="29">Him, as the stag forgets to graze for fright,</l>

lines.text: Seeing the wolf at distance in the glade,
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="30">Seeing the wolf at distance in the glade,</l>

lines.text: And flies, high panting, you shall fly, despite
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="31">And flies, high panting, you shall fly, despite</l>
<l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="32">Boasts to your leman made.</l>

lines.text: What though Achilles' wrathful fleet postpone
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="33">What though Achilles' wrathful fleet postpone</l>

lines.text: The day of doom to Troy and Troy's proud dames,
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="34">The day of doom to <placeName key="perseus,Troy">Troy</placeName> and <placeName key="perseus,Troy">Troy</placeName>'s proud dames,</l>

lines.text: Her towers shall fall, the number'd winters flown,
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="35">Her towers shall fall, the number'd winters flown,</l>
<l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="36">Wrapp'd in Achaenan flames.”</l>

edition: John Conington; George Bell and Sons, London 1882

lines.text: O lovelier than the lovely dame
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="1">O lovelier than the lovely dame</l>

lines.text: That bore you, sentence as you please
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="2">That bore you, sentence as you please</l>

lines.text: Those scurril verses, be it flame
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="3">Those scurril verses, be it flame</l>

lines.text: Your vengeance craves, or Hadrian seas.
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="4">Your vengeance craves, or Hadrian seas.</l>

lines.text: Not Cybele, nor he that haunts
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="5">Not Cybele, nor he that haunts</l>

lines.text: Rich Pytho, worse the brain confounds,
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="6">Rich <placeName key="tgn,7010770">Pytho</placeName>, worse the brain confounds,</l>
<l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="7">Not Bacchus, nor the Corybants</l>

lines.text: Clash their loud gongs with fiercer sounds
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="8">Clash their loud gongs with fiercer sounds</l>

lines.text: Than savage wrath; nor sword nor spear
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="9">Than savage wrath; nor sword nor spear</l>

lines.text: Appals it, no, nor ocean's frown,
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="10">Appals it, no, nor ocean's frown,</l>

<l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="11">Nor ravening fire, nor <placeName key="tgn,1125260">Jupiter</placeName>
                     </l>
<l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="12">In hideous ruin crashing down.</l>

lines.text: Prometheus, forced, they say, to add
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="13">Prometheus, forced, they say, to add</l>

lines.text: To his prime clay some favourite part
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="14">To his prime clay some favourite part</l>

lines.text: From every kind, took lion mad,
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="15">From every kind, took lion mad,</l>

lines.text: And lodged its gall in man's poor heart.
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="16">And lodged its gall in man's poor heart.</l>
<l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="17">'Twas wrath that laid Thyestes low;</l>
<l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="18">'Tis wrath that oft destruction calls</l>

lines.text: On cities, and invites the foe
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="19">On cities, and invites the foe</l>

lines.text: To drive his plough o'er ruin'd walls.
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="20">To drive his plough o'er ruin'd walls.</l>

lines.text: Then calm your spirit; I can tell
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="21">Then calm your spirit; I can tell</l>

lines.text: How once, when youth in all my veins
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="22">How once, when youth in all my veins</l>

lines.text: Was glowing, blind with rage, I fell
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="23">Was glowing, blind with rage, I fell</l>

lines.text: On friend and foe in ribald strains.
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="24">On friend and foe in ribald strains.</l>

lines.text: Come, let me change my sour for sweet,
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="25">Come, let me change my sour for sweet,</l>
<l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="26">And smile complacent as before:</l>
