<l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="27">Hear me my palinode repeat,</l>

lines.text: And give me back your heart once more.
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="28">And give me back your heart once more.</l>

edition: John Conington; George Bell and Sons, London 1882

lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="1">The pleasures of Lucretilis</l>

lines.text: Tempt Faunus from his Grecian seat;
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="2">Tempt Faunus from his Grecian seat;</l>

lines.text: He keeps my little goats in bliss
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="3">He keeps my little goats in bliss</l>

lines.text: Apart from wind, and rain, and heat.
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="4">Apart from wind, and rain, and heat.</l>

lines.text: In safety rambling o'er the sward
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="5">In safety rambling o'er the sward</l>

lines.text: For arbutes and for thyme they peer,
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="6">For arbutes and for thyme they peer,</l>

lines.text: The ladies of the unfragrant lord,
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="7">The ladies of the unfragrant lord,</l>

lines.text: Nor vipers, green with venom, fear,
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="8">Nor vipers, green with venom, fear,</l>

lines.text: Nor savage wolves, of Mars' own breed,
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="9">Nor savage wolves, of Mars' own breed,</l>
<l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="10">My <placeName key="perseus,Tyndaris">Tyndaris</placeName>, while <placeName key="tgn,1047264">Ustica</placeName>'s dell</l>

lines.text: Is vocal with the silvan reed,
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="11">Is vocal with the silvan reed,</l>

lines.text: And music thrills the limestone fell.
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="12">And music thrills the limestone fell.</l>

lines.text: Heaven is my guardian; heaven approves
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="13">Heaven is my guardian; heaven approves</l>

lines.text: A blameless life, by song made sweet;
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="14">A blameless life, by song made sweet;</l>

lines.text: Come hither, and the fields and groves
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="15">Come hither, and the fields and groves</l>

lines.text: Their horn shall empty at your feet.
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="16">Their horn shall empty at your feet.</l>

lines.text: Here, shelter'd by a friendiy tree,
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="17">Here, shelter'd by a friendiy tree,</l>

lines.text: In Teian measures you shall sing
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="18">In Teian measures you shall sing</l>
<l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="19">Bright Circe and Penelope,</l>

lines.text: Love-smitten both by one sharp sting.
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="20">Love-smitten both by one sharp sting.</l>

lines.text: Here shall you quaff beneath the shade
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="21">Here shall you quaff beneath the shade</l>

lines.text: Sweet Lesbian draughts that injure none,
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="22">Sweet Lesbian draughts that injure none,</l>

lines.text: Nor fear lest Mars the realm invade
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="23">Nor fear lest Mars the realm invade</l>
<l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="24">Of Semele's Thyonian son,</l>

lines.text: Lest Cyrus on a foe too weak
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="25">Lest Cyrus on a foe too weak</l>

lines.text: Lay the rude hand of wild excess,
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="26">Lay the rude hand of wild excess,</l>

lines.text: His passion on your chaplet wreak,
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="27">His passion on your chaplet wreak,</l>
<l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="28">Or spoil your undeserving dress.</l>

edition: John Conington; George Bell and Sons, London 1882

lines.text: Varus, are your trees in planting? put in none before the vine,
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="1">Varus, are your trees in planting? put in none before the vine,</l>

lines.text: In the rich domain of Tibur, by the walls of Catilus;
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="2">In the rich domain of <placeName key="perseus,Tibur">Tibur</placeName>, by the walls of Catilus;</l>

lines.text: There's a power above that hampers all that sober brains design,
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="3">There's a power above that hampers all that sober brains design,</l>

lines.text: And the troubles man is heir to thus are quell'd, and only thus.
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="4">And the troubles man is heir to thus are quell'd, and only thus.</l>

lines.text: Who can talk of want or warfare when the wine is in his head,
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="5">Who can talk of want or warfare when the wine is in his head,</l>

lines.text: Not of thee, good father Bacchus, and of Venus fair and bright?
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="6">Not of thee, good father Bacchus, and of Venus fair and bright?</l>

lines.text: But should any dream of licence, there's a lesson may be read,
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="7">But should any dream of licence, there's a lesson may be read,</l>

lines.text: How 'twas wine that drove the Centaurs with the Lapithae to fight.
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="8">How 'twas wine that drove the Centaurs with the Lapithae to fight.</l>

lines.text: And the Thracians too may warn us; truth and falsehood, good and ill,
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="9">And the Thracians too may warn us; truth and falsehood, good and ill,</l>

lines.text: How they mix them, when the wine-god's hand is heavy on them laid!
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="10">How they mix them, when the wine-god's hand is heavy on them laid!</l>

lines.text: Never, never, gracious Bacchus, may I move thee 'gainst thy will,
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="11">Never, never, gracious Bacchus, may I move thee 'gainst thy will,</l>

lines.text: Or uncover what is hidden in the verdure of thy shade!
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="12">Or uncover what is hidden in the verdure of thy shade!</l>

lines.text: Silence thou thy savage cymbals, and the Berecyntine horn;
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="13">Silence thou thy savage cymbals, and the Berecyntine horn;</l>

lines.text: In their train Self-love still follows, dully, desperately blind,
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="14">In their train Self-love still follows, dully, desperately blind,</l>

lines.text: And Vain-glory, towering upwards in its emptyheaded scorn,
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="15">And Vain-glory, towering upwards in its emptyheaded scorn,</l>

lines.text: And the Faith that keeps no secrets, with a window in its mind.
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="16">And the Faith that keeps no secrets, with a window in its mind.</l>

edition: John Conington; George Bell and Sons, London 1882

lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="1">Cupid's mother, cruel dame,</l>

lines.text: And Semele's Theban boy, and Licence bold,
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="2">And Semele's Theban boy, and Licence bold,</l>
<l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="3">Bid me kindle into flame</l>

lines.text: This heart, by waning passion now left cold.
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="4">This heart, by waning passion now left cold.</l>
<l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="5">O, the charms of Glycera,</l>

lines.text: That hue, more dazzling than the Parian stone!
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="6">That hue, more dazzling than the Parian stone!</l>
<l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="7">O, that sweet tormenting play,</l>

lines.text: That too fair face, that blinds when look'd upon!
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="8">That too fair face, that blinds when look'd upon!</l>

lines.text: Venus comes in all her might,
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="9">Venus comes in all her might,</l>

lines.text: Quits Cyprus for my heart, nor lets me tell
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="10">Quits <placeName key="tgn,1000112">Cyprus</placeName> for my heart, nor lets me tell</l>

lines.text: Of the Parthian, bold in flight,
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="11">Of the Parthian, bold in flight,</l>

lines.text: Nor Scythian hordes, nor aught that breaks her spell.
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="12">Nor Scythian hordes, nor aught that breaks her spell.</l>
<l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="13">Heap the grassy altar up,</l>

lines.text: Bring vervain, boys, and sacred frankincense;
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="14">Bring vervain, boys, and sacred frankincense;</l>
<l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="15">Fill the sacrificial cup;</l>

lines.text: A victim's blood will soothe her vehemence.
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="16">A victim's blood will soothe her vehemence.</l>

edition: John Conington; George Bell and Sons, London 1882

lines.text: Not large my cups, nor rich my cheer,
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="1">Not large my cups, nor rich my cheer,</l>

lines.text: This Sabine wine, which erst I seal'd,
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="2">This <placeName key="tgn,7021127">Sabine</placeName> wine, which erst I seal'd,</l>
<l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="3">That day the applauding theatre</l>
<l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="4">Your welcome peal'd,</l>
<l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="5">Dear knight Maecenas! as 'twere fain</l>
<l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="6">That your paternal river's banks,</l>
<l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="7">And <placeName key="tgn,7001168">Vatican</placeName>, in sportive strain,</l>
<l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="8">Should echo thanks.</l>

lines.text: For you Calenian grapes are press'd,
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="9">For you Calenian grapes are press'd,</l>

lines.text: And Caecuban; these cups of mine
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="10">And Caecuban; these cups of mine</l>
<l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="11">Falernum's bounty ne'er has bless'd,</l>
<l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="12">Nor Formian vine.</l>

edition: John Conington; George Bell and Sons, London 1882

lines.text: Of Dian's praises, tender maidens, tell;
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="1">Of Dian's praises, tender maidens, tell;</l>

lines.text: Of Cynthus' unshorn god, young striplings, sing;
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="2">Of Cynthus' unshorn god, young striplings, sing;</l>
<l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="3">And bright <placeName key="tgn,2013536">Latona</placeName>, well</l>
<l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="4">Beloved of Heaven's high king.</l>

lines.text: Sing her that streams and silvan foliage loves,
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="5">Sing her that streams and silvan foliage loves,</l>

lines.text: Whate'er on Algidus' chill brow is seen,
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="6">Whate'er on Algidus' chill brow is seen,</l>
<l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="7">In Erymanthian groves</l>
<l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="8">Dark-leaved, or Cragus green.</l>

lines.text: Sing Tempe too, glad youths, in strain as loud,
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="9">Sing <placeName key="tgn,7014367">Tempe</placeName> too, glad youths, in strain as loud,</l>

lines.text: And Phoebus' birthplace, and that shoulder fair,
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="10">And Phoebus' birthplace, and that shoulder fair,</l>
<l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="11">His golden quiver proud</l>
<l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="12">And brother's lyre to bear.</l>

lines.text: His arm shall banish Hunger, Plague, and War
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="13">His arm shall banish Hunger, Plague, and War</l>

lines.text: To Persia and to Britain's coast, away
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="14">To <placeName key="tgn,7000231">Persia</placeName> and to <placeName key="tgn,7008653">Britain</placeName>'s coast, away</l>
<l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="15">From <placeName key="perseus,Rome">Rome</placeName> and Caesar far,</l>

lines.text: If you have zeal to pray.
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="16">If you have zeal to pray.</l>

edition: John Conington; George Bell and Sons, London 1882

lines.text: No need of Moorish archer's craft
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="1">No need of Moorish archer's craft</l>

lines.text: To guard the pure and stainless liver;
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="2">To guard the pure and stainless liver;</l>

lines.text: He wants not, Fuscus, poison'd shaft
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="3">He wants not, Fuscus, poison'd shaft</l>
<l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="4">To store his quiver,</l>
<l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="5">Whether he traverse Libyan shoals,</l>
<l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="6">Or <placeName key="tgn,1108814">Caucasus</placeName>, forlorn and horrent,</l>

lines.text: Or lands where far Hydaspes rolls
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="7">Or lands where far <placeName key="tgn,7002541">Hydaspes</placeName> rolls</l>
<l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="8">His fabled torrent.</l>
<l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="9">A wolf, while roaming trouble-free</l>

lines.text: In Sabine wood, as fancy led me,
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="10">In <placeName key="tgn,7021127">Sabine</placeName> wood, as fancy led me,</l>
<l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="11">Unarm'd I sang my Lalage,</l>
<l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="12">Beheld, and fled me.</l>

lines.text: Dire monster! in her broad oak woods
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="13">Dire monster! in her broad oak woods</l>

lines.text: Fierce Daunia fosters none such other,
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="14">Fierce Daunia fosters none such other,</l>

lines.text: Nor Juba's land, of lion broods
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="15">Nor <placeName key="tgn,1094266">Juba</placeName>'s land, of lion broods</l>
<l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="16">The thirsty mother.</l>

lines.text: Place me where on the ice-bound plain
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="17">Place me where on the ice-bound plain</l>

lines.text: No tree is cheer'd by summer breezes,
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="18">No tree is cheer'd by summer breezes,</l>

lines.text: Where Jove descends in sleety rain
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="19">Where Jove descends in sleety rain</l>
<l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="20">Or sullen freezes;</l>

lines.text: Place me where none can live for heat,
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="21">Place me where none can live for heat,</l>
<l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="22">'Neath Phoebus' very chariot plant me,</l>

lines.text: That smile so sweet, that voice so sweet,
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="23">That smile so sweet, that voice so sweet,</l>
<l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="24">Shall still enchant me.</l>

edition: John Conington; George Bell and Sons, London 1882

lines.text: You fly me, Chloe, as o'er trackless hills
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="1">You fly me, Chloe, as o'er trackless hills</l>

lines.text: A young fawn runs her timorous dam to find,
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="2">A young fawn runs her timorous dam to find,</l>
<l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="3">Whom empty terror thrills</l>
<l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="4">Of woods and whispering wind.</l>

lines.text: Whether 'tis Spring's first shiver, faintly heard
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="5">Whether 'tis Spring's first shiver, faintly heard</l>

lines.text: Through the light leaves, or lizards in the brake
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="6">Through the light leaves, or lizards in the brake</l>
<l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="7">The rustling thorns have stirr'd,</l>

lines.text: Her heart, her knees, they quake.
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="8">Her heart, her knees, they quake.</l>

lines.text: Yet I, who chase you, no grim lion am,
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="9">Yet I, who chase you, no grim lion am,</l>

lines.text: No tiger fell, to crush you in my gripe:
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="10">No tiger fell, to crush you in my gripe:</l>

lines.text: Come, learn to leave your dam.
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="11">Come, learn to leave your dam.</l>
<l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="12">For lover's kisses ripe.</l>

edition: John Conington; George Bell and Sons, London 1882

lines.text: Why blush to let our tears unmeasured fall
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="1">Why blush to let our tears unmeasured fall</l>

lines.text: For one so dear? Begin the mournful stave,
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="2">For one so dear?  Begin the mournful stave,</l>

lines.text: Melpomene, to whom the sire of all
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="3">Melpomene, to whom the sire of all</l>
<l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="4">Sweet voice with music gave.</l>

lines.text: And sleeps he then the heavy sleep of death,
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="5">And sleeps he then the heavy sleep of death,</l>
<l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="6">Quintilius?  Piety, twin sister dear</l>

lines.text: Of Justice! naked Truth! unsullied Faith!
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="7">Of Justice! naked Truth! unsullied Faith!</l>

lines.text: When will ye find his peer?
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="8">When will ye find his peer?</l>

lines.text: By many a good man wept, Quintilius dies;
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="9">By many a good man wept, Quintilius dies;</l>

lines.text: By none than you, my Virgil, trulier wept:
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="10">By none than you, my Virgil, trulier wept:</l>

lines.text: Devout in vain, you chide the faithless skies,
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="11">Devout in vain, you chide the faithless skies,</l>
<l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="12">Asking your loan ill-kept.</l>

lines.text: No, though more suasive than the bard of Thrace
lines.xml:
<l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="13">No, though more suasive than the bard of <placeName key="tgn,7002756">Thrace</placeName>
                     </l>

lines.text: You swept the lyre that trees were fain to hear,
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="14">You swept the lyre that trees were fain to hear,</l>

lines.text: Ne'er should the blood revisit his pale face
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="15">Ne'er should the blood revisit his pale face</l>
<l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="16">Whom once with wand severe</l>

lines.text: Mercury has folded with the sons of night,
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="17">Mercury has folded with the sons of night,</l>

lines.text: Untaught to prayer Fate's prison to unseal.
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="18">Untaught to prayer Fate's prison to unseal.</l>

lines.text: Ah, heavy grief! but patience makes more light
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="19">Ah, heavy grief! but patience makes more light</l>
<l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="20">What sorrow may not heal.</l>

edition: John Conington; George Bell and Sons, London 1882

lines.text: The Muses love me: fear and grief,
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="1">The Muses love me: fear and grief,</l>

lines.text: The winds may blow them to the sea;
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="2">The winds may blow them to the sea;</l>

lines.text: Who quail before the wintry chief
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="3">Who quail before the wintry chief</l>

lines.text: Of Scythia's realm, is nought to me.
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="4">Of <placeName key="tgn,6005315">Scythia</placeName>'s realm, is nought to me.</l>
<l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="5">What cloud o'er Tiridates lowers,</l>

lines.text: I care not, I. O, nymph divine
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="6">I care not, I.  O, nymph divine</l>

lines.text: Of virgin springs, with sunniest flowers
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="7">Of virgin springs, with sunniest flowers</l>

lines.text: A chaplet for my Lamia twine,
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="8">A chaplet for my <placeName key="tgn,7010893">Lamia</placeName> twine,</l>

lines.text: Pimplea sweet! my praise were vain
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="9">Pimplea sweet! my praise were vain</l>

lines.text: Without thee. String this maiden lyre,
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="10">Without thee.  String this maiden lyre,</l>

lines.text: Attune for him the Lesbian strain,
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="11">Attune for him the Lesbian strain,</l>

lines.text: O goddess, with thy sister quire!
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="12">O goddess, with thy sister quire!</l>

edition: John Conington; George Bell and Sons, London 1882

lines.text: What, fight with cups that should give joy?
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="1">What, fight with cups that should give joy?</l>
<l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="2">'Tis barbarous; leave such savage ways</l>
<l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="3">To Thracians. Bacchus, shamefaced boy,</l>

lines.text: Is blushing at your bloody frays.
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="4">Is blushing at your bloody frays.</l>

lines.text: The Median sabre! lights and wine!
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="5">The Median sabre! lights and wine!</l>
<l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="6">Was stranger contrast ever seen?</l>

lines.text: Cease, cease this brawling, comrades mine,
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="7">Cease, cease this brawling, comrades mine,</l>

lines.text: And still upon your elbows lean.
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="8">And still upon your elbows lean.</l>

lines.text: Well, shall I take a toper's part
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="9">Well, shall I take a toper's part</l>

lines.text: Of fierce Falernian? let our guest,
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="10">Of fierce Falernian? let our guest,</l>
<l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="11">Megilla's brother, say what dart</l>

lines.text: Gave the death-wound that makes him blest.
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="12">Gave the death-wound that makes him blest.</l>
<l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="13">He hesitates? no other hire</l>

lines.text: Shall tempt my sober brains. Whate'er
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="14">Shall tempt my sober brains.  Whate'er</l>

lines.text: The goddess tames you, no base fire
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="15">The goddess tames you, no base fire</l>
<l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="16">She kindles; 'tis some gentle fair</l>

lines.text: Allures you still. Come, tell me truth,
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="17">Allures you still.  Come, tell me truth,</l>

lines.text: And trust my honour—That the name?
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="18">And trust my honour—That the name?</l>

lines.text: That wild Charybdis yours? Poor youth!
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="19">That wild Charybdis yours?  Poor youth!</l>

lines.text: O, you deserved a better flame!
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="20">O, you deserved a better flame!</l>
<l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="21">What wizard, what Thessalian spell,</l>

lines.text: What god can save you, hamper'd thus?
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="22">What god can save you, hamper'd thus?</l>

lines.text: To cope with this Chimaera fell
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="23">To cope with this Chimaera fell</l>
<l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="24">Would task another Pegasus.</l>

edition: John Conington; George Bell and Sons, London 1882

lines.text: The sea, the earth, the innumerable sand,
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="1">The sea, the earth, the innumerable sand,</l>

lines.text: Archytas, thou couldst measure; now, alas!
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="2">Archytas, thou couldst measure; now, alas!</l>

lines.text: A little dust on Matine shore has spann'd
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="3">A little dust on Matine shore has spann'd</l>

lines.text: That soaring spirit; vain it was to pass
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="4">That soaring spirit; vain it was to pass</l>

lines.text: The gates of heaven, and send thy soul in quest
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="5">The gates of heaven, and send thy soul in quest</l>

lines.text: O'er air's wide realms; for thou hadst yet to die.
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="6">O'er air's wide realms; for thou hadst yet to die.</l>

lines.text: Ay, dead is Pelops' father, heaven's own guest,
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="7">Ay, dead is Pelops' father, heaven's own guest,</l>

lines.text: And old Tithonus, rapt from earth to sky,
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="8">And old Tithonus, rapt from earth to sky,</l>

lines.text: And Minos, made the council-friend of Jove;
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="9">And Minos, made the council-friend of Jove;</l>

lines.text: And Panthus' son has yielded up his breath
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="10">And Panthus' son has yielded up his breath</l>

lines.text: Once more, though down he pluck'd the shield, to prove
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="11">Once more, though down he pluck'd the shield, to prove</l>

lines.text: His prowess under Troy, and bade grim death
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="12">His prowess under <placeName key="perseus,Troy">Troy</placeName>, and bade grim death</l>

lines.text: O'er skin and nerves alone exert its power,
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="13">O'er skin and nerves alone exert its power,</l>

lines.text: Not he, you grant, in nature meanly read.
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="14">Not he, you grant, in nature meanly read.</l>
<l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="15">Yes, all “await the inevitable hour;”</l>

lines.text: The downward journey all one day must tread.
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="16">The downward journey all one day must tread.</l>

lines.text: Some bleed, to glut the war-god's savage eyes;
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="17">Some bleed, to glut the war-god's savage eyes;</l>

lines.text: Fate meets the sailor from the hungry brine;
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="18">Fate meets the sailor from the hungry brine;</l>

lines.text: Youth jostles age in funeral obsequies;
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="19">Youth jostles age in funeral obsequies;</l>

lines.text: Each brow in turn is touch'd by Proserpine.
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="20">Each brow in turn is touch'd by Proserpine.</l>

lines.text: Me, too, Orion's mate, the Southern blast,
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="21">Me, too, Orion's mate, the Southern blast,</l>

lines.text: Whelm'd in deep death beneath the Illyrian wave.
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="22">Whelm'd in deep death beneath the Illyrian wave.</l>

lines.text: But grudge not, sailor, of driven sand to cast
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="23">But grudge not, sailor, of driven sand to cast</l>

lines.text: A handful on my head, that owns no grave.
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="24">A handful on my head, that owns no grave.</l>

lines.text: So, though the eastern tempests loudly threat
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="25">So, though the eastern tempests loudly threat</l>

lines.text: Hesperia's main, may green Venusia's crown
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="26">Hesperia's main, may green <placeName key="perseus,Venusia">Venusia</placeName>'s crown</l>

lines.text: Be stripp'd, while you lie warm; may blessings yet
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="27">Be stripp'd, while you lie warm; may blessings yet</l>

lines.text: Stream from Tarentum's guard, great Neptune, down,
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="28">Stream from <placeName key="tgn,7004100">Tarentum</placeName>'s guard, great Neptune, down,</l>

lines.text: And gracious Jove, into your open lap!
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="29">And gracious Jove, into your open lap!</l>

lines.text: What! shrink you not from crime whose punishment
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="30">What!  shrink you not from crime whose punishment</l>

lines.text: Falls on your innocent children? it may hap
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="31">Falls on your innocent children? it may hap</l>

lines.text: Imperious Fate will make yourself repent.
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="32">Imperious Fate will make yourself repent.</l>

lines.text: My prayers shall reach the avengers of all wrong;
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="33">My prayers shall reach the avengers of all wrong;</l>

lines.text: No expiations shall the curse unbind.
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="34">No expiations shall the curse unbind.</l>

lines.text: Great though your haste, I would not task you long;
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="35">Great though your haste, I would not task you long;</l>

lines.text: Thrice sprinkle dust, then scud before the wind.
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="36">Thrice sprinkle dust, then scud before the wind.</l>

edition: John Conington; George Bell and Sons, London 1882

lines.text: Your heart on Arab wealth is set,
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="1">Your heart on Arab wealth is set,</l>

lines.text: Good Iccius: you would try your steel
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="2">Good Iccius: you would try your steel</l>
<l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="3">On <placeName key="tgn,7016796">Saba</placeName>'s kings, unconquerd yet,</l>

lines.text: And make the Mede your fetters feel.
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="4">And make the <placeName key="tgn,1045322">Mede</placeName> your fetters feel.</l>

lines.text: Come, tell me what barbarian fair
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="5">Come, tell me what barbarian fair</l>

lines.text: Will serve you now, her bridegroom slain?
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="6">Will serve you now, her bridegroom slain?</l>

lines.text: What page from court with essenced hair
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="7">What page from court with essenced hair</l>

lines.text: Will tender you the bowl you drain,
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="8">Will tender you the bowl you drain,</l>

lines.text: Well skill'd to bend the Serian bow
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="9">Well skill'd to bend the Serian bow</l>

lines.text: His father carried? Who shall say
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="10">His father carried? Who shall say</l>

lines.text: That rivers may not uphill flow,
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="11">That rivers may not uphill flow,</l>

lines.text: And Tiber's self return one day,
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="12">And <placeName key="tgn,1130786">Tiber</placeName>'s self return one day,</l>

lines.text: If you would change Panaetius' works,
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="13">If you would change Panaetius' works,</l>

lines.text: That costly purchase, and the clan
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="14">That costly purchase, and the clan</l>

lines.text: Of Socrates, for shields and dirks,
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="15">Of Socrates, for shields and dirks,</l>

lines.text: Whom once we thought a saner man?
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="16">Whom once we thought a saner man?</l>

edition: John Conington; George Bell and Sons, London 1882

lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="1">Come, Cnidian, Paphian Venus, come,</l>
<l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="2">Thy well-beloved <placeName key="tgn,1000112">Cyprus</placeName> spurn,</l>

lines.text: Haste, where for thee in Glycera's home
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="3">Haste, where for thee in Glycera's home</l>
<l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="4">Sweet odours burn.</l>

lines.text: Bring too thy Cupid, glowing warm,
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="5">Bring too thy Cupid, glowing warm,</l>

lines.text: Graces and Nymphs, unzoned and free,
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="6">Graces and Nymphs, unzoned and free,</l>

lines.text: And Youth, that lacking thee lacks charm,
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="7">And Youth, that lacking thee lacks charm,</l>
<l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="8">And Mercury.</l>

edition: John Conington; George Bell and Sons, London 1882

lines.text: What blessing shall the bard entreat
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="1">What blessing shall the bard entreat</l>

lines.text: The god he hallows, as he pours
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="2">The god he hallows, as he pours</l>

lines.text: The winecup? Not the mounds of wheat
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="3">The winecup? Not the mounds of wheat</l>
<l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="4">That load Sardinian threshing floors;</l>
<l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="5">Not Indian gold or ivory—no,</l>

lines.text: Nor flocks that o'er Calabria stray,
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="6">Nor flocks that o'er <placeName key="tgn,7007850">Calabria</placeName> stray,</l>

lines.text: Nor fields that Liris, still and slow,
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="7">Nor fields that Liris, still and slow,</l>
<l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="8">Is eating, unperceived, away.</l>

lines.text: Let those whose fate allows them train
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="9">Let those whose fate allows them train</l>
<l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="10">Calenum's vine; let trader bold</l>

lines.text: From golden cups rich liquor drain
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="11">From golden cups rich liquor drain</l>

lines.text: For wares of Syria bought and sold,
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="12">For wares of <placeName key="tgn,1000140">Syria</placeName> bought and sold,</l>

lines.text: Heaven's favourite, sooth, for thrice a year
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="13">Heaven's favourite, sooth, for thrice a year</l>

lines.text: He comes and goes across the brine
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="14">He comes and goes across the brine</l>
<l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="15">Undamaged.  I in plenty here</l>
<l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="16">On endives, mallows, succory dine.</l>

lines.text: O grant me, Phoebus, calm content,
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="17">O grant me, Phoebus, calm content,</l>
<l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="18">Strength unimpaird, a mind entire,</l>
<l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="19">Old age without dishonour spent,</l>
<l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="20">Nor unbefriended by the lyre!</l>

edition: John Conington; George Bell and Sons, London 1882

lines.text: They call;—if aught in shady dell
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="1">They call;—if aught in shady dell</l>

lines.text: We twain have warbled, to remain
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="2">We twain have warbled, to remain</l>

lines.text: Long months or years, now breathe, my shell,
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="3">Long months or years, now breathe, my shell,</l>
<l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="4">A Roman strain,</l>

lines.text: Thou, strung by Lesbos' minstrel hand,
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="5">Thou, strung by <placeName key="tgn,7002672">Lesbos</placeName>' minstrel hand,</l>

lines.text: The bard, who 'mid the clash of steel,
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="6">The bard, who 'mid the clash of steel,</l>

lines.text: Or haply mooring to the strand
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="7">Or haply mooring to the strand</l>
<l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="8">His batter'd keel,</l>

lines.text: Of Bacchus and the Muses sung,
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="9">Of Bacchus and the Muses sung,</l>

lines.text: And Cupid, still at Venus' side,
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="10">And Cupid, still at Venus' side,</l>
<l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="11">And Lycus, beautiful and young,</l>
<l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="12">Dark-hair'd, dark-eyed.</l>

lines.text: O sweetest lyre, to Phoebus dear,
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="13">O sweetest lyre, to Phoebus dear,</l>
<l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="14">Delight of Jove's high festival,</l>

lines.text: Blest balm in trouble, hail and hear
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="15">Blest balm in trouble, hail and hear</l>
<l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="16">Whene'er I call!</l>

edition: John Conington; George Bell and Sons, London 1882

lines.text: What, Albius! why this passionate despair
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="1">What, Albius! why this passionate despair</l>

lines.text: For cruel Glycera? why melt your voice
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="2">For cruel Glycera? why melt your voice</l>

lines.text: In dolorous strains, because the perjured fair
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="3">In dolorous strains, because the perjured fair</l>
<l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="4">Has made a younger choice?</l>

lines.text: See, narrow-brow'd Lycoris, how she glows
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="5">See, narrow-brow'd Lycoris, how she glows</l>

lines.text: For Cyrus! Cyrus turns away his head
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="6">For Cyrus!  Cyrus turns away his head</l>

lines.text: To Pholoe's frown; but sooner gentle roes
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="7">To Pholoe's frown; but sooner gentle roes</l>
<l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="8">Apulian wolves shall wed,</l>

lines.text: Than Pholoe to so mean a conqueror strike:
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="9">Than Pholoe to so mean a conqueror strike:</l>

lines.text: So Venus wills it; 'neath her brazen yoke
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="10">So Venus wills it; 'neath her brazen yoke</l>

lines.text: She loves to couple forms and minds unlike,
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="11">She loves to couple forms and minds unlike,</l>
<l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="12">All for a heartless joke.</l>

lines.text: For me sweet Love had forged a milder spell;
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="13">For me sweet Love had forged a milder spell;</l>

lines.text: But Myrtale still kept me her fond slave,
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="14">But Myrtale still kept me her fond slave,</l>

lines.text: More stormy she than the tempestuous swell
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="15">More stormy she than the tempestuous swell</l>
<l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="16">That crests <placeName key="tgn,7007850">Calabria</placeName>'s wave.</l>

edition: John Conington; George Bell and Sons, London 1882

lines.text: My prayers were scant, my offerings few,
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="1">My prayers were scant, my offerings few,</l>

lines.text: While witless wisdom fool'd my mind;
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="2">While witless wisdom fool'd my mind;</l>

lines.text: But now I trim my sails anew,
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="3">But now I trim my sails anew,</l>

lines.text: And trace the course I left behind.
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="4">And trace the course I left behind.</l>

lines.text: For lo! the sire of heaven on high,
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="5">For lo! the sire of heaven on high,</l>

lines.text: By whose fierce bolts the clouds are riven,
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="6">By whose fierce bolts the clouds are riven,</l>
<l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="7">Today through an unclouded sky</l>

lines.text: His thundering steeds and car has driven.
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="8">His thundering steeds and car has driven.</l>

lines.text: E'en now dull earth and wandering floods,
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="9">E'en now dull earth and wandering floods,</l>
<l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="10">And Atlas' limitary range,</l>

lines.text: And Styx, and Taenarus' dark abodes
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="11">And Styx, and Taenarus' dark abodes</l>

lines.text: Are reeling. He can lowliest change
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="12">Are reeling.  He can lowliest change</l>

lines.text: And loftiest; bring the mighty down
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="13">And loftiest; bring the mighty down</l>

lines.text: And lift the weak; with whirring flight
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="14">And lift the weak; with whirring flight</l>

lines.text: Comes Fortune, plucks the monarch's crown,
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="15">Comes Fortune, plucks the monarch's crown,</l>

lines.text: And decks therewith some meaner wight.
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="16">And decks therewith some meaner wight.</l>

edition: John Conington; George Bell and Sons, London 1882

lines.text: Lady of Antium, grave and stern!
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="1">Lady of <placeName key="perseus,Antium">Antium</placeName>, grave and stern!</l>

lines.text: O Goddess, who canst lift the low
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="2">O Goddess, who canst lift the low</l>

lines.text: To high estate, and sudden turn
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="3">To high estate, and sudden turn</l>

lines.text: A triumph to a funeral show!
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="4">A triumph to a funeral show!</l>

lines.text: Thee the poor hind that tills the soil
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="5">Thee the poor hind that tills the soil</l>

lines.text: Implores; their queen they own in thee,
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="6">Implores; their queen they own in thee,</l>
<l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="7">Who in Bithynian vessel toil</l>
<l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="8">Amid the vex'd Carpathian sea.</l>

lines.text: Thee Dacians fierce, and Scythian hordes,
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="9">Thee Dacians fierce, and Scythian hordes,</l>

lines.text: Peoples and towns, and Rome, their head,
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="10">Peoples and towns, and <placeName key="perseus,Rome">Rome</placeName>, their head,</l>
<l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="11">And mothers of barbarian lords,</l>

lines.text: And tyrants in their purple dread,
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="12">And tyrants in their purple dread,</l>

lines.text: Lest, spurn'd by thee in scorn, should fall
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="13">Lest, spurn'd by thee in scorn, should fall</l>

lines.text: The state's tall prop, lest crowds on fire
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="14">The state's tall prop, lest crowds on fire</l>

lines.text: To arms, to arms! the loiterers call,
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="15">To arms, to arms! the loiterers call,</l>

lines.text: And thrones be tumbled in the mire.
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="16">And thrones be tumbled in the mire.</l>
<l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="17">Necessity precedes thee still</l>

lines.text: With hard fierce eyes and heavy tramp:
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="18">With hard fierce eyes and heavy tramp:</l>

lines.text: Her hand the nails and wedges fill,
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="19">Her hand the nails and wedges fill,</l>

lines.text: The molten lead and stubborn clamp.
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="20">The molten lead and stubborn clamp.</l>

lines.text: Hope, precious Truth in garb of white,
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="21">Hope, precious Truth in garb of white,</l>

lines.text: Attend thee still, nor quit thy side
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="22">Attend thee still, nor quit thy side</l>

lines.text: When with changed robes thou tak'st thy flight
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="23">When with changed robes thou tak'st thy flight</l>

lines.text: In anger from the homes of pride.
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="24">In anger from the homes of pride.</l>

lines.text: Then the false herd, the faithless fair,
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="25">Then the false herd, the faithless fair,</l>

lines.text: Start backward; when the wine runs dry.
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="26">Start backward; when the wine runs dry.</l>

lines.text: The jocund guests, too light to bear
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="27">The jocund guests, too light to bear</l>
<l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="28">An equal yoke, asunder fly.</l>

lines.text: O shield our Caesar as he goes
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="29">O shield our Caesar as he goes</l>

lines.text: To furthest Britain, and his band,
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="30">To furthest <placeName key="tgn,7008653">Britain</placeName>, and his band,</l>

lines.text: Rome's harvest! Send on Eastern foes
lines.xml:
<l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="31">
                        <placeName key="perseus,Rome">Rome</placeName>'s harvest! Send on Eastern foes</l>

lines.text: Their fear, and on the Red Sea strand!
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="32">Their fear, and on the <placeName key="tgn,7016791">Red Sea</placeName> strand!</l>

lines.text: O wounds that scarce have ceased to run!
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="33">O wounds that scarce have ceased to run!</l>

lines.text: O brother's blood! O iron time!
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="34">O brother's blood!  O iron time!</l>

lines.text: What horror have we left undone?
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="35">What horror have we left undone?</l>

lines.text: Has conscience shrunk from aught of crime?
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="36">Has conscience shrunk from aught of crime?</l>

lines.text: What shrine has rapine held in awe?
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="37">What shrine has rapine held in awe?</l>

lines.text: What altar spared? O haste and beat
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="38">What altar spared?  O haste and beat</l>

lines.text: The blunted steel we yet may draw
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="39">The blunted steel we yet may draw</l>
<l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="40">On Arab and on Massagete!</l>

edition: John Conington; George Bell and Sons, London 1882

lines.text: Bid the lyre and cittern play;
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="1">Bid the lyre and cittern play;</l>

lines.text: Enkindle incense, shed the victim's gore;
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="2">Enkindle incense, shed the victim's gore;</l>
<l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="3">Heaven has watch'd o'er Numida,</l>

lines.text: And brings him safe from far Hispania's shore.
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="4">And brings him safe from far <placeName key="tgn,1000095">Hispania</placeName>'s shore.</l>
<l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="5">Now, returning, he bestows</l>

lines.text: On each dear comrade all the love he can;
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="6">On each dear comrade all the love he can;</l>

lines.text: But to Lamia most he owes,
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="7">But to <placeName key="perseus,Lamia">Lamia</placeName> most he owes,</l>

lines.text: By whose sweet side he grew from boy to man.
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="8">By whose sweet side he grew from boy to man.</l>
<l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="9">Note we in our calendar</l>

lines.text: This festal day with whitest mark from Crete:
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="10">This festal day with whitest mark from <placeName key="tgn,7012056">Crete</placeName>:</l>

lines.text: Let it flow, the old wine-jar,
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="11">Let it flow, the old wine-jar,</l>

lines.text: And ply to Salian time your restless feet.
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="12">And ply to Salian time your restless feet.</l>
<l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="13">Damalis tosses off her wine,</l>

lines.text: But Bassus sure must prove her match tonight.
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="14">But Bassus sure must prove her match tonight.</l>

lines.text: Give us roses all to twine,
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="15">Give us roses all to twine,</l>

lines.text: And parsley green, and lilies deathly white.
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="16">And parsley green, and lilies deathly white.</l>
<l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="17">Every melting eye will rest</l>

lines.text: On Damalis' lovely face; but none may part
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="18">On Damalis' lovely face; but none may part</l>
<l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="19">Damalis from our new-found guest;</l>

lines.text: She clings, and clings, like ivy, round his heart.
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="20">She clings, and clings, like ivy, round his heart.</l>

edition: John Conington; George Bell and Sons, London 1882

lines.text: Now drink we deep, now featly tread
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="1">Now drink we deep, now featly tread</l>

lines.text: A measure; now before each shrine
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="2">A measure; now before each shrine</l>

lines.text: With Salian feasts the table spread;
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="3">With Salian feasts the table spread;</l>

lines.text: The time invites us, comrades mine.
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="4">The time invites us, comrades mine.</l>
<l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="5">'Twas shame to broach, before today,</l>
<l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="6">The Caecuban, while <placeName key="tgn,7016833">Egypt</placeName>'s dame</l>

lines.text: Threaten'd our power in dust to lay
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="7">Threaten'd our power in dust to lay</l>

lines.text: And wrap the Capitol in flame,
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="8">And wrap the Capitol in flame,</l>

lines.text: Girt with her foul emasculate throng,
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="9">Girt with her foul emasculate throng,</l>

lines.text: By Fortune's sweet new wine befool'd,
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="10">By Fortune's sweet new wine befool'd,</l>
<l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="11">In hope's ungovern'd weakness strong</l>

lines.text: To hope for all; but soon she cool'd,
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="12">To hope for all; but soon she cool'd,</l>

lines.text: To see one ship from burning 'scape;
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="13">To see one ship from burning 'scape;</l>

lines.text: Great Caesar taught her dizzy brain,
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="14">Great Caesar taught her dizzy brain,</l>
<l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="15">Made mad by Mareotic grape,</l>

lines.text: To feel the sobering truth of pain,
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="16">To feel the sobering truth of pain,</l>

lines.text: And gave her chase from Italy,
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="17">And gave her chase from <placeName key="tgn,1000080">Italy</placeName>,</l>

lines.text: As after doves fierce falcons speed,
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="18">As after doves fierce falcons speed,</l>
<l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="19">As hunters 'neath Haemonia's sky</l>

lines.text: Chase the tired hare, so might he lead
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="20">Chase the tired hare, so might he lead</l>

lines.text: The fiend enchain'd; she sought to die
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="21">The fiend enchain'd; she sought to die</l>

lines.text: More nobly, nor with woman's dread
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="22">More nobly, nor with woman's dread</l>

lines.text: Quail'd at the steel, nor timorously
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="23">Quail'd at the steel, nor timorously</l>

lines.text: In her fleet ships to covert fled.
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="24">In her fleet ships to covert fled.</l>

lines.text: Amid her ruin'd halls she stood
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="25">Amid her ruin'd halls she stood</l>

lines.text: Unblench'd, and fearless to the end
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="26">Unblench'd, and fearless to the end</l>

lines.text: Grasp'd the fell snakes, that all her blood
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="27">Grasp'd the fell snakes, that all her blood</l>

lines.text: Might with the cold black venom blend,
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="28">Might with the cold black venom blend,</l>

lines.text: Death's purpose flushing in her face;
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="29">Death's purpose flushing in her face;</l>

lines.text: Nor to our ships the glory gave,
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="30">Nor to our ships the glory gave,</l>

lines.text: That she, no vulgar dame, should grace
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="31">That she, no vulgar dame, should grace</l>

lines.text: A triumph, crownless, and a slave.
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="32">A triumph, crownless, and a slave.</l>

edition: John Conington; George Bell and Sons, London 1882

lines.text: No Persian cumber, boy, for me;
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="1">No Persian cumber, boy, for me;</l>
<l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="2">I hate your garlands linden-plaited;</l>

lines.text: Leave winter's rose where on the tree
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="3">Leave winter's rose where on the tree</l>
<l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="4">It hangs belated.</l>

lines.text: Wreath me plain myrtle; never think
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="5">Wreath me plain myrtle; never think</l>
<l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="6">Plain myrtle either's wear unfitting,</l>

lines.text: Yours as you wait, mine as I drink
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="7">Yours as you wait, mine as I drink</l>
<l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="8">In vine-bower sitting.</l>

edition: John Conington; George Bell and Sons, London 1882

lines.text: The broils that from Metellus date,
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="1">The broils that from Metellus date,</l>

lines.text: The secret springs, the dark intrigues,
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="2">The secret springs, the dark intrigues,</l>

lines.text: The freaks of Fortune, and the great
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="3">The freaks of Fortune, and the great</l>
<l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="4">Confederate in disastrous leagues,</l>

lines.text: And arms with uncleansed slaughter red,
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="5">And arms with uncleansed slaughter red,</l>

lines.text: A work of danger and distrust,
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="6">A work of danger and distrust,</l>

lines.text: You treat, as one on fire should tread
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="7">You treat, as one on fire should tread</l>

lines.text: Scarce hid by treacherous ashen crust.
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="8">Scarce hid by treacherous ashen crust.</l>

lines.text: Let Tragedy's stern muse be mute
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="9">Let Tragedy's stern muse be mute</l>

lines.text: Awhile; and when your order'd page
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="10">Awhile; and when your order'd page</l>

lines.text: Has told Rome's tale, that buskin'd foot
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="11">Has told <placeName key="perseus,Rome">Rome</placeName>'s tale, that buskin'd foot</l>

lines.text: Again shall mount the Attic stage,
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="12">Again shall mount the Attic stage,</l>
<l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="13">Pollio, the pale defendant's shield,</l>

lines.text: In deep debate the senate's stay,
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="14">In deep debate the senate's stay,</l>
<l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="15">The hero of Dalmatic field</l>

lines.text: By Triumph crown'd with deathless bay.
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="16">By Triumph crown'd with deathless bay.</l>

lines.text: E'en now with trumpet's threatening blare
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="17">E'en now with trumpet's threatening blare</l>

lines.text: You thrill our ears; the clarion brays;
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="18">You thrill our ears; the clarion brays;</l>

lines.text: The lightnings of the armour scare
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="19">The lightnings of the armour scare</l>

lines.text: The steed, and daunt the rider's gaze.
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="20">The steed, and daunt the rider's gaze.</l>

lines.text: Methinks I hear of leaders proud
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="21">Methinks I hear of leaders proud</l>
<l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="22">With no uncomely dust distain'd,</l>

lines.text: And all the world by conquest bow'd,
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="23">And all the world by conquest bow'd,</l>
<l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="24">And only Cato's soul unchain'd.</l>

lines.text: Yes, Juno and the powers on high
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="25">Yes, Juno and the powers on high</l>

lines.text: That left their Afric to its doom,
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="26">That left their Afric to its doom,</l>
<l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="27">Have led the victors' progeny</l>
<l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="28">As victims to Jugurtha's tomb.</l>

lines.text: What field, by Latian blood-drops fed,
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="29">What field, by Latian blood-drops fed,</l>
<l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="30">Proclaims not the unnatural deeds</l>

lines.text: It buries, and the earthquake dread
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="31">It buries, and the earthquake dread</l>

lines.text: Whose distant thunder shook the Medes?
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="32">Whose distant thunder shook the Medes?</l>

lines.text: What gulf, what river has not seen
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="33">What gulf, what river has not seen</l>

lines.text: Those sights of sorrow? nay, what sea
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="34">Those sights of sorrow? nay, what sea</l>

lines.text: Has Daunian carnage yet left green?
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="35">Has Daunian carnage yet left green?</l>

lines.text: What coast from Roman blood is free?
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="36">What coast from Roman blood is free?</l>

lines.text: But pause, gay Muse, nor leave your play
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="37">But pause, gay Muse, nor leave your play</l>
<l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="38">Another Cean dirge to sing;</l>

lines.text: With me to Venus' bower away,
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="39">With me to Venus' bower away,</l>

lines.text: And there attune a lighter string.
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="40">And there attune a lighter string.</l>

edition: John Conington; George Bell and Sons, London 1882

lines.text: The silver, Sallust, shows not fair
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="1">The silver, Sallust, shows not fair</l>

lines.text: While buried in the greedy mine:
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="2">While buried in the greedy mine:</l>

lines.text: You love it not till moderate wear
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="3">You love it not till moderate wear</l>
<l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="4">Have given it shine.</l>
<l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="5">Honour to Proculeius!  he</l>

lines.text: To brethren play'd a father's part;
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="6">To brethren play'd a father's part;</l>

lines.text: Fame shall embalm through years to be
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="7">Fame shall embalm through years to be</l>
<l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="8">That noble heart.</l>

lines.text: Who curbs a greedy soul may boast
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="9">Who curbs a greedy soul may boast</l>

lines.text: More power than if his broad-based throne
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="10">More power than if his broad-based throne</l>

lines.text: Bridged Libya's sea, and either coast
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="11">Bridged <placeName key="tgn,1000172">Libya</placeName>'s sea, and either coast</l>
<l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="12">Were all his own.</l>
<l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="13">Indulgence bids the dropsy grow;</l>

lines.text: Who fain would quench the palate's flame
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="14">Who fain would quench the palate's flame</l>

lines.text: Must rescue from the watery foe
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="15">Must rescue from the watery foe</l>
<l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="16">The pale weak frame.</l>
<l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="17">Phraates, throned where Cyrus sate,</l>

lines.text: May count for blest with vulgar herds,
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="18">May count for blest with vulgar herds,</l>

lines.text: But not with Virtue; soon or late
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="19">But not with Virtue; soon or late</l>
<l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="20">From lying words</l>

lines.text: She weans men's lips; for him she keeps
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="21">She weans men's lips; for him she keeps</l>

lines.text: The crown, the purple, and the bays,
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="22">The crown, the purple, and the bays,</l>

lines.text: Who dares to look on treasure-heaps
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="23">Who dares to look on treasure-heaps</l>
<l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="24">With unblench'd gaze.</l>

edition: John Conington; George Bell and Sons, London 1882

lines.text: An equal mind, when storms o'ercloud,
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="1">An equal mind, when storms o'ercloud,</l>
<l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="2">Maintain, nor 'neath a brighter sky</l>

lines.text: Let pleasure make your heart too proud,
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="3">Let pleasure make your heart too proud,</l>

lines.text: O Dellius, Dellius! sure te die,
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="4">O Dellius, Dellius! sure te die,</l>

lines.text: Whether in gloom you spend each year,
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="5">Whether in gloom you spend each year,</l>

lines.text: Or through long holydays at ease
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="6">Or through long holydays at ease</l>

lines.text: In grassy nook your spirit cheer
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="7">In grassy nook your spirit cheer</l>
<l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="8">With old Falernian vintages,</l>

lines.text: Where poplar pale, and pine-tree high
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="9">Where poplar pale, and pine-tree high</l>
<l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="10">Their hospitable shadows spread</l>
<l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="11">Entwined, and panting waters try</l>

lines.text: To hurry down their zigzag bed.
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="12">To hurry down their zigzag bed.</l>

lines.text: Bring wine and scents, and roses' bloom,
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="13">Bring wine and scents, and roses' bloom,</l>

lines.text: Too brief, alas! to that sweet place;
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="14">Too brief, alas! to that sweet place;</l>

lines.text: While life, and fortune, and the loom
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="15">While life, and fortune, and the loom</l>

lines.text: Of the Three Sisters yield you grace.
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="16">Of the Three Sisters yield you grace.</l>

lines.text: Soon must you leave the woods you buy,
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="17">Soon must you leave the woods you buy,</l>

lines.text: Your villa, wash'd by Tiber's flow,
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="18">Your villa, wash'd by <placeName key="tgn,1130786">Tiber</placeName>'s flow,</l>

lines.text: Leave,—and your treasures, heap'd so high,
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="19">Leave,—and your treasures, heap'd so high,</l>

lines.text: Your reckless heir will level low.
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="20">Your reckless heir will level low.</l>
<l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="21">Whether from <placeName key="perseus,Argos">Argos</placeName>' founder born</l>

lines.text: In wealth you lived beneath the sun,
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="22">In wealth you lived beneath the sun,</l>

lines.text: Or nursed in beggary and scorn,
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="23">Or nursed in beggary and scorn,</l>

lines.text: You fall to Death, who pities none.
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="24">You fall to Death, who pities none.</l>

lines.text: One way all travel; the dark urn
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="25">One way all travel; the dark urn</l>

lines.text: Shakes each man's lot, that soon or late
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="26">Shakes each man's lot, that soon or late</l>

lines.text: Will force him, hopeless of return,
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="27">Will force him, hopeless of return,</l>

lines.text: On board the exile-ship of Fate.
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="28">On board the exile-ship of Fate.</l>

edition: John Conington; George Bell and Sons, London 1882

lines.text: Why, Xanthias, blush to own you love
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="1">Why, Xanthias, blush to own you love</l>
<l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="2">Your slave? Briseis, long ago,</l>
<l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="3">A captive, could Achilles move</l>
<l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="4">With breast of snow.</l>
<l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="5">Tecmessa's charms enslaved her lord,</l>
<l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="6">Stout Ajax, heir of Telamon;</l>
<l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="7">Atrides, in his pride, adored</l>
<l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="8">The maid he won,</l>

lines.text: When Troy to Thessaly gave way,
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="9">When <placeName key="perseus,Troy">Troy</placeName> to <placeName key="tgn,7001399">Thessaly</placeName> gave way,</l>

lines.text: And Hector's all too quick decease
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="10">And Hector's all too quick decease</l>
<l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="11">Made <placeName key="tgn,7016140">Pergamus</placeName> an easier prey</l>
<l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="12">To wearied <placeName key="tgn,1000074">Greece</placeName>.</l>

lines.text: What if, as auburn Phyllis' mate,
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="13">What if, as auburn Phyllis' mate,</l>

lines.text: You graft yourself on regal stem?
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="14">You graft yourself on regal stem?</l>

lines.text: Oh yes! be sure her sires were great;
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="15">Oh yes! be sure her sires were great;</l>
<l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="16">She weeps for them.</l>

lines.text: Believe me, from no rascal scum
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="17">Believe me, from no rascal scum</l>

lines.text: Your charmer sprang; so true a flame,
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="18">Your charmer sprang; so true a flame,</l>

lines.text: Such hate of greed, could never come
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="19">Such hate of greed, could never come</l>
<l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="20">From vulgar dame.</l>
<l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="21">With honest fervour I commend</l>

lines.text: Those lips, those eyes; you need not fear
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="22">Those lips, those eyes; you need not fear</l>

lines.text: A rival, hurrying on to end
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="23">A rival, hurrying on to end</l>
<l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="24">His fortieth year.</l>

edition: John Conington; George Bell and Sons, London 1882

lines.text: Septimius, who with me would brave
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="1">Septimius, who with me would brave</l>
<l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="2">Far <placeName key="tgn,7007512">Gades</placeName>, and Cantabrian land</l>

lines.text: Untamed by Rome, and Moorish wave
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="3">Untamed by <placeName key="perseus,Rome">Rome</placeName>, and Moorish wave</l>
<l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="4">That whirls the sand;</l>

lines.text: Fair Tibur, town of Argive kings,
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="5">Fair <placeName key="perseus,Tibur">Tibur</placeName>, town of <placeName key="tgn,5001993">Argive</placeName> kings,</l>

lines.text: There would I end my days serene,
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="6">There would I end my days serene,</l>

lines.text: At rest from seas and travellings,
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="7">At rest from seas and travellings,</l>
<l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="8">And service seen.</l>

lines.text: Should angry Fate those wishes foil,
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="9">Should angry Fate those wishes foil,</l>

lines.text: Then let me seek Galesus, sweet
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="10">Then let me seek Galesus, sweet</l>

lines.text: To skin-clad sheep, and that rich soil,
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="11">To skin-clad sheep, and that rich soil,</l>
<l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="12">The Spartan's seat.</l>

lines.text: O, what can match the green recess,
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="13">O, what can match the green recess,</l>

lines.text: Whose honey not to Hybla yields,
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="14">Whose honey not to Hybla yields,</l>

lines.text: Whose olives vie with those that bless
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="15">Whose olives vie with those that bless</l>

<l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="16">
                        <placeName key="perseus,Venafrum">Venafrum</placeName>'s fields?</l>

lines.text: Long springs, mild winters glad that spot
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="17">Long springs, mild winters glad that spot</l>

lines.text: By Jove's good grace, and Aulon, dear
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="18">By Jove's good grace, and <placeName key="tgn,7010744">Aulon</placeName>, dear</l>
<l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="19">To fruitful Bacchus, envies not</l>
<l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="20">Falernian cheer.</l>

lines.text: That spot, those happy heights desire
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="21">That spot, those happy heights desire</l>

lines.text: Our sojourn; there, when life shall end,
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="22">Our sojourn; there, when life shall end,</l>

lines.text: Your tear shall dew my yet warm pyre,
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="23">Your tear shall dew my yet warm pyre,</l>
<l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="24">Your bard and friend.</l>

edition: John Conington; George Bell and Sons, London 1882

lines.text: O, oft with me in troublous time
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="1">O, oft with me in troublous time</l>

lines.text: Involved, when Brutus warr'd in Greece,
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="2">Involved, when Brutus warr'd in <placeName key="tgn,1000074">Greece</placeName>,</l>

lines.text: Who gives you back to your own clime
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="3">Who gives you back to your own clime</l>

lines.text: And your own gods, a man of peace,
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="4">And your own gods, a man of peace,</l>

lines.text: Pompey, the earliest friend I knew,
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="5">Pompey, the earliest friend I knew,</l>

lines.text: With whom I oft cut short the hours
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="6">With whom I oft cut short the hours</l>

lines.text: With wine, my hair bright bathed in dew
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="7">With wine, my hair bright bathed in dew</l>

lines.text: Of Syrian oils, and wreathed with flowers?
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="8">Of Syrian oils, and wreathed with flowers?</l>

lines.text: With you I shared Philippi's rout,
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="9">With you I shared <placeName key="perseus,Philippi">Philippi</placeName>'s rout,</l>
<l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="10">Unseemly parted from my shield,</l>

lines.text: When Valour fell, and warriors stout
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="11">When Valour fell, and warriors stout</l>

lines.text: Were tumbled on the inglorious field:
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="12">Were tumbled on the inglorious field:</l>

lines.text: But I was saved by Mercury,
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="13">But I was saved by Mercury,</l>

lines.text: Wrapp'd in thick mist, yet trembling sore,
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="14">Wrapp'd in thick mist, yet trembling sore,</l>

lines.text: While you to that tempestuous sea
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="15">While you to that tempestuous sea</l>

lines.text: Were swept by battle's tide once more.
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="16">Were swept by battle's tide once more.</l>

lines.text: Come, pay to Jove the feast you owe;
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="17">Come, pay to Jove the feast you owe;</l>

lines.text: Lay down those limbs, with warfare spent,
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="18">Lay down those limbs, with warfare spent,</l>

lines.text: Beneath my laurel; nor be slow
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="19">Beneath my laurel; nor be slow</l>

lines.text: To drain my cask; for you 'twas meant.
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="20">To drain my cask; for you 'twas meant.</l>

lines.text: Lethe's true draught is Massic wine;
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="21">Lethe's true draught is Massic wine;</l>

lines.text: Fill high the goblet; pour out free
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="22">Fill high the goblet; pour out free</l>
