lines.text: Rich streams of unguent. Who will twine
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="23">Rich streams of unguent.  Who will twine</l>
<l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="24">The hasty wreath from myrtle-tree</l>

lines.text: Or parsley? Whom will Venus seat
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="25">Or parsley?  Whom will Venus seat</l>

lines.text: Chairman of cups? Are Bacchants sane?
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="26">Chairman of cups? Are Bacchants sane?</l>

lines.text: Then I'll be sober. O, 'tis sweet
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="27">Then I'll be sober.  O, 'tis sweet</l>

lines.text: To fool, when friends come home again!
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="28">To fool, when friends come home again!</l>

edition: John Conington; George Bell and Sons, London 1882

lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="1">Had chastisement for perjured truth,</l>

lines.text: Barine, mark'd you with a curse—
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="2">Barine, mark'd you with a curse—</l>

lines.text: Did one wry nail, or one black tooth,
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="3">Did one wry nail, or one black tooth,</l>
<l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="4">But make you worse—</l>

lines.text: I'd trust you; but, when plighted lies
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="5">I'd trust you; but, when plighted lies</l>

lines.text: Have pledged you deepest, lovelier far
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="6">Have pledged you deepest, lovelier far</l>

lines.text: You sparkle forth, of all young eyes
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="7">You sparkle forth, of all young eyes</l>
<l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="8">The ruling star.</l>

lines.text: 'Tis gain to mock your mother's bones,
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="9">'Tis gain to mock your mother's bones,</l>

lines.text: And night's still signs, and all the sky,
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="10">And night's still signs, and all the sky,</l>

lines.text: And gods, that on their glorious thrones
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="11">And gods, that on their glorious thrones</l>
<l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="12">Chill Death defy.</l>

lines.text: Ay, Venus smiles; the pure nymphs smile,
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="13">Ay, Venus smiles; the pure nymphs smile,</l>
<l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="14">And Cupid, tyrant-lord of hearts,</l>

lines.text: Sharpening on bloody stone the while
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="15">Sharpening on bloody stone the while</l>
<l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="16">His fiery darts.</l>

lines.text: New captives fill the nets you weave;
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="17">New captives fill the nets you weave;</l>

lines.text: New slaves are bred; and those before,
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="18">New slaves are bred; and those before,</l>

lines.text: Though oft they threaten, never leave
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="19">Though oft they threaten, never leave</l>
<l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="20">Your godless door.</l>

lines.text: The mother dreads you for her son,
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="21">The mother dreads you for her son,</l>

lines.text: The thrifty sire, the new-wed bride,
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="22">The thrifty sire, the new-wed bride,</l>

lines.text: Lest, lured by you, her precious one
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="23">Lest, lured by you, her precious one</l>
<l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="24">Should leave her side.</l>

edition: John Conington; George Bell and Sons, London 1882

lines.text: The rain, it rains not every day
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="1">The rain, it rains not every day</l>

lines.text: On the soak'd meads; the Caspian main
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="2">On the soak'd meads; the Caspian main</l>

lines.text: Not always feels the unequal sway
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="3">Not always feels the unequal sway</l>

lines.text: Of storms, nor on Armenia's plain,
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="4">Of storms, nor on <placeName key="tgn,7006651">Armenia</placeName>'s plain,</l>

lines.text: Dear Valgius, lies the cold dull snow
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="5">Dear Valgius, lies the cold dull snow</l>

lines.text: Through all the year; nor northwinds keen
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="6">Through all the year; nor northwinds keen</l>
<l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="7">Upon Garganian oakwoods blow,</l>

lines.text: And strip the ashes of their green.
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="8">And strip the ashes of their green.</l>

lines.text: You still with tearful tones pursue
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="9">You still with tearful tones pursue</l>

lines.text: Your lost, lost Mystes; Hesper sees
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="10">Your lost, lost Mystes; Hesper sees</l>

lines.text: Your passion when he brings the dew,
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="11">Your passion when he brings the dew,</l>

lines.text: And when before the sun he flees.
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="12">And when before the sun he flees.</l>
<l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="13">Yet not for loved Antilochus</l>

lines.text: Grey Nestor wasted all his years
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="14">Grey Nestor wasted all his years</l>

lines.text: In grief; nor o'er young Troilus
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="15">In grief; nor o'er young Troilus</l>

lines.text: His parents' and his sisters' tears
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="16">His parents' and his sisters' tears</l>

lines.text: For ever flow'd. At length have done
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="17">For ever flow'd.  At length have done</l>

lines.text: With these soft sorrows; rather tell
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="18">With these soft sorrows; rather tell</l>
<l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="19">Of Caesar's trophies newly won,</l>
<l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="20">And hoar Niphates' icy fell,</l>
<l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="21">And Medus' flood, 'mid conquer'd tribes</l>
<l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="22">Rolling a less presumptuous tide,</l>

lines.text: And Scythians taught, as Rome prescribes,
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="23">And Scythians taught, as <placeName key="perseus,Rome">Rome</placeName> prescribes,</l>

lines.text: Henceforth o'er narrower steppes to ride.
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="24">Henceforth o'er narrower steppes to ride.</l>

edition: John Conington; George Bell and Sons, London 1882

lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="1">Licinius, trust a seaman's lore:</l>

lines.text: Steer not too boldly to the deep,
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="2">Steer not too boldly to the deep,</l>

lines.text: Nor, fearing storms, by treacherous shore
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="3">Nor, fearing storms, by treacherous shore</l>
<l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="4">Too closely creep.</l>

lines.text: Who makes the golden mean his guide,
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="5">Who makes the golden mean his guide,</l>

lines.text: Shuns miser's cabin, foul and dark,
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="6">Shuns miser's cabin, foul and dark,</l>

lines.text: Shuns gilded roofs, where pomp and pride
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="7">Shuns gilded roofs, where pomp and pride</l>
<l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="8">Are envy's mark.</l>

lines.text: With fiercer blasts the pine's dim height
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="9">With fiercer blasts the pine's dim height</l>

lines.text: Is rock'd; proud towers with heavier fall
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="10">Is rock'd; proud towers with heavier fall</l>

lines.text: Crash to the ground; and thunders smite
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="11">Crash to the ground; and thunders smite</l>
<l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="12">The mountains tall.</l>

lines.text: In sadness hope, in gladness fear
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="13">In sadness hope, in gladness fear</l>
<l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="14">'Gainst coming change will fortify</l>

lines.text: Your breast. The storms that Jupiter
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="15">Your breast. The storms that Jupiter</l>
<l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="16">Sweeps o'er the sky</l>

lines.text: He chases. Why should rain today
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="17">He chases.  Why should rain today</l>
<l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="18">Bring rain tomorrow? Python's foe</l>

lines.text: Is pleased sometimes his lyre to play,
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="19">Is pleased sometimes his lyre to play,</l>
<l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="20">Nor bends his bow.</l>

lines.text: Be brave in trouble; meet distress
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="21">Be brave in trouble; meet distress</l>

lines.text: With dauntless front; but when the gale
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="22">With dauntless front; but when the gale</l>

lines.text: Too prosperous blows, be wise no less,
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="23">Too prosperous blows, be wise no less,</l>
<l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="24">And shorten sail.</l>

edition: John Conington; George Bell and Sons, London 1882

lines.text: O ask not what those sons of war,
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="1">O ask not what those sons of war,</l>
<l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="2">Cantabrian, Scythian, each intend,</l>

lines.text: Disjoin'd from us by Hadria's bar,
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="3">Disjoin'd from us by <placeName key="perseus,Hadria">Hadria</placeName>'s bar,</l>

lines.text: Nor puzzle, Quintius, how to spend
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="4">Nor puzzle, Quintius, how to spend</l>

lines.text: A life so simple. Youth removes,
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="5">A life so simple.  Youth removes,</l>

lines.text: And Beauty too; and hoar Decay
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="6">And Beauty too; and hoar Decay</l>

lines.text: Drives out the wanton tribe of Loves
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="7">Drives out the wanton tribe of Loves</l>

lines.text: And Sleep, that came or night or day.
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="8">And Sleep, that came or night or day.</l>

lines.text: The sweet spring-flowers not always keep
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="9">The sweet spring-flowers not always keep</l>

lines.text: Their bloom, nor moonlight shines the same
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="10">Their bloom, nor moonlight shines the same</l>

lines.text: Each evening. Why with thoughts too deep
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="11">Each evening. Why with thoughts too deep</l>

lines.text: O'ertask a mind of mortal frame?
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="12">O'ertask a mind of mortal frame?</l>

lines.text: Why not, just thrown at careless ease
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="13">Why not, just thrown at careless ease</l>

lines.text: 'Neath plane or pine, our locks of grey
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="14">'Neath plane or pine, our locks of grey</l>
<l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="15">Perfumed with Syrian essences</l>

lines.text: And wreathed with roses, while we may,
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="16">And wreathed with roses, while we may,</l>

lines.text: Lie drinking? Bacchus puts to shame
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="17">Lie drinking? Bacchus puts to shame</l>

lines.text: The cares that waste us. Where's the slave
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="18">The cares that waste us.  Where's the slave</l>

lines.text: To quench the fierce Falernian's flame
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="19">To quench the fierce Falernian's flame</l>

lines.text: With water from the passing wave?
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="20">With water from the passing wave?</l>

lines.text: Who'll coax coy Lyde from her home?
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="21">Who'll coax coy Lyde from her home?</l>

lines.text: Go, bid her take her ivory lyre,
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="22">Go, bid her take her ivory lyre,</l>

lines.text: The runaway, and haste to come,
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="23">The runaway, and haste to come,</l>

lines.text: Her wild hair bound with Spartan tire.
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="24">Her wild hair bound with Spartan tire.</l>

edition: John Conington; George Bell and Sons, London 1882

lines.text: The weary war where fierce Numantia bled,
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="1">The weary war where fierce <placeName key="tgn,7017511">Numantia</placeName> bled,</l>

lines.text: Fell Hannibal, the swoln Sicilian main
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="2">Fell Hannibal, the swoln Sicilian main</l>

lines.text: Purpled with Punic blood—not mine to wed
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="3">Purpled with Punic blood—not mine to wed</l>

lines.text: These to the lyre's soft strain,
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="4">These to the lyre's soft strain,</l>

lines.text: Nor cruel Lapithae, nor, mad with wine,
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="5">Nor cruel Lapithae, nor, mad with wine,</l>

lines.text: Centaurs, nor, by Herculean arm o'ercome,
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="6">Centaurs, nor, by Herculean arm o'ercome,</l>

lines.text: The earth-born youth, whose terrors dimm'd the shine
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="7">The earth-born youth, whose terrors dimm'd the shine</l>
<l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="8">Of the resplendent dome</l>

lines.text: Of ancient Saturn. You, Maecenas, best
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="9">Of ancient Saturn.  You, Maecenas, best</l>

lines.text: In pictured prose of Caesar's warrior feats
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="10">In pictured prose of Caesar's warrior feats</l>

lines.text: Will tell, and captive kings with haughty crest
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="11">Will tell, and captive kings with haughty crest</l>
<l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="12">Led through the Roman streets.</l>

lines.text: On me the Muse has laid her charge to tell
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="13">On me the Muse has laid her charge to tell</l>

lines.text: Of your Licymnia's voice, the lustrous hue
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="14">Of your Licymnia's voice, the lustrous hue</l>

lines.text: Of her bright eye, her heart that beats so well
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="15">Of her bright eye, her heart that beats so well</l>
<l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="16">To mutual passion true:</l>

lines.text: How nought she does but lends her added grace,
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="17">How nought she does but lends her added grace,</l>

lines.text: Whether she dance, or join in bantering play,
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="18">Whether she dance, or join in bantering play,</l>

lines.text: Or with soft arms the maiden choir embrace
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="19">Or with soft arms the maiden choir embrace</l>
<l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="20">On great Diana's day.</l>

lines.text: Say, would you change for all the wealth possest
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="21">Say, would you change for all the wealth possest</l>

lines.text: By rich Achaemenes or Phrygia's heir,
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="22">By rich Achaemenes or <placeName key="tgn,7002613">Phrygia</placeName>'s heir,</l>

lines.text: Or the full stores of Araby the blest,
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="23">Or the full stores of Araby the blest,</l>

lines.text: One lock of her dear hair,
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="24">One lock of her dear hair,</l>

lines.text: While to your burning lips she bends her neck,
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="25">While to your burning lips she bends her neck,</l>

lines.text: Or with kind cruelty denies the due
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="26">Or with kind cruelty denies the due</l>

lines.text: She means you not to beg for, but to take,
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="27">She means you not to beg for, but to take,</l>
<l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="28">Or snatches it from you?</l>

edition: John Conington; George Bell and Sons, London 1882

lines.text: Black day he chose for planting thee,
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="1">Black day he chose for planting thee,</l>

lines.text: Accurst he rear'd thee from the ground,
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="2">Accurst he rear'd thee from the ground,</l>

lines.text: The bane of children yet to be,
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="3">The bane of children yet to be,</l>

lines.text: The scandal of the village round.
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="4">The scandal of the village round.</l>

lines.text: His father's throat the monster press'd
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="5">His father's throat the monster press'd</l>

lines.text: Beside, and on his hearthstone spilt,
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="6">Beside, and on his hearthstone spilt,</l>

lines.text: I ween, the blood of midnight guest;
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="7">I ween, the blood of midnight guest;</l>

lines.text: Black Colchian drugs, whate'er of guilt
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="8">Black Colchian drugs, whate'er of guilt</l>

lines.text: Is hatch'd on earth, he dealt in all—
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="9">Is hatch'd on earth, he dealt in all—</l>

lines.text: Who planted in my rural stead
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="10">Who planted in my rural stead</l>

lines.text: Thee, fatal wood, thee, sure to fall
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="11">Thee, fatal wood, thee, sure to fall</l>
<l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="12">Upon thy blameless master's head.</l>

lines.text: The dangers of the hour! no thought
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="13">The dangers of the hour! no thought</l>

lines.text: We give them; Punic seaman's fear
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="14">We give them; Punic seaman's fear</l>

lines.text: Is all of Bosporus, nor aught
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="15">Is all of <placeName key="tgn,1115068">Bosporus</placeName>, nor aught</l>
<l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="16">Reeks he of pitfalls otherwhere;</l>

lines.text: The soldier fears the mask'd retreat
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="17">The soldier fears the mask'd retreat</l>

lines.text: Of Parthia; Parthia dreads the thrall
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="18">Of <placeName key="tgn,7016768">Parthia</placeName>; <placeName key="tgn,7016768">Parthia</placeName> dreads the thrall</l>

lines.text: Of Rome; but Death with noiseless feet
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="19">Of <placeName key="perseus,Rome">Rome</placeName>; but Death with noiseless feet</l>

lines.text: Has stolen and will steal on all.
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="20">Has stolen and will steal on all.</l>

lines.text: How near dark Pluto's court I stood,
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="21">How near dark Pluto's court I stood,</l>
<l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="22">And Aeacus' judicial throne,</l>

lines.text: The blest seclusion of the good,
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="23">The blest seclusion of the good,</l>

lines.text: And Sappho, with sweet lyric moan
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="24">And Sappho, with sweet lyric moan</l>
<l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="25">Bewailing her ungentle sex,</l>
<l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="26">And thee, Alcaeus, louder far</l>

lines.text: Chanting thy tale of woful wrecks,
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="27">Chanting thy tale of woful wrecks,</l>
<l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="28">Of woful exile, woful war!</l>

lines.text: In sacred awe the silent dead
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="29">In sacred awe the silent dead</l>

lines.text: Attend on each: but when the song
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="30">Attend on each: but when the song</l>

lines.text: Of combat tells and tyrants fled,
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="31">Of combat tells and tyrants fled,</l>

lines.text: Keen ears, press'd shoulders, closer throng.
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="32">Keen ears, press'd shoulders, closer throng.</l>

lines.text: What marvel, when at those sweet airs
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="33">What marvel, when at those sweet airs</l>
<l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="34">The hundred-headed beast spell-bound</l>

lines.text: Each black ear droops, and Furies' hairs
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="35">Each black ear droops, and Furies' hairs</l>

lines.text: Uncoil their serpents at the sound?
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="36">Uncoil their serpents at the sound?</l>
<l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="37">Prometheus too and Pelops' sire</l>

lines.text: In listening lose the sense of woe;
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="38">In listening lose the sense of woe;</l>
<l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="39">Orion hearkens to the lyre,</l>

lines.text: And lets the lynx and lion go.
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="40">And lets the lynx and lion go.</l>

edition: John Conington; George Bell and Sons, London 1882

lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="1">Ah, Postumus! they fleet away,</l>

lines.text: Our years, nor piety one hour
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="2">Our years, nor piety one hour</l>

lines.text: Can win from wrinkles and decay,
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="3">Can win from wrinkles and decay,</l>
<l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="4">And Death's indomitable power;</l>

lines.text: Not though three hundred bullocks flame
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="5">Not though three hundred bullocks flame</l>

lines.text: Each year, to soothe the tearless king
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="6">Each year, to soothe the tearless king</l>

lines.text: Who holds huge Geryon's triple frame
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="7">Who holds huge Geryon's triple frame</l>

lines.text: And Tityos in his watery ring,
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="8">And Tityos in his watery ring,</l>

lines.text: That circling flood, which all must stem,
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="9">That circling flood, which all must stem,</l>

lines.text: Who eat the fruits that Nature yields,
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="10">Who eat the fruits that Nature yields,</l>
<l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="11">Wearers of haughtiest diadem,</l>

lines.text: Or humblest tillers of the fields.
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="12">Or humblest tillers of the fields.</l>

lines.text: In vain we shun war's contact red
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="13">In vain we shun war's contact red</l>

lines.text: Or storm-tost spray of Hadrian main:
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="14">Or storm-tost spray of Hadrian main:</l>

lines.text: In vain, the season through, we dread
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="15">In vain, the season through, we dread</l>

lines.text: For our frail lives Scirocco's bane.
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="16">For our frail lives Scirocco's bane.</l>
<l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="17">Cocytus' black and stagnant ooze</l>

lines.text: Must welcome you, and Danaus' seed
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="18">Must welcome you, and Danaus' seed</l>
<l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="19">Ill-famed, and ancient Sisyphus</l>
<l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="20">To never-ending toil decreed.</l>

lines.text: Your land, your house, your lovely bride
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="21">Your land, your house, your lovely bride</l>

lines.text: Must lose you; of your cherish'd trees
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="22">Must lose you; of your cherish'd trees</l>

lines.text: None to its fleeting master's side
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="23">None to its fleeting master's side</l>

lines.text: Will cleave, but those sad cypresses.
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="24">Will cleave, but those sad cypresses.</l>

lines.text: Your heir, a larger soul, will drain
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="25">Your heir, a larger soul, will drain</l>
<l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="26">The hundred-padlock'd Caecuban,</l>

lines.text: And richer spilth the pavement stain
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="27">And richer spilth the pavement stain</l>

lines.text: Than e'er at pontiff's supper ran.
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="28">Than e'er at pontiff's supper ran.</l>

edition: John Conington; George Bell and Sons, London 1882

lines.text: Few roods of ground the piles we raise
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="1">Few roods of ground the piles we raise</l>

lines.text: Will leave to plough; ponds wider spread
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="2">Will leave to plough; ponds wider spread</l>

lines.text: Than Lucrine lake will meet the gaze
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="3">Than Lucrine lake will meet the gaze</l>

lines.text: On every side; the plane unwed
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="4">On every side; the plane unwed</l>

lines.text: Will top the elm; the violet-bed,
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="5">Will top the elm; the violet-bed,</l>
<l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="6">The myrtle, each delicious sweet,</l>

lines.text: On olive-grounds their scent will shed,
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="7">On olive-grounds their scent will shed,</l>

lines.text: Where once were fruit-trees yielding meat;
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="8">Where once were fruit-trees yielding meat;</l>

lines.text: Thick bays will screen the midday range
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="9">Thick bays will screen the midday range</l>

lines.text: Of fiercest suns. Not such the rule
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="10">Of fiercest suns.  Not such the rule</l>
<l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="11">Of Romulus, and Cato sage,</l>

lines.text: And all the bearded, good old school.
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="12">And all the bearded, good old school.</l>

lines.text: Each Roman's wealth was little worth,
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="13">Each Roman's wealth was little worth,</l>
<l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="14">His country's much; no colonnade</l>

lines.text: For private pleasance wooed the North
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="15">For private pleasance wooed the North</l>
<l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="16">With cool “prolixity of shade.”</l>

lines.text: None might the casual sod disdain
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="17">None might the casual sod disdain</l>

lines.text: To roof his home; a town alone,
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="18">To roof his home; a town alone,</l>

lines.text: At public charge, a sacred fane
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="19">At public charge, a sacred fane</l>

lines.text: Were honour'd with the pomp of stone.
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="20">Were honour'd with the pomp of stone.</l>

edition: John Conington; George Bell and Sons, London 1882

lines.text: For ease, in wide Aegean caught,
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="1">For ease, in wide <placeName key="tgn,7002675">Aegean</placeName> caught,</l>

lines.text: The sailor prays, when clouds are hiding
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="2">The sailor prays, when clouds are hiding</l>

lines.text: The moon, nor shines of starlight aught
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="3">The moon, nor shines of starlight aught</l>
<l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="4">For seaman's guiding:</l>

lines.text: For ease the Mede, with quiver gay:
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="5">For ease the <placeName key="tgn,1045322">Mede</placeName>, with quiver gay:</l>

lines.text: For ease rude Thrace, in battle cruel:
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="6">For ease rude <placeName key="tgn,7002756">Thrace</placeName>, in battle cruel:</l>

lines.text: Can purple buy it, Grosphus? Nay,
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="7">Can purple buy it, Grosphus? Nay,</l>
<l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="8">Nor gold, nor jewel.</l>

lines.text: No pomp, no lictor clears the way
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="9">No pomp, no lictor clears the way</l>
<l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="10">'Mid rabble-routs of troublous feelings,</l>

lines.text: Nor quells the cares that sport and play
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="11">Nor quells the cares that sport and play</l>
<l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="12">Round gilded ceilings.</l>

lines.text: More happy he whose modest board
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="13">More happy he whose modest board</l>
<l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="14">His father's well-worn silver brightens;</l>

lines.text: No fear, nor lust for sordid hoard,
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="15">No fear, nor lust for sordid hoard,</l>
<l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="16">His light sleep frightens.</l>

lines.text: Why bend our bows of little span?
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="17">Why bend our bows of little span?</l>

lines.text: Why change our homes for regions under
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="18">Why change our homes for regions under</l>
<l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="19">Another sun? What exiled man</l>
<l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="20">From self can sunder?</l>

lines.text: Care climbs the bark, and trims the sail,
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="21">Care climbs the bark, and trims the sail,</l>

lines.text: Curst fiend! nor troops of horse can 'scape her,
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="22">Curst fiend! nor troops of horse can 'scape her,</l>

lines.text: More swift than stag, more swift than gale
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="23">More swift than stag, more swift than gale</l>
<l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="24">That drives the vapour.</l>

lines.text: Blest in the present, look not forth
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="25">Blest in the present, look not forth</l>

lines.text: On ills beyond, but soothe each bitter
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="26">On ills beyond, but soothe each bitter</l>

lines.text: With slow, calm smile. No suns on earth
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="27">With slow, calm smile.  No suns on earth</l>
<l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="28">Unclouded glitter.</l>

lines.text: Achilles' light was quench'd at noon;
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="29">Achilles' light was quench'd at noon;</l>
<l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="30">A long decay Tithonus minish'd;</l>

lines.text: My hours, it may be, yet will run
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="31">My hours, it may be, yet will run</l>
<l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="32">When yours are flnish'd.</l>
<l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="33">For you Sicilian heifers low,</l>

lines.text: Bleat countless flocks; for you are neighing
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="34">Bleat countless flocks; for you are neighing</l>
<l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="35">Proud coursers; Afric purples glow</l>
<l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="36">For your arraying</l>

lines.text: With double dyes; a small domain,
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="37">With double dyes; a small domain,</l>

lines.text: The soul that breathed in Grecian harping,
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="38">The soul that breathed in Grecian harping,</l>

lines.text: My portion these; and high disdain
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="39">My portion these; and high disdain</l>
<l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="40">Of ribald carping.</l>

edition: John Conington; George Bell and Sons, London 1882

lines.text: Why rend my heart with that sad sigh?
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="1">Why rend my heart with that sad sigh?</l>

lines.text: It cannot please the gods or me
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="2">It cannot please the gods or me</l>

lines.text: That you, Maecenas, first should die,
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="3">That you, Maecenas, first should die,</l>
<l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="4">My pillar of prosperity.</l>

lines.text: Ah! should I lose one half my soul
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="5">Ah! should I lose one half my soul</l>
<l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="6">Untimely, can the other stay</l>

lines.text: Behind it? Life that is not whole,
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="7">Behind it?  Life that is not whole,</l>

lines.text: Is that as sweet? The self-same day
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="8">Is <emph>that</emph> as sweet?  The self-same day</l>

lines.text: Shall crush us twain; no idle oath
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="9">Shall crush us twain; no idle oath</l>

lines.text: Has Horace sworn; whene'er you go,
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="10">Has Horace sworn; whene'er you go,</l>

lines.text: We both will travel, travel both
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="11">We both will travel, travel both</l>

lines.text: The last dark journey down below.
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="12">The last dark journey down below.</l>
<l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="13">No, not Chimaera's fiery breath,</l>

lines.text: Nor Gyas, could he rise again,
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="14">Nor Gyas, could he rise again,</l>

lines.text: Shall part us; Justice, strong as death,
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="15">Shall part us; Justice, strong as death,</l>

lines.text: So wills it; so the Fates ordain.
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="16">So wills it; so the Fates ordain.</l>
<l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="17">Whether 'twas Libra saw me born</l>
<l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="18">Or angry Scorpio, lord malign</l>
<l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="19">Of natal hour, or Capricorn,</l>

lines.text: The tyrant of the western brine,
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="20">The tyrant of the western brine,</l>

lines.text: Our planets sure with concord strange
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="21">Our planets sure with concord strange</l>

lines.text: Are blended. You by Jove's blest power
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="22">Are blended.  You by Jove's blest power</l>

lines.text: Were snatch'd from out the baleful range
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="23">Were snatch'd from out the baleful range</l>

lines.text: Of Saturn, and the evil hour
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="24">Of Saturn, and the evil hour</l>

lines.text: Was stay'd, when rapturous benches full
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="25">Was stay'd, when rapturous benches full</l>

lines.text: Three times the auspicious thunder peal'd;
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="26">Three times the auspicious thunder peal'd;</l>

lines.text: Me the curst trunk, that smote my skull,
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="27">Me the curst trunk, that smote my skull,</l>

lines.text: Had slain; but Faunus, strong to shield
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="28">Had slain; but Faunus, strong to shield</l>

lines.text: The friends of Mercury, check'd the blow
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="29">The friends of Mercury, check'd the blow</l>

lines.text: In mid descent. Be sure to pay
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="30">In mid descent.  Be sure to pay</l>

lines.text: The victims and the fane you owe;
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="31">The victims and the fane you owe;</l>

lines.text: Your bard a humbler lamb will slay.
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="32">Your bard a humbler lamb will slay.</l>

edition: John Conington; George Bell and Sons, London 1882

lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="1">Carven ivory have I none</l>

lines.text: No golden cornice in my dwelling shines;
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="2">No golden cornice in my dwelling shines;</l>
<l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="3">Pillars choice of Libyan stone</l>

lines.text: Upbear no architrave from Attic mines;
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="4">Upbear no architrave from Attic mines;</l>
<l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="5">'Twas not mine to enter in</l>

lines.text: To Attalus' broad realms, an unknown heir,
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="6">To Attalus' broad realms, an unknown heir,</l>

lines.text: Nor for me fair clients spin
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="7">Nor for me fair clients spin</l>

lines.text: Laconian purples for their patron's wear.
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="8">Laconian purples for their patron's wear.</l>

lines.text: Truth is mine, and Genius mine;
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="9">Truth is mine, and Genius mine;</l>

lines.text: The rich man comes, and knocks at my low door:
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="10">The rich man comes, and knocks at my low door:</l>
<l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="11">Favour'd thus, I ne'er repine,</l>

lines.text: Nor weary out indulgent Heaven for more:
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="12">Nor weary out indulgent Heaven for more:</l>
<l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="13">In my <placeName key="tgn,7021127">Sabine</placeName> homestead blest,</l>

lines.text: Why should I further tax a generous friend?
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="14">Why should I further tax a generous friend?</l>
<l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="15">Suns are hurrying suns a-west,</l>

lines.text: And newborn moons make speed to meet their end.
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="16">And newborn moons make speed to meet their end.</l>

lines.text: You have hands to square and hew
lines.xml:
<l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="17">
                        <emph>You</emph> have hands to square and hew</l>

lines.text: Vast marble-blocks, hard on your day of doom,
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="18">Vast marble-blocks, hard on your day of doom,</l>
<l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="19">Ever building mansions new,</l>

lines.text: Nor thinking of the mansion of the tomb.
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="20">Nor thinking of the mansion of the tomb.</l>

lines.text: Now you press on ocean's bound,
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="21">Now you press on ocean's bound,</l>

lines.text: Where waves on Baiae beat, as earth were scant;
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="22">Where waves on <placeName key="tgn,7004516">Baiae</placeName> beat, as earth were scant;</l>
<l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="23">Now absorb your neighbour's ground,</l>

lines.text: And tear his landmarks up, your own to plant.
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="24">And tear his landmarks up, your own to plant.</l>
<l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="25">Hedges set round clients' farms</l>

lines.text: Your avarice tramples; see, the outcasts fly,
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="26">Your avarice tramples; see, the outcasts fly,</l>

lines.text: Wife and husband, in their arms
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="27">Wife and husband, in their arms</l>

lines.text: Their fathers' gods, their squalid family.
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="28">Their fathers' gods, their squalid family.</l>

lines.text: Yet no hall that wealth e'er plann'd
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="29">Yet no hall that wealth e'er plann'd</l>

lines.text: Waits you more surely than the wider room
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="30">Waits you more surely than the wider room</l>

lines.text: Traced by Death's yet greedier hand.
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="31">Traced by Death's yet greedier hand.</l>

lines.text: Why strain so far? you cannot leap the tomb.
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="32">Why strain so far? you cannot leap the tomb.</l>
<l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="33">Earth removes the impartial sod</l>

lines.text: Alike for beggar and for monarch's child:
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="34">Alike for beggar and for monarch's child:</l>

lines.text: Nor the slave of Hell's dark god
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="35">Nor the slave of Hell's dark god</l>

lines.text: Convey'd Prometheus back, with bribe beguiled.
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="36">Convey'd Prometheus back, with bribe beguiled.</l>
<l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="37">Pelops he and Pelops' sire</l>

lines.text: Holds, spite of pride, in close captivity;
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="38">Holds, spite of pride, in close captivity;</l>
<l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="39">Beggars, who of labour tire,</l>

lines.text: Call'd or uncall'd, he hears and sets them free.
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="40">Call'd or uncall'd, he hears and sets them free.</l>

edition: John Conington; George Bell and Sons, London 1882

lines.text: Bacchus I saw in mountain glades
lines.xml:
<l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="1">
                        <placeName key="tgn,2097807">Bacchus</placeName> I saw in mountain glades</l>
<l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="2">Retired (believe it, after years!)</l>

lines.text: Teaching his strains to Dryad maids,
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="3">Teaching his strains to Dryad maids,</l>

lines.text: While goat-hoof'd satyrs prick'd their ears.
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="4">While goat-hoof'd satyrs prick'd their ears.</l>

lines.text: Evoe! my eyes with terror glare;
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="5">Evoe! my eyes with terror glare;</l>

lines.text: My heart is revelling with the god;
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="6">My heart is revelling with the god;</l>
<l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="7">'Tis madness!  Evoe! spare, O spare,</l>

lines.text: Dread wielder of the ivied rod!
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="8">Dread wielder of the ivied rod!</l>

lines.text: Yes, I may sing the Thyiad crew,
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="9">Yes, I may sing the Thyiad crew,</l>

lines.text: The stream of wine, the sparkling rills
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="10">The stream of wine, the sparkling rills</l>

lines.text: That run with milk, and honey-dew
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="11">That run with milk, and honey-dew</l>

lines.text: That from the hollow trunk distils;
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="12">That from the hollow trunk distils;</l>

lines.text: And I may sing thy consort's crown,
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="13">And I may sing thy consort's crown,</l>

lines.text: New set in heaven, and Pentheus' hall
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="14">New set in heaven, and Pentheus' hall</l>
<l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="15">With ruthless ruin thundering down,</l>
<l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="16">And proud Lycurgus' funeral.</l>

lines.text: Thou turn'st the rivers, thou the sea;
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="17">Thou turn'st the rivers, thou the sea;</l>

lines.text: Thou, on far summits, moist with wine,
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="18">Thou, on far summits, moist with wine,</l>
<l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="19">Thy Bacchants' tresses harmlessly</l>
<l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="20">Dost knot with living serpent-twine.</l>

lines.text: Thou, when the giants, threatening wrack,
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="21">Thou, when the giants, threatening wrack,</l>
<l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="22">Were clambering up Jove's citadel,</l>
<l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="23">Didst hurl o'erweening Rhoetus back,</l>

lines.text: In tooth and claw a lion fell.
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="24">In tooth and claw a lion fell.</l>

lines.text: Who knew thy feats in dance and play
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="25">Who knew thy feats in dance and play</l>

lines.text: Deem'd thee belike for war's rough game
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="26">Deem'd thee belike for war's rough game</l>
<l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="27">Unmeet: but peace and battle-fray</l>

lines.text: Found thee, their centre, still the same.
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="28">Found thee, their centre, still the same.</l>

lines.text: Grim Cerberus wagg'd his tail to see
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="29">Grim Cerberus wagg'd his tail to see</l>

lines.text: Thy golden horn, nor dreamd of wrong.
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="30">Thy golden horn, nor dreamd of wrong.</l>
<l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="31">But gently fawning, follow'd thee,</l>

lines.text: And lick'd thy feet with triple tongue.
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="32">And lick'd thy feet with triple tongue.</l>

edition: John Conington; George Bell and Sons, London 1882

lines.text: No vulgar wing, nor weakly plied,
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="1">No vulgar wing, nor weakly plied,</l>

lines.text: Shall bear me through the liquid sky;
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="2">Shall bear me through the liquid sky;</l>

lines.text: A two-form'd bard, no more to bide
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="3">A two-form'd bard, no more to bide</l>

lines.text: Within the range of envy's eye
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="4">Within the range of envy's eye</l>

lines.text: 'Mid haunts of men. I, all ungraced
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="5">'Mid haunts of men.  I, all ungraced</l>

lines.text: By gentle blood, I, whom you call
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="6">By gentle blood, I, whom you call</l>

lines.text: Your friend, Maecenas, shall not taste
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="7">Your friend, Maecenas, shall not taste</l>

lines.text: Of death, nor chafe in Lethe's thrall.
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="8">Of death, nor chafe in Lethe's thrall.</l>

lines.text: E'en now a rougher skin expands
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="9">E'en now a rougher skin expands</l>

lines.text: Along my legs: above I change
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="10">Along my legs: above I change</l>

lines.text: To a white bird; and o'er my hands
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="11">To a white bird; and o'er my hands</l>

lines.text: And shoulders grows a plumage strange:
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="12">And shoulders grows a plumage strange:</l>

lines.text: Fleeter than Icarus, see me float
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="13">Fleeter than Icarus, see me float</l>

lines.text: O'er Bosporus, singing as I go,
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="14">O'er Bosporus, singing as I go,</l>
<l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="15">And o'er Gaetulian sands remote,</l>
<l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="16">And Hyperborean fields of snow;</l>

lines.text: By Dacian horde, that masks its fear
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="17">By Dacian horde, that masks its fear</l>

lines.text: Of Marsic steel, shall I be known,
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="18">Of Marsic steel, shall I be known,</l>

lines.text: And furthest Scythian: Spain shall hear
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="19">And furthest Scythian: <placeName key="tgn,1000095">Spain</placeName> shall hear</l>

lines.text: My warbling, and the banks of Rhone.
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="20">My warbling, and the banks of <placeName key="tgn,7023890">Rhone</placeName>.</l>

lines.text: No dirges for my fancied death;
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="21">No dirges for my fancied death;</l>

lines.text: No weak lament, no mournful stave;
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="22">No weak lament, no mournful stave;</l>

lines.text: All clamorous grief were waste of breath,
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="23">All clamorous grief were waste of breath,</l>

lines.text: And vain the tribute of a grave.
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="24">And vain the tribute of a grave.</l>

edition: John Conington; George Bell and Sons, London 1882

lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="1">Bid the unhallow'd crowd avaunt!</l>
<l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="2">Keep holy silence; strains unknown</l>
<l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="3">Till now, the Muses' hierophant,</l>

lines.text: I sing to youths and maids alone.
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="4">I sing to youths and maids alone.</l>

lines.text: Kings o'er their flocks the sceptre wield;
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="5">Kings o'er their flocks the sceptre wield;</l>

lines.text: E'en kings beneath Jove's sceptre bow:
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="6">E'en kings beneath Jove's sceptre bow:</l>
<l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="7">Victor in giant battle-field,</l>

lines.text: He moves all nature with his brow.
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="8">He moves all nature with his brow.</l>

lines.text: This man his planted walks extends
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="9">This man his planted walks extends</l>

lines.text: Beyond his peers; an older name
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="10">Beyond his peers; an older name</l>

lines.text: One to the people's choice commends;
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="11">One to the people's choice commends;</l>

lines.text: One boasts a more unsullied fame;
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="12">One boasts a more unsullied fame;</l>

lines.text: One plumes him on a larger crowd
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="13">One plumes him on a larger crowd</l>

lines.text: Of clients. What are great or small?
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="14">Of clients. What are great or small?</l>

lines.text: Death takes the mean man with the proud;
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="15">Death takes the mean man with the proud;</l>

lines.text: The fatal urn has room for all.
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="16">The fatal urn has room for all.</l>

lines.text: When guilty Pomp the drawn sword sees
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="17">When guilty Pomp the drawn sword sees</l>

lines.text: Hung o'er her, richest feasts in vain
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="18">Hung o'er her, richest feasts in vain</l>

lines.text: Strain their sweet juice her taste to please;
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="19">Strain their sweet juice her taste to please;</l>

lines.text: No lutes, no singing birds again
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="20">No lutes, no singing birds again</l>

lines.text: Will bring her sleep. Sleep knows no pride;
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="21">Will bring her sleep.  Sleep knows no pride;</l>

lines.text: It scorns not cots of village hinds,
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="22">It scorns not cots of village hinds,</l>
<l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="23">Nor shadow-trembling river-side,</l>

lines.text: Nor Tempe, stirr'd by western winds.
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="24">Nor <placeName key="tgn,7014367">Tempe</placeName>, stirr'd by western winds.</l>
<l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="25">Who, having competence, has all,</l>

lines.text: The tumult of the sea defies,
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="26">The tumult of the sea defies,</l>
<l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="27">Nor fears Arcturus' angry fall,</l>

lines.text: Nor fears the Kid-star's sullen rise,
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="28">Nor fears the Kid-star's sullen rise,</l>

lines.text: Though hail-storms on the vineyard beat,
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="29">Though hail-storms on the vineyard beat,</l>

lines.text: Though crops deceive, though trees complain,
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="30">Though crops deceive, though trees complain,</l>

lines.text: One while of showers, one while of heat,
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="31">One while of showers, one while of heat,</l>

lines.text: One while of winter's barbarous reign.
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="32">One while of winter's barbarous reign.</l>

lines.text: Fish feel the narrowing of the main
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="33">Fish feel the narrowing of the main</l>

lines.text: From sunken piles, while on the strand
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="34">From sunken piles, while on the strand</l>
<l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="35">Contractors with their busy train</l>

lines.text: Let down huge stones, and lords of land
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="36">Let down huge stones, and lords of land</l>

lines.text: Affect the sea: but fierce Alarm
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="37">Affect the sea: but fierce Alarm</l>

lines.text: Can clamber to the master's side:
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="38">Can clamber to the master's side:</l>

lines.text: Black Cares can up ihe galley swarm,
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="39">Black Cares can up ihe galley swarm,</l>

lines.text: And close behind the horseman ride.
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="40">And close behind the horseman ride.</l>

lines.text: If Phrygian marbles soothe not pain,
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="41">If Phrygian marbles soothe not pain,</l>
<l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="42">Nor star-bright purple's costliest wear,</l>

lines.text: Nor vines of true Falernian strain,
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="43">Nor vines of true Falernian strain,</l>
<l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="44">Nor Achaemenian spices rare,</l>

lines.text: Why with rich gate and pillard range
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="45">Why with rich gate and pillard range</l>

lines.text: Upbuild new mansions, twice as high,
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="46">Upbuild new mansions, twice as high,</l>

lines.text: Or why my Sabine vale exchange
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="47">Or why my <placeName key="tgn,7021127">Sabine</placeName> vale exchange</l>
<l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="48">For more laborious luxury?</l>

edition: John Conington; George Bell and Sons, London 1882

lines.text: To suffer hardness with good cheer,
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="1">To suffer hardness with good cheer,</l>

lines.text: In sternest school of warfare bred,
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="2">In sternest school of warfare bred,</l>

lines.text: Our youth should learn; let steed and spear
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="3">Our youth should learn; let steed and spear</l>

lines.text: Make him one day the Parthian's dread;
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="4">Make him one day the Parthian's dread;</l>

lines.text: Cold skies, keen perils, brace his life.
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="5">Cold skies, keen perils, brace his life.</l>

lines.text: Methinks I see from rampired town
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="6">Methinks I see from rampired town</l>
<l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="7">Some battling tyrant's matron wife,</l>

lines.text: Some maiden, look in terror down,—
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="8">Some maiden, look in terror down,—</l>

lines.text: “Ah, my dear lord, untrain'd in war!
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="9">“Ah, my dear lord, untrain'd in war!</l>

lines.text: O tempt not the infuriate mood
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="10">O tempt not the infuriate mood</l>

lines.text: Of that fell lion I see! from far
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="11">Of that fell lion I see! from far</l>

lines.text: He plunges through a tide of blood!“
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="12">He plunges through a tide of blood!“</l>

lines.text: What joy, for fatherland to die!
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="13">What joy, for fatherland to die!</l>

lines.text: Death's darts e'en flying feet o'ertake,
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="14">Death's darts e'en flying feet o'ertake,</l>
<l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="15">Nor spare a recreant chivalry,</l>

lines.text: A back that cowers, or loins that quake.
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="16">A back that cowers, or loins that quake.</l>
<l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="17">True Virtue never knows defeat:</l>

lines.text: Her robes she keeps unsullied still,
lines.xml:
<l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="18">
                        <emph>Her</emph> robes she keeps unsullied still,</l>

lines.text: Nor takes, nor quits, her curule seat
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="19">Nor takes, nor quits, <emph>her</emph> curule seat</l>

lines.text: To please a people's veering will.
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="20">To please a people's veering will.</l>

lines.text: True Virtue opens heaven to worth:
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="21">True Virtue opens heaven to worth:</l>

lines.text: She makes the way she does not find:
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="22">She makes the way she does not find:</l>

lines.text: The vulgar crowd, the humid earth,
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="23">The vulgar crowd, the humid earth,</l>
<l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="24">Her soaring pinion leaves behind.</l>

lines.text: Seal'd lips have blessings sure to come:
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="25">Seal'd lips have blessings sure to come:</l>
<l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="26">Who drags <placeName key="tgn,7011134">Eleusis</placeName>' rite today,</l>

lines.text: That man shall never share my home,
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="27">That man shall never share my home,</l>

lines.text: Or join my voyage: roofs give way
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="28">Or join my voyage: roofs give way</l>

lines.text: And boats are wreck'd: true men and thieves
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="29">And boats are wreck'd: true men and thieves</l>
<l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="30">Neglected Justice oft confounds:</l>

lines.text: Though Vengeance halt, she seldom leaves
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="31">Though Vengeance halt, she seldom leaves</l>

lines.text: The wretch whose flying steps she hounds.
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="32">The wretch whose flying steps she hounds.</l>

edition: John Conington; George Bell and Sons, London 1882

lines.text: The man of firm and righteous will,
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="1">The man of firm and righteous will,</l>

lines.text: No rabble, clamorous for the wrong,
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="2">No rabble, clamorous for the wrong,</l>

lines.text: No tyrant's brow, whose frown may kill,
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="3">No tyrant's brow, whose frown may kill,</l>

lines.text: Can shake the strength that makes him strong:
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="4">Can shake the strength that makes him strong:</l>

lines.text: Not winds, that chafe the sea they sway,
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="5">Not winds, that chafe the sea they sway,</l>

lines.text: Nor Jove's right hand, with lightning red:
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="6">Nor Jove's right hand, with lightning red:</l>

lines.text: Should Nature's pillar'd frame give way,
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="7">Should Nature's pillar'd frame give way,</l>

lines.text: That wreck would strike one fearless head.
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="8">That wreck would strike one fearless head.</l>

<l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="9">Pollux and roving <placeName key="tgn,2086286">Hercules</placeName>
                     </l>

lines.text: Thus won their way to Heaven's proud steep,
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="10">Thus won their way to Heaven's proud steep,</l>
<l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="11">'Mid whom Augustus, couch'd at ease,</l>

lines.text: Dyes his red lips with nectar deep.
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="12">Dyes his red lips with nectar deep.</l>

lines.text: For this, great Bacchus, tigers drew
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="13">For this, great <placeName key="tgn,2097807">Bacchus</placeName>, tigers drew</l>

lines.text: Thy glorious car, untaught to slave
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="14">Thy glorious car, untaught to slave</l>
<l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="15">In harness: thus Quirinus flew</l>

lines.text: On Mars' wing'd steeds from Acheron's wave,
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="16">On <placeName key="tgn,2090583">Mars</placeName>' wing'd steeds from Acheron's wave,</l>

lines.text: When Juno spoke with Heaven's assent:
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="17">When <placeName key="tgn,2075297">Juno</placeName> spoke with Heaven's assent:</l>
<l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="18">“O <placeName key="tgn,7002329">Ilium</placeName>, <placeName key="tgn,7002329">Ilium</placeName>, wretched town!</l>
<l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="19">The judge accurst, incontinent,</l>

lines.text: And stranger dame have dragg'd thee down.
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="20">And stranger dame have dragg'd thee down.</l>

lines.text: Pallas and I, since Priam's sire
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="21">Pallas and I, since Priam's sire</l>

lines.text: Denied the gods his pledged reward,
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="22">Denied the gods his pledged reward,</l>

lines.text: Had doom'd them all to sword and fire,
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="23">Had doom'd them all to sword and fire,</l>

lines.text: The people and their perjured lord.
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="24">The people and their perjured lord.</l>

lines.text: No more the adulterous guest can charm
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="25">No more the adulterous guest can charm</l>

lines.text: The Spartan queen: the house forsworn
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="26">The Spartan queen: the house forsworn</l>

lines.text: No more repels by Hector's arm
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="27">No more repels by Hector's arm</l>
<l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="28">My warriors, baffled and outworn:</l>

lines.text: Hush'd is the war our strife made long:
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="29">Hush'd is the war our strife made long:</l>

lines.text: I welcome now, my hatred o'er,
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="30">I welcome now, my hatred o'er,</l>

lines.text: A grandson in the child of wrong,
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="31">A grandson in the child of wrong,</l>

lines.text: Him whom the Trojan priestess bore.
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="32">Him whom the Trojan priestess bore.</l>

lines.text: Receive him, Mars! the gates of flame
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="33">Receive him, Mars! the gates of flame</l>

lines.text: May open: let him taste forgiven
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="34">May open: let him taste forgiven</l>

lines.text: The nectar, and enrol his name
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="35">The nectar, and enrol his name</l>

lines.text: Among the peaceful ranks of Heaven.
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="36">Among the peaceful ranks of Heaven.</l>

lines.text: Let the wide waters sever still
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="37">Let the wide waters sever still</l>

lines.text: Ilium and Rome, the exiled race
lines.xml:
<l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="38">
                        <placeName key="tgn,7002329">Ilium</placeName> and <placeName key="perseus,Rome">Rome</placeName>, the exiled race</l>

lines.text: May reign and prosper where they will:
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="39">May reign and prosper where they will:</l>
<l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="40">So but in <placeName key="tgn,7008038">Paris</placeName>' burial-place</l>

lines.text: The cattle sport, the wild beasts hide
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="41">The cattle sport, the wild beasts hide</l>

lines.text: Their cubs, the Capitol may stand
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="42">Their cubs, the Capitol may stand</l>

lines.text: All bright, and Rome in warlike pride
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="43">All bright, and <placeName key="perseus,Rome">Rome</placeName> in warlike pride</l>

lines.text: O'er Media stretch a conqueror's hand.
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="44">O'er Media stretch a conqueror's hand.</l>

lines.text: Aye, let her scatter far and wide
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="45">Aye, let her scatter far and wide</l>

lines.text: Her terror, where tbe land-lock'd waves
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="46">Her terror, where tbe land-lock'd waves</l>

<l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="47">
                        <placeName key="tgn,1000003">Europe</placeName> from Afric's shore divide,</l>

lines.text: Where swelling Nile the corn-field laves—
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="48">Where swelling <placeName key="tgn,1127805">Nile</placeName> the corn-field laves—</l>

lines.text: Of strength more potent to disdain
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="49">Of strength more potent to disdain</l>

lines.text: Hid gold, best buried in the mine,
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="50">Hid gold, best buried in the mine,</l>

lines.text: Than gather it with hand profane,
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="51">Than gather it with hand profane,</l>

lines.text: That for man's greed would rob a shrine.
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="52">That for man's greed would rob a shrine.</l>

lines.text: Whate'er the bound to earth ordain'd,
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="53">Whate'er the bound to earth ordain'd,</l>

lines.text: There let her reach the arm of power,
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="54">There let her reach the arm of power,</l>

lines.text: Travelling, where raves the fire unrein'd,
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="55">Travelling, where raves the fire unrein'd,</l>

lines.text: And where the storm-cloud and the shower.
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="56">And where the storm-cloud and the shower.</l>

lines.text: Yet, warlike Roman, know thy doom,
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="57">Yet, warlike Roman, know thy doom,</l>

lines.text: Nor, drunken with a conqueror's joy,
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="58">Nor, drunken with a conqueror's joy,</l>

lines.text: Or blind with duteous zeal, presume
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="59">Or blind with duteous zeal, presume</l>
<l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="60">To build again ancestral <placeName key="perseus,Troy">Troy</placeName>.</l>

lines.text: Should Troy revive to hateful life,
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="61">Should <placeName key="perseus,Troy">Troy</placeName> revive to hateful life,</l>

lines.text: Her star again should set in gore,
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="62">Her star again should set in gore,</l>

lines.text: While I, Jove's sister and his wife,
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="63">While I, Jove's sister and his wife,</l>

lines.text: To victory led my host once more.
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="64">To victory led my host once more.</l>

lines.text: Though Phoebus thrice in brazen mail
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="65">Though Phoebus thrice in brazen mail</l>

lines.text: Should case her towers, they thrice should fall,
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="66">Should case her towers, they thrice should fall,</l>

lines.text: Storm'd by my Greeks: thrice wives should wail
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="67">Storm'd by my Greeks: thrice wives should wail</l>

lines.text: Husband and son, themselves in thrall.”—
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="68">Husband and son, themselves in thrall.”—</l>

lines.text: Such thunders from the lyre of love!
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="69">Such thunders from the lyre of love!</l>
<l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="70">Back, wayward Muse! refrain, refrain</l>

lines.text: To tell the talk of gods above,
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="71">To tell the talk of gods above,</l>

lines.text: And dwarf high themes in puny strain.
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="72">And dwarf high themes in puny strain.</l>

edition: John Conington; George Bell and Sons, London 1882

lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="1">Come down, Calliope, from above:</l>

lines.text: Breathe on the pipe a strain of fire:
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="2">Breathe on the pipe a strain of fire:</l>

lines.text: Or if a graver note thou love,
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="3">Or if a graver note thou love,</l>

lines.text: With Phoebus' cittern and his lyre.
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="4">With Phoebus' cittern and his lyre.</l>

lines.text: You hear her? or is this the play
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="5">You hear her? or is this the play</l>
<l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="6">Of fond illusion? Hark! meseems</l>

lines.text: Through gardens of the good I stray,
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="7">Through gardens of the good I stray,</l>
<l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="8">'Mid murmuring gales and purling streams.</l>

lines.text: Me, as I lay on Vultur's steep,
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="9">Me, as I lay on Vultur's steep,</l>
<l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="10">A truant past <placeName key="tgn,7010380">Apulia</placeName>'s bound,</l>

lines.text: O'ertired, poor child, with play and sleep,
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="11">O'ertired, poor child, with play and sleep,</l>

lines.text: With living green the stock-doves crown'd—
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="12">With living green the stock-doves crown'd—</l>
<l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="13">A legend, nay, a miracle,</l>
<l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="14">By Acherontia's nestlings told,</l>

lines.text: By all in Bantine glade that dwell,
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="15">By all in Bantine glade that dwell,</l>

lines.text: Or till the rich Forentan mould.
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="16">Or till the rich Forentan mould.</l>

lines.text: “Bears, vipers, spared him as he lay,
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="17">“Bears, vipers, spared him as he lay,</l>

lines.text: The sacred garland deck'd his hair,
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="18">The sacred garland deck'd his hair,</l>

lines.text: The myrtle blended with the bay:
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="19">The myrtle blended with the bay:</l>

lines.text: The child's inspired: the gods were there.”
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="20">The child's inspired: the gods were there.”</l>

lines.text: Your grace, sweet Muses, shields me still
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="21">Your grace, sweet Muses, shields me still</l>

lines.text: On Sabine heights, or lets me range
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="22">On <placeName key="tgn,7021127">Sabine</placeName> heights, or lets me range</l>
<l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="23">Where cool <placeName key="perseus,Praeneste">Praeneste</placeName>, <placeName key="perseus,Tibur">Tibur</placeName>'s hill,</l>
<l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="24">Or liquid <placeName key="perseus,Baiae">Baiae</placeName> proffers change.</l>

lines.text: Me to your springs, your dances true,
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="25">Me to your springs, your dances true,</l>

lines.text: Philippi bore not to the ground,
lines.xml:
<l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="26">
                        <placeName key="tgn,7010789">Philippi</placeName> bore not to the ground,</l>

lines.text: Nor the doom'd tree in falling slew,
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="27">Nor the doom'd tree in falling slew,</l>
<l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="28">Nor billowy Palinurus drown'd.</l>

lines.text: Grant me your presence, blithe and fain
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="29">Grant me your presence, blithe and fain</l>

lines.text: Mad Bosporus shall my bark explore;
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="30">Mad <placeName key="tgn,1115068">Bosporus</placeName> shall my bark explore;</l>

lines.text: My foot shall tread the sandy plain
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="31">My foot shall tread the sandy plain</l>
<l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="32">That glows beside Assyria's shore;</l>
<l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="33">'Mid Briton tribes, the stranger's foe,</l>

lines.text: And Spaniards, drunk with horses' blood,
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="34">And Spaniards, drunk with horses' blood,</l>

lines.text: And quiver'd Scythians, will I go
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="35">And quiver'd Scythians, will I go</l>

lines.text: Unharm'd, and look on Tanais' flood.
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="36">Unharm'd, and look on <placeName key="tgn,1123466">Tanais</placeName>' flood.</l>

lines.text: When Caesar's self in peaceful town
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="37">When Caesar's self in peaceful town</l>

lines.text: The weary veteran's home has made,
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="38">The weary veteran's home has made,</l>

lines.text: You bid him lay his helmet down
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="39">You bid him lay his helmet down</l>

lines.text: And rest in your Pierian shade.
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="40">And rest in your Pierian shade.</l>

lines.text: Mild thoughts you plant, and joy to see
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="41">Mild thoughts you plant, and joy to see</l>
