lines.text: Mild thoughts take root. The nations know
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="42">Mild thoughts take root.  The nations know</l>
<l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="43">How with descending thunder he</l>
<l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="44">The impious Titans hurl'd below,</l>

lines.text: Who rules dull earth and stormy seas,
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="45">Who rules dull earth and stormy seas,</l>

lines.text: And towns of men, and realms of pain,
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="46">And towns of men, and realms of pain,</l>
<l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="47">And gods, and mortal companies,</l>
<l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="48">Alone, impartial in his reign.</l>

lines.text: Yet Jove had fear'd the giant rush,
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="49">Yet Jove had fear'd the giant rush,</l>

lines.text: Their upraised arms, their port of pride,
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="50">Their upraised arms, their port of pride,</l>

lines.text: And the twin brethren bent to push
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="51">And the twin brethren bent to push</l>
<l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="52">Huge <placeName key="tgn,4008379">Pelion</placeName> up <placeName key="tgn,7011019">Olympus</placeName>' side.</l>

lines.text: But Typhon, Mimas, what could these,
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="53">But Typhon, Mimas, what could these,</l>
<l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="54">Or what Porphyrion's stalwart scorn,</l>

lines.text: Rhoetus, or he whose spears were trees,
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="55">Rhoetus, or he whose spears were trees,</l>
<l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="56">Enceladus, from earth uptorn,</l>

lines.text: As on they rush'd in mad career
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="57">As on they rush'd in mad career</l>

lines.text: 'Gainst Pallas' shield? Here met the foe
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="58">'Gainst Pallas' shield? Here met the foe</l>
<l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="59">Fierce <placeName key="tgn,1050339">Vulcan</placeName>, queenly Juno here,</l>

lines.text: And he who ne'er shall quit his bow,
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="60">And he who ne'er shall quit his bow,</l>

lines.text: Who laves in clear Castalian flood
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="61">Who laves in clear Castalian flood</l>

lines.text: His locks, and loves the leafy growth
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="62">His locks, and loves the leafy growth</l>

lines.text: Of Lycia next his native wood,
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="63">Of <placeName key="tgn,7001294">Lycia</placeName> next his native wood,</l>

lines.text: The Delian and the Pataran both.
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="64">The Delian and the Pataran both.</l>

lines.text: Strength, mindless, falls by its own weight;
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="65">Strength, mindless, falls by its own weight;</l>

lines.text: Strength, mix'd with mind, is made more strong
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="66">Strength, mix'd with mind, is made more strong</l>

lines.text: By the just gods, who surely hate
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="67">By the just gods, who surely hate</l>

lines.text: The strength whose thoughts are set on wrong.
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="68">The strength whose thoughts are set on wrong.</l>
<l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="69">Let hundred-handed Gyas bear</l>
<l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="70">His witness, and Orion known</l>

lines.text: Tempter of Dian, chaste and fair,
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="71">Tempter of Dian, chaste and fair,</l>
<l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="72">By Dian's maiden dart o'erthrown.</l>

lines.text: Hurl'd on the monstrous shapes she bred,
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="73">Hurl'd on the monstrous shapes she bred,</l>

lines.text: Earth groans, and mourns her children thrust
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="74">Earth groans, and mourns her children thrust</l>

lines.text: To Orcus; Aetna's weight of lead
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="75">To Orcus; <placeName key="tgn,7003867">Aetna</placeName>'s weight of lead</l>

lines.text: Keeps down the fire that breaks its crust;
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="76">Keeps down the fire that breaks its crust;</l>

lines.text: Still sits the bird on Tityos' breast,
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="77">Still sits the bird on Tityos' breast,</l>
<l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="78">The warder of Unlawful love;</l>
<l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="79">Still suffers lewd Pirithous, prest</l>

lines.text: By massive chains no hand may move.
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="80">By massive chains no hand may move.</l>

edition: John Conington; George Bell and Sons, London 1882

lines.text: Jove rules in heaven, his thunder shows;
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="1">Jove rules in heaven, his thunder shows;</l>
<l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="2">Henceforth Augustus earth shall own</l>

lines.text: Her present god, now Briton foes
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="3">Her present god, now Briton foes</l>

lines.text: And Persians bow before his throne.
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="4">And Persians bow before his throne.</l>

lines.text: Has Crassus' soldier ta'en to wife
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="5">Has Crassus' soldier ta'en to wife</l>

lines.text: A base barbarian, and grown grey
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="6">A base barbarian, and grown grey</l>
<l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="7">(Woe, for a nation's tainted life!)</l>
<l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="8">Earning his foemen-kinsmen's pay,</l>

lines.text: His king, forsooth, a Mede, his sire
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="9">His king, forsooth, a <placeName key="tgn,1045322">Mede</placeName>, his sire</l>

lines.text: A Marsian? can he name forget,
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="10">A Marsian? can he name forget,</l>
<l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="11">Gown, sacred shield, undying fire,</l>

lines.text: And Jove and Rome are standing yet?
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="12">And Jove and <placeName key="perseus,Rome">Rome</placeName> are standing yet?</l>
<l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="13">'Twas this that Regulus foresaw,</l>

lines.text: What time he spurn'd the foul disgrace
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="14">What time he spurn'd the foul disgrace</l>

lines.text: Of peace, whose precedent would draw
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="15">Of peace, whose precedent would draw</l>
<l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="16">Destruction on an unborn race,</l>

lines.text: Should aught but death the prisoner's chain
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="17">Should aught but death the prisoner's chain</l>
<l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="18">Unrivet. “I have seen,” he said,</l>
<l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="19">“<placeName key="perseus,Rome">Rome</placeName>'s eagle in a Punic fane,</l>

lines.text: And armour, ne'er a blood-drop shed,
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="20">And armour, ne'er a blood-drop shed,</l>

lines.text: Stripp'd from the soldier; I have seen
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="21">Stripp'd from the soldier; I have seen</l>

lines.text: Free sons of Rome with arms fast tied;
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="22">Free sons of <placeName key="perseus,Rome">Rome</placeName> with arms fast tied;</l>

lines.text: The fields we spoil'd with corn are green,
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="23">The fields we spoil'd with corn are green,</l>

lines.text: And Carthage opes her portals wide.
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="24">And <placeName key="perseus,Carthage">Carthage</placeName> opes her portals wide.</l>

lines.text: The warrior, sure, redeem'd by gold,
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="25">The warrior, sure, redeem'd by gold,</l>

lines.text: Will fight the bolder! Aye, you heap
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="26">Will fight the bolder! Aye, you heap</l>

lines.text: On baseness loss. The hues of old
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="27">On baseness loss.  The hues of old</l>

lines.text: Revisit not the wool we steep;
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="28">Revisit not the wool we steep;</l>

lines.text: And genuine worth, expell'd by fear,
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="29">And genuine worth, expell'd by fear,</l>

lines.text: Returns not to the worthless slave.
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="30">Returns not to the worthless slave.</l>

lines.text: Break but her meshes, will the deer
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="31">Break but her meshes, will the deer</l>

lines.text: Assail you? then will he be brave
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="32">Assail you? then will he be brave</l>

lines.text: Who once to faithless foes has knelt;
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="33">Who once to faithless foes has knelt;</l>

lines.text: Yes, Carthage yet his spear will fly,
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="34">Yes, <placeName key="perseus,Carthage">Carthage</placeName> yet his spear will fly,</l>

lines.text: Who with bound arms the cord has felt,
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="35">Who with bound arms the cord has felt,</l>

lines.text: The coward, and has fear'd to die.
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="36">The coward, and has fear'd to die.</l>

lines.text: He knows not, he, how life is won;
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="37">He knows not, he, how life is won;</l>

lines.text: Thinks war, like peace, a thing of trade!
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="38">Thinks war, like peace, a thing of trade!</l>

lines.text: Great art thou, Carthage! mate the sun,
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="39">Great art thou, <placeName key="perseus,Carthage">Carthage</placeName>! mate the sun,</l>

lines.text: While Italy in dust is laid!”
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="40">While <placeName key="tgn,1000080">Italy</placeName> in dust is laid!”</l>

lines.text: His wife's pure kiss he waved aside,
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="41">His wife's pure kiss he waved aside,</l>

lines.text: And prattling boys, as one disgraced,
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="42">And prattling boys, as one disgraced,</l>

lines.text: They tell us, and with manly pride
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="43">They tell us, and with manly pride</l>

lines.text: Stern on the ground his visage placed.
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="44">Stern on the ground his visage placed.</l>

lines.text: With counsel thus ne'er else aread
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="45">With counsel thus ne'er else aread</l>

lines.text: He nerved the fathers' weak intent,
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="46">He nerved the fathers' weak intent,</l>

lines.text: And, girt by friends that mourn'd him, sped
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="47">And, girt by friends that mourn'd him, sped</l>
<l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="48">Into illustrious banishment.</l>

lines.text: Well witting what the torturer's art
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="49">Well witting what the torturer's art</l>
<l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="50">Design'd him, with like unconcern</l>

lines.text: The press of kin he push'd apart
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="51">The press of kin he push'd apart</l>
<l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="52">And crowds encumbering his return,</l>

lines.text: As though, some tedious business o'er
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="53">As though, some tedious business o'er</l>

lines.text: Of clients' court, his journey lay
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="54">Of clients' court, his journey lay</l>
<l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="55">Towards <placeName key="perseus,Venafrum">Venafrum</placeName>'s grassy floor,</l>
<l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="56">Or Sparta-built <placeName key="tgn,7004100">Tarentum</placeName>'s bay.</l>

edition: John Conington; George Bell and Sons, London 1882

lines.text: Your fathers' guilt you still must pay,
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="1">Your fathers' guilt you still must pay,</l>

lines.text: Till, Roman, you restore each shrine,
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="2">Till, Roman, you restore each shrine,</l>
<l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="3">Each temple, 'mouldering in decay,</l>
<l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="4">And smoke-grimed statue, scarce divine.</l>
<l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="5">Revering Heaven, you rule below;</l>

lines.text: Be that your base, your coping still;
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="6">Be that your base, your coping still;</l>
<l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="7">'Tis Heaven neglected bids o'erflow</l>
<l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="8">The measure of Italian ill.</l>
<l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="9">Now Pacorus and Monaeses twice</l>

lines.text: Have given our unblest arms the foil;
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="10">Have given our unblest arms the foil;</l>
<l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="11">Their necklaces, of mean device;</l>

lines.text: Smiling they deck with Roman spoil.
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="12">Smiling they deck with Roman spoil.</l>

lines.text: Our city, torn by faction's throes,
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="13">Our city, torn by faction's throes,</l>
<l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="14">Dacian and Ethiop well-nigh razed,</l>

lines.text: These with their dreadful navy, those
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="15">These with their dreadful navy, those</l>
<l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="16">For archer-prowess rather praised.</l>
<l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="17">An evil age erewhile debased</l>

lines.text: The marriage-bed, the race, the home;
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="18">The marriage-bed, the race, the home;</l>

lines.text: Thence rose the flood whose waters waste
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="19">Thence rose the flood whose waters waste</l>

lines.text: The nation and the name of Rome.
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="20">The nation and the name of <placeName key="perseus,Rome">Rome</placeName>.</l>

lines.text: Not such their birth, who stain'd for us
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="21">Not such their birth, who stain'd for us</l>

lines.text: The sea with Punic carnage red,
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="22">The sea with Punic carnage red,</l>
<l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="23">Smote Pyrrhus, smote Antiochus,</l>
<l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="24">And Hannibal, the Roman's dread.</l>
<l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="25">Theirs was a hardy soldier-brood,</l>

lines.text: Inured all day the land to till
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="26">Inured all day the land to till</l>

lines.text: With Sabine spade, then shoulder wood
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="27">With <placeName key="tgn,7021127">Sabine</placeName> spade, then shoulder wood</l>

lines.text: Hewn at a stern old mother's will,
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="28">Hewn at a stern old mother's will,</l>

lines.text: When sunset lengthen'd from each height
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="29">When sunset lengthen'd from each height</l>

lines.text: The shadows, and unyoked the steer,
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="30">The shadows, and unyoked the steer,</l>
<l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="31">Restoring in its westward flight</l>

lines.text: The hour to toilworn travail dear.
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="32">The hour to toilworn travail dear.</l>

lines.text: What has not cankering Time made worse?
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="33">What has not cankering Time made worse?</l>
<l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="34">Viler than grandsires, sires beget</l>

lines.text: Ourselves, yet baser, soon to curse
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="35">Ourselves, yet baser, soon to curse</l>

lines.text: The world with offspring baser yet.
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="36">The world with offspring baser yet.</l>

edition: John Conington; George Bell and Sons, London 1882

lines.text: Why weep for him whom sweet Favonian airs
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="1">Why weep for him whom sweet Favonian airs</l>

lines.text: Will waft next spring, Asteria, back to you,
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="2">Will waft next spring, Asteria, back to you,</l>
<l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="3">Rich with <placeName key="tgn,7016608">Bithynia</placeName>'s wares,</l>
<l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="4">A lover fond and true,</l>

lines.text: Your Gyges? He, detain'd by stormy stress
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="5">Your Gyges? He, detain'd by stormy stress</l>

lines.text: At Oricum, about the Goat-star's rise,
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="6">At Oricum, about the Goat-star's rise,</l>
<l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="7">Cold, wakeful, comfortless,</l>
<l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="8">The long night weeping lies.</l>
<l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="9">Meantime his lovesick hostess' messenger</l>

lines.text: Talks of the flames that waste poor Chloe's heart
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="10">Talks of the flames that waste poor Chloe's heart</l>
<l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="11">(Flames lit for you, not her!)</l>
<l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="12">With a besieger's art;</l>

lines.text: Shows how a treacherous woman's lying breath
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="13">Shows how a treacherous woman's lying breath</l>

lines.text: Once on a time on trustful Proetus won
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="14">Once on a time on trustful Proetus won</l>
<l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="15">To doom to early death</l>
<l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="16">Too chaste Bellerophon;</l>

lines.text: Warns him of Peleus' peril, all but slain
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="17">Warns him of Peleus' peril, all but slain</l>

lines.text: For virtuous scorn of fair Hippolyta,
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="18">For virtuous scorn of fair Hippolyta,</l>
<l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="19">And tells again each tale</l>
<l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="20">That e'er led heart astray.</l>

lines.text: In vain; for deafer than Icarian seas
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="21">In vain; for deafer than Icarian seas</l>

lines.text: He hears, untainted yet. But, lady fair,
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="22">He hears, untainted yet. But, lady fair,</l>
<l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="23">What if Enipeus please</l>
<l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="24">Your listless eye? beware!</l>

lines.text: Though true it be that none with surer seat
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="25">Though true it be that none with surer seat</l>

lines.text: O'er Mars's grassy turf is seen to ride,
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="26">O'er Mars's grassy turf is seen to ride,</l>
<l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="27">Nor any swims so fleet</l>
<l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="28">Adown the Tuscan tide,</l>

lines.text: Yet keep each evening door and window barr'd;
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="29">Yet keep each evening door and window barr'd;</l>

lines.text: Look not abroad when music strikes up shrill,
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="30">Look not abroad when music strikes up shrill,</l>

lines.text: And though he call you hard,
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="31">And though he call you hard,</l>
<l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="32">Remain obdurate still.</l>

edition: John Conington; George Bell and Sons, London 1882

lines.text: The first of March! a man unwed!
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="1">The first of March! a man unwed!</l>

lines.text: What can these flowers, this censer mean?
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="2">What can these flowers, this censer mean?</l>

lines.text: Or what these embers, glowing red
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="3">Or what these embers, glowing red</l>
<l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="4">On sods of green?</l>

lines.text: You ask, in either language skill'd!
lines.xml:
<l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="5">
                        <emph>You</emph> ask, in either language skill'd!</l>

lines.text: A feast I vow'd to Bacchus free,
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="6">A feast I vow'd to Bacchus free,</l>

lines.text: A white he-goat, when all but kill'd
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="7">A white he-goat, when all but kill'd</l>
<l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="8">By falling tree.</l>

lines.text: So, when that holyday comes round,
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="9">So, when that holyday comes round,</l>

lines.text: It sees me still the rosin clear
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="10">It sees me still the rosin clear</l>

lines.text: From this my wine-jar, first embrown'd
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="11">From this my wine-jar, first embrown'd</l>
<l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="12">In Tullus' year.</l>

lines.text: Come, crush one hundred cups for life
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="13">Come, crush one hundred cups for life</l>
<l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="14">Preserved, Maecenas; keep till day</l>

lines.text: The candles lit; let noise and strife
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="15">The candles lit; let noise and strife</l>
<l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="16">Be far away.</l>

lines.text: Lay down that load of state-concern;
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="17">Lay down that load of state-concern;</l>

lines.text: The Dacian hosts are all o'erthrown;
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="18">The Dacian hosts are all o'erthrown;</l>

lines.text: The Mede, that sought our overturn,
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="19">The <placeName key="tgn,1045322">Mede</placeName>, that sought our overturn,</l>
<l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="20">Now seeks his own;</l>

lines.text: A servant now, our ancient foe,
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="21">A servant now, our ancient foe,</l>

lines.text: The Spaniard, wears at last our chain;
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="22">The Spaniard, wears at last our chain;</l>

lines.text: The Scythian half unbends his bow
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="23">The Scythian half unbends his bow</l>
<l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="24">And quits the plain.</l>

lines.text: Then fret not lest the state should ail;
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="25">Then fret not lest the state should ail;</l>

lines.text: A private man such thoughts may spare;
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="26">A private man such thoughts may spare;</l>
<l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="27">Enjoy the present hour's regale,</l>
<l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="28">And banish care.</l>

edition: John Conington; George Bell and Sons, London 1882

lines.text: While I had power to bless you,
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="1">While I had power to bless you,</l>
lines.speaker: Horace

lines.text: Nor any round that neck his arms did fling
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="2">Nor any round that neck his arms did fling</l>
lines.speaker: Horace

lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="3">More privileged to caress you,</l>
lines.speaker: Horace

lines.text: Happier was Horace than the Persian king.
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="4">Happier was Horace than the Persian king.</l>
lines.speaker: Horace

lines.text: While you for none were pining
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="5">While you for none were pining</l>
lines.speaker: Lydia

lines.text: Sorer, nor Lydia after Chloe came,
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="6">Sorer, nor Lydia after Chloe came,</l>
lines.speaker: Lydia

lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="7">Lydia, her peers outshining,</l>
lines.speaker: Lydia

lines.text: Might match her own with Ilia's Roman fame.
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="8">Might match her own with Ilia's Roman fame.</l>
lines.speaker: Lydia

lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="9">Now Chloe is my treasure,</l>
lines.speaker: Horace

lines.text: Whose voice, whose touch, can make sweet music flow:
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="10">Whose voice, whose touch, can make sweet music flow:</l>
lines.speaker: Horace

lines.text: For her I'd die with pleasure,
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="11">For her I'd die with pleasure,</l>
lines.speaker: Horace

lines.text: Would Fate but spare the dear survivor so.
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="12">Would Fate but spare the dear survivor so.</l>
lines.speaker: Horace

lines.text: I love my own fond lover,
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="13">I love my own fond lover,</l>
lines.speaker: Lydia

lines.text: Young Calais, son of Thurian Ornytus:
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="14">Young <placeName key="tgn,7009002">Calais</placeName>, son of Thurian Ornytus:</l>
lines.speaker: Lydia

lines.text: For him I'd die twice over,
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="15">For him I'd die twice over,</l>
lines.speaker: Lydia

lines.text: Would Fate but spare the sweet survivor thus.
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="16">Would Fate but spare the sweet survivor thus.</l>
lines.speaker: Lydia

lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="17">What now, if Love returning</l>
lines.speaker: Horace

lines.text: Should pair us 'neath his brazen yoke once more,
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="18">Should pair us 'neath his brazen yoke once more,</l>
lines.speaker: Horace

lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="19">And, bright-hair'd Chloe spurning,</l>
lines.speaker: Horace

lines.text: Horace to off-cast Lydia ope his door?
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="20">Horace to off-cast Lydia ope his door?</l>
lines.speaker: Horace

lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="21">Though he is fairer, milder,</l>
lines.speaker: Lydia

lines.text: Than starlight, you lighter than bark of tree,
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="22">Than starlight, you lighter than bark of tree,</l>
lines.speaker: Lydia

lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="23">Than stormy <placeName key="tgn,7008301">Hadria</placeName> wilder,</l>
lines.speaker: Lydia

lines.text: With you to live, to die, were bliss for me.
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="24">With you to live, to die, were bliss for me.</l>
lines.speaker: Lydia

edition: John Conington; George Bell and Sons, London 1882

lines.text: Ah Lyce! though your drink were Tanais,
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="1">Ah Lyce! though your drink were <placeName key="tgn,1123466">Tanais</placeName>,</l>

lines.text: Your husband some rude savage, you would weep
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="2">Your husband some rude savage, you would weep</l>

lines.text: To leave me shivering, on a night like this,
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="3">To leave me shivering, on a night like this,</l>
<l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="4">Where storms their watches keep.</l>

lines.text: Hark! how your door is creaking! how the grove
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="5">Hark! how your door is creaking! how the grove</l>

lines.text: In your fair courtyard, while the wild winds blow,
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="6">In your fair courtyard, while the wild winds blow,</l>

lines.text: Wails in accord! with what transparence Jove
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="7">Wails in accord! with what transparence Jove</l>
<l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="8">Is glazing the driven snow!</l>

lines.text: Cease that proud temper: Venus loves it not:
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="9">Cease that proud temper: Venus loves it not:</l>

lines.text: The rope may break, the wheel may backward turn:
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="10">The rope may break, the wheel may backward turn:</l>

lines.text: Begetting you, no Tuscan sire begot
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="11">Begetting you, no Tuscan sire begot</l>
<l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="12">Penelope the stern.</l>

lines.text: O, though no gift, no “prevalence of prayer,”
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="13">O, though no gift, no “prevalence of prayer,”</l>

lines.text: Nor lovers' paleness deep as violet,
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="14">Nor lovers' paleness deep as violet,</l>

lines.text: Nor husband, smit with a Pierian fair,
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="15">Nor husband, smit with a Pierian fair,</l>
<l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="16">Move you, have pity yet!</l>

lines.text: O harder e'en than toughest heart of oak,
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="17">O harder e'en than toughest heart of oak,</l>

lines.text: Deafer than uncharm'd snake to suppliant moans!
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="18">Deafer than uncharm'd snake to suppliant moans!</l>

lines.text: This side, I warn you, will not always brook
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="19">This side, I warn you, will not always brook</l>
<l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="20">Rain-water and cold stones.</l>

edition: John Conington; George Bell and Sons, London 1882

lines.text: Come, Mercury, by whose minstrel spell
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="1">Come, Mercury, by whose minstrel spell</l>
<l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="2">Amphion raised the Theban stones,</l>

lines.text: Come, with thy seven sweet strings, my shell,
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="3">Come, with thy seven sweet strings, my shell,</l>
<l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="4">Thy “diverse tones,”</l>

lines.text: Nor vocal once nor pleasant, now
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="5">Nor vocal once nor pleasant, now</l>

lines.text: To rich man's board and temple dear:
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="6">To rich man's board and temple dear:</l>

lines.text: Put forth thy power, till Lyde bow
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="7">Put forth thy power, till Lyde bow</l>
<l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="8">Her stubborn ear.</l>

lines.text: She, like a three-year colt unbroke,
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="9">She, like a three-year colt unbroke,</l>

lines.text: Is frisking o'er the spacious plain,
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="10">Is frisking o'er the spacious plain,</l>

lines.text: Too shy to bear a lover's yoke,
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="11">Too shy to bear a lover's yoke,</l>
<l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="12">A husband's rein.</l>

lines.text: The wood, the tiger, at thy call
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="13">The wood, the tiger, at thy call</l>

lines.text: Have follow'd: thou caust rivers stay:
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="14">Have follow'd: thou caust rivers stay:</l>

lines.text: The monstrous guard of Pluto's hall
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="15">The monstrous guard of Pluto's hall</l>
<l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="16">To thee gave way,</l>

lines.text: Grim Cerberus, round whose Gorgon head
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="17">Grim Cerberus, round whose Gorgon head</l>

lines.text: A hundred snakes are hissing death,
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="18">A hundred snakes are hissing death,</l>

lines.text: Whose triple jaws black venom shed,
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="19">Whose triple jaws black venom shed,</l>
<l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="20">And sickening breath.</l>
<l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="21">Ixion too and Tityos smooth'd</l>

lines.text: Their rugged brows: the urn stood dry
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="22">Their rugged brows: the urn stood dry</l>

lines.text: One hour, while Danaus' maids were sooth'd
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="23">One hour, while Danaus' maids were sooth'd</l>
<l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="24">With minstrelsy.</l>

lines.text: Let Lyde hear those maidens' guilt,
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="25">Let Lyde hear those maidens' guilt,</l>

lines.text: Their famous doom, the ceaseless drain
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="26">Their famous doom, the ceaseless drain</l>
<l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="27">Of outpour'd water, ever spilt,</l>
<l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="28">And all the pain</l>

lines.text: Reserved for sinners, e'en when dead:
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="29">Reserved for sinners, e'en when dead:</l>

lines.text: Those impious hands, (could crime do more?)
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="30">Those impious hands, (could crime do more?)</l>

lines.text: Those impious hands had hearts to shed
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="31">Those impious hands had hearts to shed</l>
<l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="32">Their bridegrooms' gore!</l>

lines.text: One only, true to Hymen's flame,
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="33">One only, true to Hymen's flame,</l>

lines.text: Was traitress to her sire forsworn:
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="34">Was traitress to her sire forsworn:</l>

lines.text: That splendid falsehood lights her name
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="35">That splendid falsehood lights her name</l>
<l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="36">Through times unborn.</l>

lines.text: “Wake!” to her youthful spouse she cried,
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="37">“Wake!” to her youthful spouse she cried,</l>

lines.text: “Wake! or you yet may sleep too well:
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="38">“Wake! or you yet may sleep too well:</l>

lines.text: Fly—from the father of your bride,
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="39">Fly—from the father of your bride,</l>
<l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="40">Her sisters fell:</l>
<l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="41">They, as she-lions bullocks rend,</l>

lines.text: Tear each her victim: I, less hard
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="42">Tear each her victim: I, less hard</l>

lines.text: Than these, will slay you not, poor friend,
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="43">Than these, will slay you not, poor friend,</l>
<l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="44">Nor hold in ward:</l>

lines.text: Me let my sire in fetters lay
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="45">Me let my sire in fetters lay</l>

lines.text: For mercy to my husband shown:
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="46">For mercy to my husband shown:</l>

lines.text: Me let him ship far hence away,
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="47">Me let him ship far hence away,</l>
<l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="48">To climes unknown.</l>

lines.text: Go; speed your flight o'er land and wave,
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="49">Go; speed your flight o'er land and wave,</l>

lines.text: While Night and Venus shield you; go
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="50">While Night and Venus shield you; go</l>

lines.text: Be blest: and on my tomb engrave
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="51">Be blest: and on my tomb engrave</l>
<l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="52">This tale of woe.”</l>

edition: John Conington; George Bell and Sons, London 1882

lines.text: How unhappy are the maidens who with Cupid may not play,
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="1">How unhappy are the maidens who with Cupid may not play,</l>

lines.text: Who may never touch the wine-cup, but must tremble all the day
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="2">Who may never touch the wine-cup, but must tremble all the day</l>

lines.text: At an uncle, and the scourging of his tongue!
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="3">At an uncle, and the scourging of his tongue!</l>

lines.text: Neobule, there's a robber takes your needle and your thread,
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="4">Neobule, there's a robber takes your needle and your thread,</l>

lines.text: Lets the lessons of Minerva run no longer in your head;
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="5">Lets the lessons of Minerva run no longer in your head;</l>

lines.text: It is Hebrus, the athletic and the young!
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="6">It is <placeName key="tgn,7002660">Hebrus</placeName>, the athletic and the young!</l>

lines.text: O, to see him when anointed he is plunging in the flood!
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="7">O, to see him when anointed he is plunging in the flood!</l>

lines.text: What a seat he has on horseback! was Bellerophon's as good?
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="8">What a seat he has on horseback! was Bellerophon's as good?</l>

lines.text: As a boxer, as a runner, past compare!
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="9">As a boxer, as a runner, past compare!</l>

lines.text: When the deer are flying blindly all the open country o'er,
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="10">When the deer are flying blindly all the open country o'er,</l>

lines.text: He can aim and he can hit them; he can steal upon the boar,
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="11">He can aim and he can hit them; he can steal upon the boar,</l>

lines.text: As it couches in the thicket unaware.
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="12">As it couches in the thicket unaware.</l>

edition: John Conington; George Bell and Sons, London 1882

lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="1">Bandusia's fount, in clearness crystalline,</l>

lines.text: O worthy of the wine, the flowers we vow!
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="2">O worthy of the wine, the flowers we vow!</l>
<l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="3">Tomorrow shall be thine</l>
<l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="4">A kid, whose crescent brow</l>

lines.text: Is sprouting all for love and victory.
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="5">Is sprouting all for love and victory.</l>

lines.text: In vain: his warm red blood, so early stirr'd.
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="6">In vain: his warm red blood, so early stirr'd.</l>
<l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="7">Thy gelid stream shall dye,</l>
<l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="8">Child of the wanton herd.</l>

lines.text: Thee the fierce Sirian star, to madness fired,
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="9">Thee the fierce Sirian star, to madness fired,</l>

lines.text: Forbears to touch: sweet cool thy waters yield
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="10">Forbears to touch: sweet cool thy waters yield</l>
<l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="11">To ox with ploughing tired,</l>
<l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="12">And lazy sheep afield.</l>

lines.text: Thou too one day shalt win proud eminence
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="13">Thou too one day shalt win proud eminence</l>

lines.text: 'Mid honour'd founts, while I the ilex sing
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="14">'Mid honour'd founts, while I the ilex sing</l>
<l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="15">Crowning the cavern, whence</l>
<l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="16">Thy babbling wavelets spring.</l>

edition: John Conington; George Bell and Sons, London 1882

lines.text: Our Hercules, they told us, Rome,
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="1">Our Hercules, they told us, <placeName key="perseus,Rome">Rome</placeName>,</l>

lines.text: Had sought the laurel Death bestows:
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="2">Had sought the laurel Death bestows:</l>

lines.text: Now Glory brings him conqueror home
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="3">Now Glory brings him conqueror home</l>
<l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="4">From Spaniard foes.</l>

lines.text: Proud of her spouse, the imperial fair
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="5">Proud of her spouse, the imperial fair</l>

lines.text: Must thank the gods that shield from death;
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="6">Must thank the gods that shield from death;</l>
<l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="7">His sister too:—let matrons wear</l>
<l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="8">The suppliant wreath</l>

lines.text: For daughters and for sons restored:
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="9">For daughters and for sons restored:</l>

lines.text: Ye youths and damsels newly wed,
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="10">Ye youths and damsels newly wed,</l>

lines.text: Let decent awe restrain each word
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="11">Let decent awe restrain each word</l>
<l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="12">Best left unsaid.</l>

lines.text: This day, true holyday to me,
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="13">This day, true holyday to me,</l>

lines.text: Shall banish care: I will not fear
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="14">Shall banish care: I will not fear</l>

lines.text: Rude broils or bloody death to see,
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="15">Rude broils or bloody death to see,</l>
<l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="16">While Caesar's here.</l>

lines.text: Quick, boy, the chaplets and the nard,
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="17">Quick, boy, the chaplets and the nard,</l>

lines.text: And wine, that knew the Marsian war,
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="18">And wine, that knew the Marsian war,</l>
<l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="19">If roving Spartacus have spared</l>
<l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="20">A single jar.</l>

lines.text: And bid Neaera come and trill,
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="21">And bid Neaera come and trill,</l>

lines.text: Her bright locks bound with careless art:
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="22">Her bright locks bound with careless art:</l>

lines.text: If her rough porter cross your will,
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="23">If her rough porter cross your will,</l>
<l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="24">Why then depart.</l>

lines.text: Soon palls the taste for noise and fray,
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="25">Soon palls the taste for noise and fray,</l>

lines.text: When hair is white and leaves are sere:
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="26">When hair is white and leaves are sere:</l>

lines.text: How had I fired in life's warm May,
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="27">How had I fired in life's warm May,</l>
<l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="28">In Plancus' year!</l>

edition: John Conington; George Bell and Sons, London 1882

lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="1">Wife of Ibycus the poor,</l>

lines.text: Let aged scandals have at length their bound:
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="2">Let aged scandals have at length their bound:</l>
<l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="3">Give your graceless doings o'er,</l>

lines.text: Ripe as you are for going underground.
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="4">Ripe as you are for going underground.</l>

lines.text: You the maidens' dance to lead,
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="5">You the maidens' dance to lead,</l>

lines.text: And cast your gloom upon those beaming stars!
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="6">And cast your gloom upon those beaming stars!</l>
<l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="7">Daughter Pholoe may succeed,</l>

lines.text: But mother Chloris what she touches mars.
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="8">But mother Chloris what she touches mars.</l>

lines.text: Young men's homes your daughter storms,
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="9">Young men's homes your daughter storms,</l>

lines.text: Like Thyiad, madden'd by the cymbals' beat:
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="10">Like Thyiad, madden'd by the cymbals' beat:</l>
<l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="11">Nothus' love her bosom warms:</l>

lines.text: She gambols like a fawn with silver feet.
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="12">She gambols like a fawn with silver feet.</l>

lines.text: Yours should be the wool that grows
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="13">Yours should be the wool that grows</l>

lines.text: By fair Luceria, not the merry lute:
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="14">By fair Luceria, not the merry lute:</l>
<l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="15">Flowers beseem not wither'd brows,.</l>

lines.text: Nor wither'd lips with emptied wine-jars suit.
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="16">Nor wither'd lips with emptied wine-jars suit.</l>

edition: John Conington; George Bell and Sons, London 1882

lines.text: Full well had Danae been secured, in truth,
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="1">Full well had Danae been secured, in truth,</l>

lines.text: By oaken portals, and a brazen tower,
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="2">By oaken portals, and a brazen tower,</l>

lines.text: And savage watch-dogs, from the roving youth
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="3">And savage watch-dogs, from the roving youth</l>
<l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="4">That prowl at midnight's hour:</l>

lines.text: But Jove and Venus mock'd with gay disdain
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="5">But Jove and Venus mock'd with gay disdain</l>

lines.text: The jealous warder of that close stronghold:
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="6">The jealous warder of that close stronghold:</l>

lines.text: The way, they knew, must soon be smooth and plain
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="7">The way, they knew, must soon be smooth and plain</l>

lines.text: When gods could change to gold.
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="8">When gods could change to gold.</l>

lines.text: Gold, gold can pass the tyrant's sentinel,
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="9">Gold, gold can pass the tyrant's sentinel,</l>

lines.text: Can shiver rocks with more resistless blow
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="10">Can shiver rocks with more resistless blow</l>

lines.text: Than is the thunder's. Argos' prophet fell,
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="11">Than is the thunder's.  <placeName key="perseus,Argos">Argos</placeName>' prophet fell,</l>

lines.text: He and his house laid low,
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="12">He and his house laid low,</l>

lines.text: And all for gain. The man of Macedon
lines.xml:
<l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="13">And all for gain.  The man of <placeName key="tgn,7002715">Macedon</placeName>
                     </l>

lines.text: Cleft gates of cities, rival kings o'erthrew
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="14">Cleft gates of cities, rival kings o'erthrew</l>

lines.text: By force of gifts: their cunning snares have won
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="15">By force of gifts: their cunning snares have won</l>
<l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="16">Rude captains and their crew.</l>

lines.text: As riches grow, care follows: men repine
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="17">As riches grow, care follows: men repine</l>

lines.text: And thirst for more. No lofty crest I raise:
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="18">And thirst for more.  No lofty crest I raise:</l>

lines.text: Wisdom that thought forbids, Maecenas mine,
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="19">Wisdom that thought forbids, Maecenas mine,</l>
<l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="20">The knightly order's praise.</l>

lines.text: He that denies himself shall gain the more
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="21">He that denies himself shall gain the more</l>

lines.text: From bounteous Heaven. I strip me of my pride,
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="22">From bounteous Heaven. I strip me of my pride,</l>

lines.text: Desert the rich man's standard, and pass o'er
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="23">Desert the rich man's standard, and pass o'er</l>
<l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="24">To bare Contentment's side,</l>

lines.text: More proud as lord of what the great despise
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="25">More proud as lord of what the great despise</l>

lines.text: Than if the wheat thresh'd on Apulia's floor
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="26">Than if the wheat thresh'd on <placeName key="tgn,7010380">Apulia</placeName>'s floor</l>

lines.text: I hoarded all in my huge granaries,
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="27">I hoarded all in my huge granaries,</l>
<l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="28">'Mid vast possessions poor.</l>

lines.text: A clear fresh stream, a little field o'ergrown
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="29">A clear fresh stream, a little field o'ergrown</l>

lines.text: With shady trees, a crop that ne'er deceives,
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="30">With shady trees, a crop that ne'er deceives,</l>

lines.text: Pass, though men know it not, their wealth, that own
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="31">Pass, though men know it not, their wealth, that own</l>
<l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="32">All Afric's golden sheaves.</l>

lines.text: Though no Calabrian bees their honey yield
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="33">Though no Calabrian bees their honey yield</l>

lines.text: For me, nor mellowing sleeps the god of wine
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="34">For me, nor mellowing sleeps the god of wine</l>

lines.text: In Formian jar, nor in Gaul's pasture-field
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="35">In Formian jar, nor in <placeName key="tgn,1000070">Gaul</placeName>'s pasture-field</l>

lines.text: The wool grows long and fine,
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="36">The wool grows long and fine,</l>

lines.text: Yet Poverty ne'er comes to break my peace;
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="37">Yet Poverty ne'er comes to break my peace;</l>

lines.text: If more I craved, you would not more refuse.
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="38">If more I craved, you would not more refuse.</l>

lines.text: Desiring less, I better shall increase
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="39">Desiring less, I better shall increase</l>
<l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="40">My tiny revenues,</l>

lines.text: Than if to Alyattes' wide domains
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="41">Than if to Alyattes' wide domains</l>

lines.text: I join'd the realms of Mygdon. Great desires
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="42">I join'd the realms of Mygdon.  Great desires</l>

lines.text: Sort with great wants. 'Tis best, when prayer obtains
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="43">Sort with great wants. 'Tis best, when prayer obtains</l>
<l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="44">No more than life requires.</l>

edition: John Conington; George Bell and Sons, London 1882

lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="1">Aelius, of Lamus' ancient name</l>
<l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="2">(For since from that high parentage</l>
<l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="3">The prehistoric Lamias came</l>

lines.text: And all who fill the storied page,
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="4">And all who fill the storied page,</l>

lines.text: No doubt you trace your line from him,
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="5">No doubt you trace your line from him,</l>

lines.text: Who stretch'd his sway o'er Formiae,
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="6">Who stretch'd his sway o'er <placeName key="perseus,Formiae">Formiae</placeName>,</l>

lines.text: And Liris, whose still waters swim
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="7">And Liris, whose still waters swim</l>

lines.text: Whore green Marica skirts the sea,
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="8">Whore green <placeName key="tgn,7002660">Marica</placeName> skirts the sea,</l>

lines.text: Lord of broad realms), an eastern gale
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="9">Lord of broad realms), an eastern gale</l>
<l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="10">Will blow to-morrow, and bestrew</l>

lines.text: The shore with weeds, with leaves the vale,
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="11">The shore with weeds, with leaves the vale,</l>

lines.text: If rain's old prophet tell me true,
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="12">If rain's old prophet tell me true,</l>
<l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="13">The raven.  Gather, while 'tis fine,</l>

lines.text: Your wood; tomorrow shall be gay
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="14">Your wood; tomorrow shall be gay</l>

lines.text: With smoking pig and streaming wine,
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="15">With smoking pig and streaming wine,</l>

lines.text: And lord and slave keep holyday.
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="16">And lord and slave keep holyday.</l>

edition: John Conington; George Bell and Sons, London 1882

lines.text: O wont the flying Nymphs to woo,
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="1">O wont the flying Nymphs to woo,</l>

lines.text: Good Faunus, through my sunny farm
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="2">Good Faunus, through my sunny farm</l>

lines.text: Pass gently, gently pass, nor do
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="3">Pass gently, gently pass, nor do</l>
<l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="4">My younglings harm.</l>

lines.text: Each year, thou know'st, a kid must die
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="5">Each year, thou know'st, a kid must die</l>

lines.text: For thee; nor lacks the wine's full stream
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="6">For thee; nor lacks the wine's full stream</l>

lines.text: To Venus' mate, the bowl; and high
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="7">To Venus' mate, the bowl; and high</l>
<l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="8">The altars steam.</l>
<l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="9">Sure as December's Nones appear,</l>

lines.text: All o'er the grass the cattle play;
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="10">All o'er the grass the cattle play;</l>

lines.text: The village, with the lazy steer,
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="11">The village, with the lazy steer,</l>
<l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="12">Keeps holyday.</l>

lines.text: Wolves rove among the fearless sheep;
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="13">Wolves rove among the fearless sheep;</l>

lines.text: The woods for thee their foliage strow;
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="14">The woods for thee their foliage strow;</l>

lines.text: The delver loves on earth to leap,
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="15">The delver loves on earth to leap,</l>
<l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="16">His ancient foe.</l>

edition: John Conington; George Bell and Sons, London 1882

lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="1">What the time from Inachus</l>

lines.text: To Codrus, who in patriot battle fell,
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="2">To Codrus, who in patriot battle fell,</l>
<l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="3">Who were sprung from Aeacus,</l>

lines.text: And how men fought at Ilion,—this you tell.
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="4">And how men fought at <placeName key="tgn,7002329">Ilion</placeName>,—this you tell.</l>

lines.text: What the wines of Chios cost,
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="5">What the wines of <placeName key="tgn,7002670">Chios</placeName> cost,</l>

lines.text: Who with due heat our water can allay,
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="6">Who with due heat our water can allay,</l>

lines.text: What the hour, and who the host
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="7">What the hour, and who the host</l>

lines.text: To give us house-room,—this you will not say
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="8">To give us house-room,—this you will not say</l>

lines.text: Ho, there! wine to moonrise, wine
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="9">Ho, there! wine to moonrise, wine</l>

lines.text: To midnight, wine to our new augur too!
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="10">To midnight, wine to our new augur too!</l>

lines.text: Nine to three or three to nine,
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="11">Nine to three or three to nine,</l>

lines.text: As each man pleases, makes proportion true.
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="12">As each man pleases, makes proportion true.</l>
<l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="13">Who the uneven Muses loves,</l>

lines.text: Will fire his dizzy brain with three times three;
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="14">Will fire his dizzy brain with three times three;</l>

lines.text: Three once told the Grace approves;
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="15">Three once told the Grace approves;</l>

lines.text: She with her two bright sisters, gay and free,
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="16">She with her two bright sisters, gay and free,</l>

lines.text: Shrinks, as maiden should, from strife:
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="17">Shrinks, as maiden should, from strife:</l>

lines.text: But I'm for madness. What has dull'd the fire
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="18">But I'm for madness.  What has dull'd the fire</l>
<l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="19">Of the Berecyntian fife?</l>

lines.text: Why hangs the flute in silence with the lyre?
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="20">Why hangs the flute in silence with the lyre?</l>
<l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="21">Out on niggard-handed boys!</l>

lines.text: Rain showers of roses; let old Lycus hear,
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="22">Rain showers of roses; let old Lycus hear,</l>
<l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="23">Envious churl, our senseless noise,</l>

lines.text: And she, our neighbour, his ill-sorted fere.
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="24">And she, our neighbour, his ill-sorted fere.</l>

lines.text: You with your bright clustering hair,
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="25">You with your bright clustering hair,</l>

lines.text: Your beauty, Telephus, like evening's sky,
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="26">Your beauty, Telephus, like evening's sky,</l>

lines.text: Rhoda loves, as young, as fair;
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="27">Rhoda loves, as young, as fair;</l>

lines.text: I for my Glycera slowly, slowly die.
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="28">I for my Glycera slowly, slowly die.</l>

edition: John Conington; George Bell and Sons, London 1882

lines.text: O born in Manlius' year with me,
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="1">O born in Manlius' year with me,</l>

lines.text: Whate'er you bring us, plaint or jest,
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="2">Whate'er you bring us, plaint or jest,</l>
<l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="3">Or passion and wild revelry,</l>

lines.text: Or, like a gentle wine-jar, rest;
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="4">Or, like a gentle wine-jar, rest;</l>

lines.text: Howe'er men call your Massic juice,
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="5">Howe'er men call your Massic juice,</l>

lines.text: Its broaching claims a festal day;
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="6">Its broaching claims a festal day;</l>
<l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="7">Come then; Corvinus bids produce</l>

lines.text: A mellower wine, and I obey.
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="8">A mellower wine, and I obey.</l>

lines.text: Though steep'd in all Socratic lore
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="9">Though steep'd in all Socratic lore</l>

lines.text: He will not slight you; do not fear.
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="10">He will not slight you; do not fear.</l>

lines.text: They say old Cato o'er and o'er
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="11">They say old Cato o'er and o'er</l>

lines.text: With wine his honest heart would cheer.
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="12">With wine his honest heart would cheer.</l>

lines.text: Tough wits to your mild torture yield
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="13">Tough wits to your mild torture yield</l>

lines.text: Their treasures; you unlock the soul
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="14">Their treasures; you unlock the soul</l>

lines.text: Of wisdom and its stores conceal'd,
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="15">Of wisdom and its stores conceal'd,</l>
<l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="16">Arm'd with Lyaeus' kind control.</l>

lines.text: 'Tis yours the drooping heart to heal;
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="17">'Tis yours the drooping heart to heal;</l>

lines.text: Your strength uplifts the poor man's horn;
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="18">Your strength uplifts the poor man's horn;</l>

lines.text: Inspired by you, the soldier's steel,
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="19">Inspired by you, the soldier's steel,</l>

lines.text: The monarch's crown, he laughs to scorn,
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="20">The monarch's crown, he laughs to scorn,</l>

lines.text: Liber and Venus, wills she so,
lines.xml:
<l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="21">
                        <placeName key="tgn,2032614">Liber</placeName> and <placeName key="tgn,2108237">Venus</placeName>, wills she so,</l>
<l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="22">And sister Graces, ne'er unknit,</l>

lines.text: And living lamps shall see you flow
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="23">And living lamps shall see you flow</l>

lines.text: Till stars before the sunrise flit.
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="24">Till stars before the sunrise flit.</l>

edition: John Conington; George Bell and Sons, London 1882

lines.text: Guardian of hill and woodland, Maid,
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="1">Guardian of hill and woodland, Maid,</l>

lines.text: Who to young wives in childbirth's hour
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="2">Who to young wives in childbirth's hour</l>
<l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="3">Thrice call'd, vouchsafest sovereign aid,</l>
<l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="4">O three-form'd power!</l>

lines.text: This pine that shades my cot be thine;
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="5">This pine that shades my cot be thine;</l>

lines.text: Here will I slay, as years come round,
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="6">Here will I slay, as years come round,</l>

lines.text: A youngling boar, whose tusks design
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="7">A youngling boar, whose tusks design</l>
<l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="8">The side-long wound.</l>

edition: John Conington; George Bell and Sons, London 1882

lines.text: If, Phidyle, your hands you lift
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="1">If, Phidyle, your hands you lift</l>

lines.text: To heaven, as each new moon is born,
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="2">To heaven, as each new moon is born,</l>

lines.text: Soothing your Lares with the gift
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="3">Soothing your <placeName key="tgn,1018972">Lares</placeName> with the gift</l>

lines.text: Of slaughter'd swine, and spice, and corn,
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="4">Of slaughter'd swine, and spice, and corn,</l>
<l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="5">Ne'er shall Scirocco's bane assail</l>

lines.text: Your vines, nor mildew blast your wheat.
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="6">Your vines, nor mildew blast your wheat.</l>

lines.text: Ne'er shall your tender younglings fail
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="7">Ne'er shall your tender younglings fail</l>

lines.text: In autumn, when the fruits are sweet.
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="8">In autumn, when the fruits are sweet.</l>
<l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="9">The destined victim 'mid the snows</l>
<l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="10">Of Algidus in oakwoods fed,</l>

lines.text: Or where the Alban herbage grows,
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="11">Or where the <placeName key="tgn,2127955">Alban</placeName> herbage grows,</l>

lines.text: Shall dye the pontiff's axes red;
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="12">Shall dye the pontiff's axes red;</l>

lines.text: No need of butcher'd sheep for you
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="13">No need of butcher'd sheep for you</l>

lines.text: To make your homely prayers prevail;
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="14">To make your homely prayers prevail;</l>

lines.text: Give but your little gods their due,
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="15">Give but your little gods their due,</l>

lines.text: The rosemary twined with myrtle frail.
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="16">The rosemary twined with myrtle frail.</l>

lines.text: The sprinkled salt, the votive meal,
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="17">The sprinkled salt, the votive meal,</l>

lines.text: As soon their favour will regain,
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="18">As soon their favour will regain,</l>

lines.text: Let but the hand be pure and leal,
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="19">Let but the hand be pure and leal,</l>

lines.text: As all the pomp of heifers slain.
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="20">As all the pomp of heifers slain.</l>

edition: John Conington; George Bell and Sons, London 1882

lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="1">Though your buried wealth surpass</l>

lines.text: The unsunn'd gold of Ind or Araby,
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="2">The unsunn'd gold of Ind or Araby,</l>

lines.text: Though with many a ponderous mass
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="3">Though with many a ponderous mass</l>

lines.text: You crowd the Tuscan and Apulian sea,
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="4">You crowd the <placeName key="tgn,2072785">Tuscan</placeName> and Apulian sea,</l>
<l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="5">Let Necessity but drive</l>

lines.text: Her wedge of adamant into that proud head,
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="6">Her wedge of adamant into that proud head,</l>
<l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="7">Vainly battling will you strive</l>

lines.text: To 'scape Death's noose, or rid your soul of dread.
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="8">To 'scape Death's noose, or rid your soul of dread.</l>
<l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="9">Better life the Scythians lead,</l>

lines.text: Trailing on waggon wheels their wandering home,
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="10">Trailing on waggon wheels their wandering home,</l>
<l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="11">Or the hardy Getan breed,</l>

lines.text: As o'er their vast unmeasured steppes they roam;
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="12">As o'er their vast unmeasured steppes they roam;</l>

lines.text: Free the crops that bless their soil;
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="13">Free the crops that bless their soil;</l>

lines.text: Their tillage wearies after one year's space;
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="14">Their tillage wearies after one year's space;</l>

lines.text: Each in turn fulfils his toil;
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="15">Each in turn fulfils his toil;</l>

lines.text: His period o'er, another takes his place.
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="16">His period o'er, another takes his place.</l>

lines.text: There the step-dame keeps her hand
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="17">There the step-dame keeps her hand</l>

lines.text: From guilty plots, from blood of orphans clean;
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="18">From guilty plots, from blood of orphans clean;</l>
<l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="19">There no downed wives command</l>

lines.text: Their feeble lords, or on adulterers lean.
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="20">Their feeble lords, or on adulterers lean.</l>

lines.text: Theirs are dowries not of gold,
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="21">Theirs are dowries not of gold,</l>

lines.text: Their parents' worth, their own pure chastity,
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="22">Their parents' worth, their own pure chastity,</l>

lines.text: True to one, to others cold;
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="23">True to one, to others cold;</l>

lines.text: They dare not sin, or, if they dare, they die.
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="24">They dare not sin, or, if they dare, they die.</l>

lines.text: O, whoe'er has heart and head
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="25">O, whoe'er has heart and head</l>

lines.text: To stay our plague of blood, our civic brawls,
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="26">To stay our plague of blood, our civic brawls,</l>

lines.text: Would he that his name be read
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="27">Would he that his name be read</l>
<l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="28">“Father of <placeName key="tgn,7013962">Rome</placeName>” on lofty pedestals,</l>

lines.text: Let him chain this lawless will,
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="29">Let him chain this lawless will,</l>

lines.text: And be our children's hero! cursed spite!
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="30">And be our children's hero! cursed spite!</l>
<l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="31">Living worth we envy still,</l>

lines.text: Then seek it with strain'd eyes, when snatch'd from sight.
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="32">Then seek it with strain'd eyes, when snatch'd from sight.</l>
<l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="33">What can sad laments avail</l>

lines.text: Unless sharp justice kill the taint of sin?
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="34">Unless sharp justice kill the taint of sin?</l>

lines.text: What can laws, that needs must fail
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="35">What can laws, that needs must fail</l>

lines.text: Shorn of the aid of manners form'd within,
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="36">Shorn of the aid of manners form'd within,</l>

lines.text: If the merchant turns not back
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="37">If the merchant turns not back</l>

lines.text: From the fierce heats that round the tropic glow,
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="38">From the fierce heats that round the tropic glow,</l>

lines.text: Turns not from the regions black
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="39">Turns not from the regions black</l>

lines.text: With northern winds, and hard with frozen snow;
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="40">With northern winds, and hard with frozen snow;</l>
<l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="41">Sailors override the wave,</l>

lines.text: While guilty poverty, more fear'd than vice.
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="42">While guilty poverty, more fear'd than vice.</l>

lines.text: Bids us crime and suffering brave,
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="43">Bids us crime and suffering brave,</l>

lines.text: And shuns the ascent of virtue's precipice?
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="44">And shuns the ascent of virtue's precipice?</l>
<l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="45">Let the Capitolian fane,</l>

lines.text: The favour'd goal of yon vociferous crowd,
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="46">The favour'd goal of yon vociferous crowd,</l>

lines.text: Aye, or let the nearest main
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="47">Aye, or let the nearest main</l>

lines.text: Receive our gold, our jewels rich and proud:
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="48">Receive our gold, our jewels rich and proud:</l>

lines.text: Slay we thus the cause of crime,
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="49">Slay we thus the cause of crime,</l>

lines.text: If yet we would repent and choose the good:
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="50">If yet we would repent and choose the good:</l>

lines.text: Ours the task to take in time
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="51">Ours the task to take in time</l>

lines.text: This baleful lust, and crush it in the bud.
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="52">This baleful lust, and crush it in the bud.</l>

lines.text: Ours to mould our weakling sons
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="53">Ours to mould our weakling sons</l>

lines.text: To nobler sentiment and manlier deed:
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="54">To nobler sentiment and manlier deed:</l>
<l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="55">Now the noble's first-born shuns</l>

lines.text: The perilous chase, nor learns to sit his steed:
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="56">The perilous chase, nor learns to sit his steed:</l>

lines.text: Set him to the unlawful dice,
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="57">Set him to the unlawful dice,</l>

lines.text: Or Grecian hoop, how skilfully he plays!
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="58">Or Grecian hoop, how skilfully he plays!</l>

lines.text: While his sire, mature in vice,
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="59">While his sire, mature in vice,</l>

lines.text: A friend, a partner, or a guest betrays,
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="60">A friend, a partner, or a guest betrays,</l>

lines.text: Hurrying, for an heir so base,
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="61">Hurrying, for an heir so base,</l>

lines.text: To gather riches. Money, root of ill,
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="62">To gather riches.  Money, root of ill,</l>

lines.text: Doubt it not, still grows apace:
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="63">Doubt it not, still grows apace:</l>

lines.text: Yet the scant heap has somewhat lacking still.
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="64">Yet the scant heap has somewhat lacking still.</l>

edition: John Conington; George Bell and Sons, London 1882

lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="1">Whither, <placeName key="tgn,2097807">Bacchus</placeName>, tear'st thou me.</l>

lines.text: FiIl'd with thy strength? What dens, what forests these,
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="2">FiIl'd with thy strength? What dens, what forests these,</l>

lines.text: Thus in wildering race I see?
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="3">Thus in wildering race I see?</l>

lines.text: What cave shall hearken to my melodies,
