lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="4">What cave shall hearken to my melodies,</l>

lines.text: Tuned to tell of Caesar's praise
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="5">Tuned to tell of Caesar's praise</l>

lines.text: And throne him high the heavenly ranks among?
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="6">And throne him high the heavenly ranks among?</l>

lines.text: Sweet and strange shall be my lays,
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="7">Sweet and strange shall be my lays,</l>

lines.text: A tale till now by poet voice unsung.
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="8">A tale till now by poet voice unsung.</l>

lines.text: As the Evian on the height,
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="9">As the <placeName key="tgn,7009171">Evian</placeName> on the height,</l>

lines.text: Roused from her sleep, looks wonderingly abroad,
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="10">Roused from her sleep, looks wonderingly abroad,</l>

lines.text: Looks on Thrace with snow-drifts white,
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="11">Looks on <placeName key="tgn,7002756">Thrace</placeName> with snow-drifts white,</l>

lines.text: And Rhodope by barbarous footstep trod,
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="12">And Rhodope by barbarous footstep trod,</l>
<l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="13">So my truant eyes admire</l>

lines.text: The banks, the desolate forests. O great King
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="14">The banks, the desolate forests.  O great King</l>
<l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="15">Who the Naiads dost inspire,</l>

lines.text: And Bacchants, strong from earth huge trees to wring!
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="16">And Bacchants, strong from earth huge trees to wring!</l>

lines.text: Not a lowly strain is mine,
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="17">Not a lowly strain is mine,</l>

lines.text: No mere man's utterance. O, 'tis venture sweet
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="18">No mere man's utterance.  O, 'tis venture sweet</l>

lines.text: Thee to follow, God of wine,
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="19">Thee to follow, God of wine,</l>

lines.text: Making the vine-branch round thy temples meet!
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="20">Making the vine-branch round thy temples meet!</l>

edition: John Conington; George Bell and Sons, London 1882

lines.text: For ladies' love I late was fit,
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="1">For ladies' love I late was fit,</l>

lines.text: And good success my warfare blest,
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="2">And good success my warfare blest,</l>

lines.text: But now my arms, my lyre I quit,
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="3">But now my arms, my lyre I quit,</l>

lines.text: And hang them up to rust or rest.
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="4">And hang them up to rust or rest.</l>

lines.text: Here, where arising from the sea
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="5">Here, where arising from the sea</l>

lines.text: Stands Venus, lay the load at last,
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="6">Stands Venus, lay the load at last,</l>
<l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="7">Links, crowbars, and artillery,</l>

lines.text: Threatening all doors that dared be fast.
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="8">Threatening all doors that dared be fast.</l>

lines.text: O Goddess! Cyprus owns thy sway,
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="9">O Goddess! <placeName key="tgn,1000112">Cyprus</placeName> owns thy sway,</l>

lines.text: And Memphis, far from Thracian snow;
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="10">And <placeName key="tgn,7001186">Memphis</placeName>, far from Thracian snow;</l>

lines.text: Raise high thy lash, and deal me, pray,
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="11">Raise high thy lash, and deal me, pray,</l>

lines.text: That haughty Chloe just one blow!
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="12">That haughty Chloe just one blow!</l>

edition: John Conington; George Bell and Sons, London 1882

lines.text: When guilt goes forth, let lapwings shrill,
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="1">When guilt goes forth, let lapwings shrill,</l>

lines.text: And dogs and foxes great with young,
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="2">And dogs and foxes great with young,</l>

lines.text: And wolves from far Lanuvian hill,
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="3">And wolves from far Lanuvian hill,</l>
<l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="4">Give clamorous tongue:</l>

lines.text: Across the roadway dart the snake,
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="5">Across the roadway dart the snake,</l>

lines.text: Frightening, like arrow loosed from string,
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="6">Frightening, like arrow loosed from string,</l>

lines.text: The horses. I, for friendship's sake,
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="7">The horses.  I, for friendship's sake,</l>
<l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="8">Watching each wing,</l>

lines.text: Ere to his haunt, the stagnant marsh,
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="9">Ere to his haunt, the stagnant marsh,</l>
<l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="10">The harbinger of tempest flies,</l>

lines.text: Will call the raven, croaking harsh,
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="11">Will call the raven, croaking harsh,</l>
<l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="12">From eastern skies.</l>
<l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="13">Farewell!—and wheresoe'er you go,</l>
<l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="14">My Galatea, think of me:</l>

lines.text: Let lefthand pie and roving crow
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="15">Let lefthand pie and roving crow</l>
<l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="16">Still leave you free.</l>

lines.text: But mark with what a front of fear
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="17">But mark with what a front of fear</l>

lines.text: Orion lowers. Ah! well I know
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="18">Orion lowers.  Ah! well I know</l>

lines.text: How Hadria glooms, how falsely clear
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="19">How <placeName key="perseus,Hadria">Hadria</placeName> glooms, how falsely clear</l>
<l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="20">The west-winds blow.</l>

lines.text: Let foemen's wives and children feel
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="21">Let foemen's wives and children feel</l>
<l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="22">The gathering south-wind's angry roar,</l>

lines.text: The black wave's crash, the thunder-peal,
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="23">The black wave's crash, the thunder-peal,</l>
<l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="24">The quivering shore.</l>

lines.text: So to the bull Europa gave
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="25">So to the bull Europa gave</l>

lines.text: Her beauteous form, and when she saw
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="26">Her beauteous form, and when she saw</l>

lines.text: The monstrous deep, the yawning grave,
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="27">The monstrous deep, the yawning grave,</l>
<l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="28">Grew pale with awe.</l>

lines.text: That morn of meadow-flowers she thought,
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="29">That morn of meadow-flowers she thought,</l>

lines.text: Weaving a crown the nymphs to please:
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="30">Weaving a crown the nymphs to please:</l>

lines.text: That gloomy night she look'd on nought
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="31">That gloomy night she look'd on nought</l>
<l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="32">But stars and seas.</l>

<l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="33">Then, as in hundred-citied <placeName key="tgn,7012056">Crete</placeName>
                     </l>

lines.text: She landed,—“O my sire!” she said,
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="34">She landed,—“O my sire!” she said,</l>
<l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="35">“O childly duty! passion's heat</l>
<l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="36">Has struck thee dead.</l>

lines.text: Whence came I? death, for maiden's shame,
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="37">Whence came I? death, for maiden's shame,</l>

lines.text: Were little. Do I wake to weep
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="38">Were little.  Do I wake to weep</l>

lines.text: My sin? or am I pure of blame,
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="39">My sin? or am I pure of blame,</l>
<l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="40">And is it sleep</l>

lines.text: From dreamland brings a form to trick
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="41">From dreamland brings a form to trick</l>

lines.text: My senses? Which was best? to go
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="42">My senses? Which was best? to go</l>

lines.text: Over the long, long waves, or pick
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="43">Over the long, long waves, or pick</l>
<l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="44">The flowers in blow?</l>

lines.text: O, were that monster made my prize,
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="45">O, were that monster made my prize,</l>

lines.text: How would I strive to wound that brow,
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="46">How would I strive to wound that brow,</l>

lines.text: How tear those horns, my frantic eyes
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="47">How tear those horns, my frantic eyes</l>
<l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="48">Adored but now!</l>

lines.text: Shameless I left my father's home;
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="49">Shameless I left my father's home;</l>

lines.text: Shameless I cheat the expectant grave;
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="50">Shameless I cheat the expectant grave;</l>

lines.text: O heaven, that naked I might roam
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="51">O heaven, that naked I might roam</l>
<l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="52">In lions' cave!</l>

lines.text: Now, ere decay my bloom devour
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="53">Now, ere decay my bloom devour</l>

lines.text: Or thin the richness of my blood,
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="54">Or thin the richness of my blood,</l>

lines.text: Fain would I fall in youth's first flower,
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="55">Fain would I fall in youth's first flower,</l>
<l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="56">The tigers' food.</l>
<l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="57">Hark! 'tis my father—‘Worthless one!</l>

lines.text: What, yet alive? the oak is nigh.
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="58">What, yet alive? the oak is nigh.</l>

lines.text: 'Twas well you kept your maiden zone,
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="59">'Twas well you kept your maiden zone,</l>
<l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="60">The noose to tie.</l>

lines.text: Or if your choice be that rude pike,
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="61">Or if your choice be that rude pike,</l>

lines.text: New barb'd with death, leap down and ask
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="62">New barb'd with death, leap down and ask</l>

lines.text: The wind to bear you. Would you like
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="63">The wind to bear you.  Would you like</l>
<l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="64">The bondmaid's task,</l>

lines.text: You, child of kings, a master's toy,
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="65">You, child of kings, a master's toy,</l>

lines.text: A mistress' slave?’” Beside her, lo!
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="66">A mistress' slave?’” Beside her, lo!</l>

lines.text: Stood Venus smiling, and her boy
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="67">Stood Venus smiling, and her boy</l>
<l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="68">With unstrung bow.</l>

lines.text: Then, when her laughter ceased, “Have done
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="69">Then, when her laughter ceased, “Have done</l>

lines.text: With fume and fret,” she cried, “my fair;
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="70">With fume and fret,” she cried, “my fair;</l>

lines.text: That odious bull will give you soon
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="71">That odious bull will give you soon</l>
<l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="72">His horns to tear.</l>

lines.text: You know not you are Jove's own dame:
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="73">You know not you are Jove's own dame:</l>
<l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="74">Away with sobbing; be resign'd</l>

lines.text: To greatness: you shall give your name
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="75">To greatness: you shall give your name</l>
<l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="76">To half mankind.”</l>

edition: John Conington; George Bell and Sons, London 1882

lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="1">Neptune's feast-day! what should man</l>

lines.text: Think first of doing? Lyde mine, be bold,
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="2">Think first of doing? Lyde mine, be bold,</l>
<l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="3">Broach the treasured Caecuban,</l>

lines.text: And batter Wisdom in her own stronghold.
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="4">And batter Wisdom in her own stronghold.</l>

lines.text: Now the noon has pass'd the full,
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="5">Now the noon has pass'd the full,</l>

lines.text: Yet sure you deem swift Time has made a halt,
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="6">Yet sure you deem swift Time has made a halt,</l>

lines.text: Tardy as you are to pull
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="7">Tardy as you are to pull</l>

lines.text: Old Bibulus' wine-jar from its sleepy vault.
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="8">Old Bibulus' wine-jar from its sleepy vault.</l>

lines.text: I will take my turn and sing
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="9">I will take my turn and sing</l>

lines.text: Neptune and Nereus' train with locks of green;
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="10">Neptune and Nereus' train with locks of green;</l>

lines.text: You shall warble to the string
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="11">You shall warble to the string</l>

lines.text: Latona and her Cynthia's arrowy sheen.
lines.xml:
<l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="12">
                        <placeName key="tgn,2013536">Latona</placeName> and her <placeName key="tgn,2056258">Cynthia</placeName>'s arrowy sheen.</l>

lines.text: Hers our latest song, who sways
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="13">Hers our latest song, who sways</l>

lines.text: Cnidos and Cyclads, and to Paphos goes
lines.xml:
<l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="14">
                        <placeName key="tgn,5003757">Cnidos</placeName> and Cyclads, and to <placeName key="tgn,7002373">Paphos</placeName> goes</l>
<l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="15">With her swans, on holydays;</l>

lines.text: Night too shall claim the homage music owes.
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="16">Night too shall claim the homage music owes.</l>

edition: John Conington; George Bell and Sons, London 1882

lines.text: Heir of Tyrrhenian kings, for you
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="1">Heir of Tyrrhenian kings, for you</l>

lines.text: A mellow cask, unbroach'd as yet,
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="2">A mellow cask, unbroach'd as yet,</l>
<l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="3">Maecenas mine, and roses new,</l>

lines.text: And fresh-drawn oil your locks to wet,
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="4">And fresh-drawn oil your locks to wet,</l>

lines.text: Are waiting here. Delay not still,
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="5">Are waiting here.  Delay not still,</l>

lines.text: Nor gaze on Tibur, never dried,
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="6">Nor gaze on <placeName key="perseus,Tibur">Tibur</placeName>, never dried,</l>

lines.text: And sloping Aesule, and the hill
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="7">And sloping Aesule, and the hill</l>
<l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="8">Of Telegon the parricide.</l>

lines.text: O leave that pomp that can but tire,
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="9">O leave that pomp that can but tire,</l>

lines.text: Those piles, among the clouds at home;
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="10">Those piles, among the clouds at home;</l>

lines.text: Cease for a moment to admire
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="11">Cease for a moment to admire</l>

lines.text: The smoke, the wealth, the noise of Rome!
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="12">The smoke, the wealth, the noise of <placeName key="perseus,Rome">Rome</placeName>!</l>

lines.text: In change e'en luxury finds a zest:
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="13">In change e'en luxury finds a zest:</l>

lines.text: The poor man's supper, neat, but spare,
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="14">The poor man's supper, neat, but spare,</l>

lines.text: With no gay couch to seat the guest,
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="15">With no gay couch to seat the guest,</l>

lines.text: Has smooth'd the rugged brow of care.
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="16">Has smooth'd the rugged brow of care.</l>

lines.text: Now glows the Ethiop maiden's sire;
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="17">Now glows the Ethiop maiden's sire;</l>
<l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="18">Now Procyon rages all ablaze;</l>

lines.text: The Lion maddens in his ire,
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="19">The Lion maddens in his ire,</l>

lines.text: As suns bring back the sultry days:
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="20">As suns bring back the sultry days:</l>

lines.text: The shepherd with his weary sheep
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="21">The shepherd with his weary sheep</l>

lines.text: Seeks out the streamlet and the trees,
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="22">Seeks out the streamlet and the trees,</l>

lines.text: Silvanus' lair: the still banks sleep
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="23">Silvanus' lair: the still banks sleep</l>
<l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="24">Untroubled by the wandering breeze.</l>
<l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="25">You ponder on imperial schemes,</l>

lines.text: And o'er the city's danger brood:
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="26">And o'er the city's danger brood:</l>

lines.text: Bactrian and Serian haunt your dreams,
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="27">Bactrian and Serian haunt your dreams,</l>

lines.text: And Tanais, toss'd by inward feud.
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="28">And <placeName key="tgn,1123466">Tanais</placeName>, toss'd by inward feud.</l>

lines.text: The issue of the time to be
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="29">The issue of the time to be</l>

lines.text: Heaven wisely hides in blackest night,
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="30">Heaven wisely hides in blackest night,</l>
<l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="31">And laughs, should man's anxiety</l>

lines.text: Transgress the bounds of man's short sight.
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="32">Transgress the bounds of man's short sight.</l>
<l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="33">Control the present: all beside</l>

lines.text: Flows like a river seaward borne,
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="34">Flows like a river seaward borne,</l>

lines.text: Now rolling on its placid tide,
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="35">Now rolling on its placid tide,</l>
<l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="36">Now whirling massy trunks uptorn,</l>

lines.text: And waveworn crags, and farms, and stock,
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="37">And waveworn crags, and farms, and stock,</l>

lines.text: In chaos blent, while hill and wood
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="38">In chaos blent, while hill and wood</l>
<l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="39">Reverberate to the enormous shock,</l>

lines.text: When savage rains the tranquil flood
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="40">When savage rains the tranquil flood</l>

lines.text: Have stirr'd to madness. Happy he,
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="41">Have stirr'd to madness.  Happy he,</l>

lines.text: Self-centred, who each night can say,
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="42">Self-centred, who each night can say,</l>

lines.text: “My life is lived: the morn may see
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="43">“My life is lived: the morn may see</l>

lines.text: A clouded or a sunny day:
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="44">A clouded or a sunny day:</l>

lines.text: That rests with Jove: but what is gone,
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="45">That rests with Jove: but what is gone,</l>

lines.text: He will not, cannot turn to nought;
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="46">He will not, cannot turn to nought;</l>

lines.text: Nor cancel, as a thing undone,
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="47">Nor cancel, as a thing undone,</l>

lines.text: What once the flying hour has brought.”
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="48">What once the flying hour has brought.”</l>

lines.text: Fortune, who loves her cruel game,
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="49">Fortune, who loves her cruel game,</l>

lines.text: Still bent upon some heartless whim,
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="50">Still bent upon some heartless whim,</l>
<l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="51">Shifts her caresses, fickle dame,</l>

lines.text: Now kind to me, and now to him:
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="52">Now kind to me, and now to him:</l>

lines.text: She stays; 'tis well: but let her shake
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="53">She stays; 'tis well: but let her shake</l>

lines.text: Those wings, her presents I resign,
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="54">Those wings, her presents I resign,</l>

lines.text: Cloak me in native worth, and take
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="55">Cloak me in native worth, and take</l>
<l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="56">Chaste Poverty undower'd for mine.</l>

lines.text: Though storms around my vessel rave,
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="57">Though storms around my vessel rave,</l>

lines.text: I will not fall to craven prayers,
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="58">I will not fall to craven prayers,</l>

lines.text: Nor bargain by my vows to save
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="59">Nor bargain by my vows to save</l>
<l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="60">My Cyprian and Sidonian wares,</l>

lines.text: Else added to the insatiate main.
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="61">Else added to the insatiate main.</l>

lines.text: Then through the wild Aegean roar
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="62">Then through the wild <placeName key="tgn,7002675">Aegean</placeName> roar</l>

lines.text: The breezes and the Brethren Twain
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="63">The breezes and the Brethren Twain</l>

lines.text: Shall waft my little boat ashore.
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="64">Shall waft my little boat ashore.</l>

edition: John Conington; George Bell and Sons, London 1882

lines.text: And now 'tis done: more durable than brass
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="1">And now 'tis done: more durable than brass</l>

lines.text: My monument shall be, and raise its head
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="2">My monument shall be, and raise its head</l>

lines.text: O'er royal pyramids: it shall not dread
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="3">O'er royal pyramids: it shall not dread</l>
<l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="4">Corroding rain or angry Boreas,</l>

lines.text: Nor the long lapse of immemorial time.
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="5">Nor the long lapse of immemorial time.</l>

lines.text: I shall not wholly die: large residue
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="6">I shall not wholly die: large residue</l>

lines.text: Shall 'scape the queen of funerals. Ever new
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="7">Shall 'scape the queen of funerals.  Ever new</l>

lines.text: My after fame shall grow, while pontiffs climb
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="8">My after fame shall grow, while pontiffs climb</l>

lines.text: With silent maids the Capitolian height.
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="9">With silent maids the Capitolian height.</l>

lines.text: “Born,” men will say, “where Aufidus is loud,
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="10">“Born,” men will say, “where Aufidus is loud,</l>

lines.text: Where Daunus, scant of streams, beneath him bow'd
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="11">Where Daunus, scant of streams, beneath him bow'd</l>

lines.text: The rustic tribes, from dimness he wax'd bright,
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="12">The rustic tribes, from dimness he wax'd bright,</l>

lines.text: First of his race to wed the Aeolian lay
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="13">First of his race to wed the Aeolian lay</l>

lines.text: To notes of Italy.” Put glory on,
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="14">To notes of <placeName key="tgn,1000080">Italy</placeName>.”  Put glory on,</l>

lines.text: My own Melpomene, by genius won,
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="15">My own Melpomene, by genius won,</l>

lines.text: And crown me of thy grace with Delphic bay.
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="16">And crown me of thy grace with Delphic bay.</l>

edition: John Conington; George Bell and Sons, London 1882

lines.text: Yet again thou wak'st the flame
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="1">Yet again thou wak'st the flame</l>

lines.text: That long had slumber'd! Spare me, Venus, spare!
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="2">That long had slumber'd!  Spare me, Venus, spare!</l>

lines.text: Trust me, I am not the same
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="3">Trust me, I am not the same</l>

lines.text: As in the reign of Cinara, kind and fair.
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="4">As in the reign of Cinara, kind and fair.</l>

lines.text: Cease thy softening spells to prove
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="5">Cease thy softening spells to prove</l>

lines.text: On this old heart, by fifty years made hard,
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="6">On this old heart, by fifty years made hard,</l>
<l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="7">Cruel Mother of sweet Love!</l>

lines.text: Haste, where gay youth solicits thy regard.
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="8">Haste, where gay youth solicits thy regard.</l>
<l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="9">With thy purple cygnets fly</l>

lines.text: To Paullus' door, a seasonable guest;
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="10">To Paullus' door, a seasonable guest;</l>
<l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="11">There within hold revelry,</l>

lines.text: There light thy flame in that congenial breast.
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="12">There light thy flame in that congenial breast.</l>

lines.text: He, with birth and beauty graced,
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="13">He, with birth and beauty graced,</l>

lines.text: The trembling client's champion, ne'er tongue-tied,
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="14">The trembling client's champion, ne'er tongue-tied,</l>
<l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="15">Master of each manly taste,</l>

lines.text: Shall bear thy conquering banners far and wide.
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="16">Shall bear thy conquering banners far and wide.</l>

lines.text: Let him smile in triumph gay,
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="17">Let him smile in triumph gay,</l>

lines.text: True heart, victorious over lavish hand,
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="18">True heart, victorious over lavish hand,</l>

lines.text: By the Alban lake that day
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="19">By the Alban lake that day</l>

lines.text: 'Neath citron roof all marble shalt thou stand:
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="20">'Neath citron roof all marble shalt thou stand:</l>
<l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="21">Incense there and fragrant spice</l>

lines.text: With odorous fumes thy nostrils shall salute;
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="22">With odorous fumes thy nostrils shall salute;</l>
<l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="23">Blended notes thine ear entice,</l>

lines.text: The lyre, the pipe, the Berecyntine flute:
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="24">The lyre, the pipe, the Berecyntine flute:</l>
<l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="25">Graceful youths and maidens bright</l>

lines.text: Shall twice a day thy tuneful praise resound,
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="26">Shall twice a day thy tuneful praise resound,</l>

lines.text: While their feet, so fair and white,
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="27">While their feet, so fair and white,</l>

lines.text: In Salian measure three times beat the ground.
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="28">In Salian measure three times beat the ground.</l>

lines.text: I can relish love no more,
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="29">I can relish love no more,</l>

lines.text: Nor flattering hopes that tell me hearts are true,
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="30">Nor flattering hopes that tell me hearts are true,</l>
<l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="31">Nor the revel's loud uproar,</l>

lines.text: Nor fresh-wreathed flowerets, bathed in vernal dew.
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="32">Nor fresh-wreathed flowerets, bathed in vernal dew.</l>
<l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="33">Ah! but why, my Ligurine,</l>

lines.text: Steal trickling tear-drops down my wasted cheek?
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="34">Steal trickling tear-drops down my wasted cheek?</l>

lines.text: Wherefore halts this tongue of mine,
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="35">Wherefore halts this tongue of mine,</l>

lines.text: So eloquent once, so faltering now and weak?
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="36">So eloquent once, so faltering now and weak?</l>

lines.text: Now I hold you in my chain,
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="37">Now I hold you in my chain,</l>

lines.text: And clasp you close, all in a nightly dream;
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="38">And clasp you close, all in a nightly dream;</l>

lines.text: Now, still dreaming, o'er the plain
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="39">Now, still dreaming, o'er the plain</l>

lines.text: I chase you; now, ah cruel! down the stream.
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="40">I chase you; now, ah cruel! down the stream.</l>

edition: John Conington; George Bell and Sons, London 1882

lines.text: Who fain at Pindar's flight would aim,
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="1">Who fain at Pindar's flight would aim,</l>
<l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="2">On waxen wings, Iulus, he</l>

lines.text: Soars heavenward, doom'd to give his name
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="3">Soars heavenward, doom'd to give his name</l>
<l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="4">To some new sea.</l>

lines.text: Pindar, like torrent from the steep
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="5">Pindar, like torrent from the steep</l>

lines.text: Which, swollen with rain, its banks o'erflows,
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="6">Which, swollen with rain, its banks o'erflows,</l>
<l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="7">With mouth unfathomably deep,</l>
<l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="8">Foams, thunders, glows,</l>
<l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="9">All worthy of Apollo's bay,</l>
<l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="10">Whether in dithyrambic roll</l>

lines.text: Pouring new words he burst away
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="11">Pouring new words he burst away</l>
<l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="12">Beyond control,</l>

lines.text: Or gods and god-born heroes tell,
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="13">Or gods and god-born heroes tell,</l>

lines.text: Whose arm with righteous death could tame
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="14">Whose arm with righteous death could tame</l>
<l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="15">Grim Centaurs, tame Chimaeras fell,</l>
<l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="16">Out-breathing flame,</l>

lines.text: Or bid the boxer or the steed
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="17">Or bid the boxer or the steed</l>

lines.text: In deathless pride of victory live,
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="18">In deathless pride of victory live,</l>

lines.text: And dower them with a nobler meed
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="19">And dower them with a nobler meed</l>
<l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="20">Than sculptors give,</l>

lines.text: Or mourn the bridegroom early torn
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="21">Or mourn the bridegroom early torn</l>

lines.text: From his young bride, and set on high
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="22">From his young bride, and set on high</l>
<l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="23">Strength, courage, virtue's golden morn,</l>
<l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="24">Too good to die.</l>

lines.text: Antonius! yes, the winds blow free,
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="25">Antonius! yes, the winds blow free,</l>

lines.text: When Dirce's swan ascends the skies,
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="26">When Dirce's swan ascends the skies,</l>

lines.text: To waft him. I, like Matine bee,
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="27">To waft him.  I, like Matine bee,</l>
<l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="28">In act and guise,</l>

lines.text: That culls its sweets through toilsome hours,
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="29">That culls its sweets through toilsome hours,</l>
<l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="30">Am roaming <placeName key="perseus,Tibur">Tibur</placeName>'s banks along,</l>
<l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="31">And fashioning with puny powers</l>
<l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="32">A laboured song.</l>

lines.text: Your Muse shall sing in loftier strain
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="33">Your Muse shall sing in loftier strain</l>

lines.text: How Caesar climbs the sacred height,
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="34">How Caesar climbs the sacred height,</l>

lines.text: The fierce Sygambrians in his train,
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="35">The fierce Sygambrians in his train,</l>
<l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="36">With laurel dight,</l>

lines.text: Than whom the Fates ne'er gave mankind
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="37">Than whom the Fates ne'er gave mankind</l>

lines.text: A richer treasure or more dear,
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="38">A richer treasure or more dear,</l>

lines.text: Nor shall, though earth again should find
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="39">Nor shall, though earth again should find</l>
<l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="40">The golden year.</l>

lines.text: Your Muse shall tell of public sports,
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="41">Your Muse shall tell of public sports,</l>
<l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="42">And holyday, and votive feast,</l>

lines.text: For Caesar's sake, and brawling courts
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="43">For Caesar's sake, and brawling courts</l>
<l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="44">Where strife has ceased.</l>

lines.text: Then, if my voice can aught avail,
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="45">Then, if my voice can aught avail,</l>

lines.text: Grateful for him our prayers have won,
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="46">Grateful for him our prayers have won,</l>

lines.text: My song shall echo, “Hail, all hail,
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="47">My song shall echo, “Hail, all hail,</l>
<l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="48">Auspicious Sun!”</l>

lines.text: There as you move, “Ho! Triumph, ho!
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="49">There as you move, “Ho! Triumph, ho!</l>

lines.text: Great Triumph!” once and yet again
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="50">Great Triumph!” once and yet again</l>

lines.text: All Rome shall cry, and spices strow
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="51">All <placeName key="perseus,Rome">Rome</placeName> shall cry, and spices strow</l>
<l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="52">Before your train.</l>

lines.text: Ten bulls, ten kine, your debt discharge:
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="53">Ten bulls, ten kine, your debt discharge:</l>

lines.text: A calf new-wean'd from parent cow,
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="54">A calf new-wean'd from parent cow,</l>

lines.text: Battening on pastures rich and large,
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="55">Battening on pastures rich and large,</l>
<l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="56">Shall quit my vow.</l>

lines.text: Like moon just dawning on the night
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="57">Like moon just dawning on the night</l>

lines.text: The crescent honours of his head;
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="58">The crescent honours of his head;</l>

lines.text: One dapple spot of snowy white,
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="59">One dapple spot of snowy white,</l>
<l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="60">The rest all red.</l>

edition: John Conington; George Bell and Sons, London 1882

lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="1">He whom thou, Melpomene,</l>

lines.text: Hast welcomed with thy smile, in life arriving,
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="2">Hast welcomed with thy smile, in life arriving,</l>

lines.text: Ne'er by boxer's skill shall be
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="3">Ne'er by boxer's skill shall be</l>

lines.text: Renown'd abroad, for Isthmian mastery striving;
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="4">Renown'd abroad, for Isthmian mastery striving;</l>
<l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="5">Him shall never fiery steed</l>

lines.text: Draw in Achaean car a conqueror seated;
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="6">Draw in Achaean car a conqueror seated;</l>
<l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="7">Him shall never martial deed</l>

lines.text: Show, crown'd with bay, after proud kings defeated,
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="8">Show, crown'd with bay, after proud kings defeated,</l>
<l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="9">Climbing Capitolian steep:</l>

lines.text: But the cool streams that make green Tibur flourish,
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="10">But the cool streams that make green <placeName key="perseus,Tibur">Tibur</placeName> flourish,</l>
<l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="11">And the tangled forest deep,</l>

lines.text: On soft Aeolian airs his fame shall nourish.
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="12">On soft Aeolian airs his fame shall nourish.</l>

lines.text: Rome, of cities first and best,
lines.xml:
<l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="13">
                        <placeName key="perseus,Rome">Rome</placeName>, of cities first and best,</l>

lines.text: Deigns by her sons' according voice to hail me
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="14">Deigns by her sons' according voice to hail me</l>
<l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="15">Fellow-bard of poets blest,</l>

lines.text: And faint and fainter envy's growls assail me.
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="16">And faint and fainter envy's growls assail me.</l>
<l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="17">Goddess, whose Pierian art</l>

lines.text: The lyre's sweet sounds can modulate and measure,
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="18">The lyre's sweet sounds can modulate and measure,</l>

lines.text: Who to dumb fish canst impart
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="19">Who to dumb fish canst impart</l>

lines.text: The music of the swan, if such thy pleasure:
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="20">The music of the swan, if such thy pleasure:</l>

lines.text: O, 'tis all of thy dear grace
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="21">O, 'tis all of thy dear grace</l>

lines.text: That every finger points me out in going
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="22">That every finger points me out in going</l>
<l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="23">Lyrist of the Roman race;</l>

lines.text: Breath, power to charm, if mine, are thy bestowing!
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="24">Breath, power to charm, if mine, are thy bestowing!</l>

edition: John Conington; George Bell and Sons, London 1882

lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="1">E'en as the lightning's minister,</l>

lines.text: Whom Jove o'er all the feather'd breed
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="2">Whom Jove o'er all the feather'd breed</l>

lines.text: Made sovereign, having proved him sure
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="3">Made sovereign, having proved him sure</l>
<l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="4">Erewhile on auburn Ganymede;</l>

lines.text: Stirr'd by warm youth and inborn power,
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="5">Stirr'd by warm youth and inborn power,</l>

lines.text: He quits the nest with timorous wing,
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="6">He quits the nest with timorous wing,</l>

lines.text: For winter's storms have ceased to lower,
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="7">For winter's storms have ceased to lower,</l>
<l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="8">And zephyrs of returuing spring</l>

lines.text: Tempt him to launch on unknown skies
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="9">Tempt him to launch on unknown skies</l>

lines.text: Next on the fold he stoops downright;
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="10">Next on the fold he stoops downright;</l>
<l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="11">Last on resisting serpents flies,</l>

lines.text: Athirst for foray and for flight:
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="12">Athirst for foray and for flight:</l>

lines.text: As tender kidling on the grass
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="13">As tender kidling on the grass</l>
<l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="14">Espies, uplooking from her food,</l>

lines.text: A lion's whelp, and knows, alas!
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="15">A lion's whelp, and knows, alas!</l>

lines.text: Those new-set teeth shall drink her blood:
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="16">Those new-set teeth shall drink her blood:</l>
<l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="17">So look'd the Raetian mountaineers</l>
<l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="18">On Drusus:—whence in every field</l>
<l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="19">They learn'd through immemorial years</l>
<l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="20">The Amazonian axe to wield,</l>

lines.text: I ask not now: not all of truth
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="21">I ask not now: not all of truth</l>

lines.text: We seekers find: enough to know
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="22">We seekers find: enough to know</l>

lines.text: The wisdom of the princely youth
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="23">The wisdom of the princely youth</l>

lines.text: Has taught our erst victorious foe
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="24">Has taught our erst victorious foe</l>

lines.text: What prowess dwells in boyish hearts
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="25">What prowess dwells in boyish hearts</l>

lines.text: Rear'd in the shrine of a pure home,
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="26">Rear'd in the shrine of a pure home,</l>
<l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="27">What strength Augustus' love imparts</l>

lines.text: To Nero's seed, the hope of Rome.
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="28">To Nero's seed, the hope of <placeName key="perseus,Rome">Rome</placeName>.</l>

lines.text: Good sons and brave good sires approve:
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="29">Good sons and brave good sires approve:</l>
<l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="30">Strong bullocks, fiery colts, attest</l>

lines.text: Their fathers' worth, nor weakling dove
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="31">Their fathers' worth, nor weakling dove</l>

lines.text: Is hatch'd in savage eagle's nest.
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="32">Is hatch'd in savage eagle's nest.</l>

lines.text: But care draws forth the power within,
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="33">But care draws forth the power within,</l>

lines.text: And cultured minds are strong for good:
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="34">And cultured minds are strong for good:</l>

lines.text: Let manners fail, the plague of sin
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="35">Let manners fail, the plague of sin</l>

lines.text: Taints e'en the course of gentle blood.
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="36">Taints e'en the course of gentle blood.</l>

lines.text: How great thy debt to Nero's race,
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="37">How great thy debt to Nero's race,</l>

lines.text: O Rome, let red Metaurus say,
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="38">O <placeName key="perseus,Rome">Rome</placeName>, let red Metaurus say,</l>
<l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="39">Slain Hasdrubal, and victory's grace</l>

lines.text: First granted on that glorious day
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="40">First granted on that glorious day</l>

lines.text: Which chased the clouds, and show'd the sun,
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="41">Which chased the clouds, and show'd the sun,</l>

<l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="42">When Hannibal o'er <placeName key="tgn,1000080">Italy</placeName>
                     </l>

lines.text: Ran, as swift flames o'er pine-woods run,
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="43">Ran, as swift flames o'er pine-woods run,</l>
<l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="44">Or Eurus o'er <placeName key="tgn,7003122">Sicilia</placeName>'s sea.</l>
<l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="45">Henceforth, by fortune aiding toil,</l>

lines.text: Rome's prowess grew: her fanes, laid waste
lines.xml:
<l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="46">
                        <placeName key="perseus,Rome">Rome</placeName>'s prowess grew: her fanes, laid waste</l>
<l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="47">By Punic sacrilege and spoil,</l>

lines.text: Beheld at length their gods replaced.
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="48">Beheld at length their gods replaced.</l>

lines.text: Then the false Libyan own'd his doom:—
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="49">Then the false Libyan own'd his doom:—</l>
<l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="50">“Weak deer, the wolves' predestined prey,</l>

lines.text: Blindly we rush on foes, from whom
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="51">Blindly we rush on foes, from whom</l>
<l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="52">'Twere triumph won to steal away.</l>

lines.text: That race which, strong from Ilion's fires,
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="53">That race which, strong from <placeName key="tgn,7002329">Ilion</placeName>'s fires,</l>

lines.text: Its gods, on Tuscan waters tost,
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="54">Its gods, on Tuscan waters tost,</l>
<l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="55">Its sons, its venerable sires,</l>
<l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="56">Bore to Ausonia's citied coast;</l>

lines.text: That race, like oak by axes shorn
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="57">That race, like oak by axes shorn</l>

lines.text: On Algidus with dark leaves rife,
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="58">On Algidus with dark leaves rife,</l>

lines.text: Laughs carnage, havoc, all to scorn,
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="59">Laughs carnage, havoc, all to scorn,</l>

lines.text: And draws new spirit from the knife.
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="60">And draws new spirit from the knife.</l>

lines.text: Not the lopp'd Hydra task'd so sore
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="61">Not the lopp'd Hydra task'd so sore</l>
<l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="62">Alcides, chafing at the foil:</l>

lines.text: No pest so fell was born of yore
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="63">No pest so fell was born of yore</l>

lines.text: From Colchian or from Theban soil.
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="64">From Colchian or from Theban soil.</l>

lines.text: Plunged in the deep, it mounts to sight
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="65">Plunged in the deep, it mounts to sight</l>

lines.text: More splendid: grappled, it will quell
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="66">More splendid: grappled, it will quell</l>

lines.text: Unbroken powers, and fight a fight
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="67">Unbroken powers, and fight a fight</l>

lines.text: Whose story widow'd wives shall tell.
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="68">Whose story widow'd wives shall tell.</l>

lines.text: No heralds shall my deeds proclaim
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="69">No heralds shall my deeds proclaim</l>

lines.text: To Carthage now: lost, lost is all:
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="70">To <placeName key="perseus,Carthage">Carthage</placeName> now: lost, lost is all:</l>

lines.text: A nation's hope, a nation's name,
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="71">A nation's hope, a nation's name,</l>
<l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="72">They died with dying Hasdrubal.”</l>

lines.text: What will not Claudian hands achieve?
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="73">What will not Claudian hands achieve?</l>

lines.text: Jove's favour is their guiding star,
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="74">Jove's favour is their guiding star,</l>
<l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="75">And watchful potencies unweave</l>

lines.text: For them the tangled paths of war.
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="76">For them the tangled paths of war.</l>

edition: John Conington; George Bell and Sons, London 1882

lines.text: Best guardian of Rome's people, dearest boon
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="1">Best guardian of <placeName key="perseus,Rome">Rome</placeName>'s people, dearest boon</l>

lines.text: Of a kind Heaven, thou lingerest all too long:
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="2">Of a kind Heaven, thou lingerest all too long:</l>

lines.text: Thou bad'st thy senate look to meet thee soon:
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="3">Thou bad'st thy senate look to meet thee soon:</l>
<l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="4">Do not thy promise wrong.</l>

lines.text: Restore, dear chief, the light thou tak'st away:
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="5">Restore, dear chief, the light thou tak'st away:</l>

lines.text: Ah! when, like spring, that gracious mien of thine
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="6">Ah! when, like spring, that gracious mien of thine</l>

lines.text: Dawns on thy Rome, more gently glides the day,
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="7">Dawns on thy <placeName key="perseus,Rome">Rome</placeName>, more gently glides the day,</l>
<l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="8">And suns serener shine.</l>

lines.text: See her whose darling child a long year past
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="9">See her whose darling child a long year past</l>

lines.text: Has dwelt beyond the wild Carpathian foam;
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="10">Has dwelt beyond the wild Carpathian foam;</l>

lines.text: That long year o'er, the envious southern blast
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="11">That long year o'er, the envious southern blast</l>

lines.text: Still bars him from his home:
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="12">Still bars him from his home:</l>

lines.text: Weeping and praying to the shore she clings,
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="13">Weeping and praying to the shore she clings,</l>

lines.text: Nor ever thence her straining eyesight turns:
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="14">Nor ever thence her straining eyesight turns:</l>

lines.text: So, smit by loyal passion's restless stings,
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="15">So, smit by loyal passion's restless stings,</l>

<l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="16">
                        <placeName key="perseus,Rome">Rome</placeName> for her Caesar yearns.</l>

lines.text: In safety range the cattle o'er the mead:
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="17">In safety range the cattle o'er the mead:</l>

lines.text: Sweet Peace, soft Plenty, swell the golden grain:
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="18">Sweet Peace, soft Plenty, swell the golden grain:</l>

lines.text: O'er unvex'd seas the sailors blithely speed:
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="19">O'er unvex'd seas the sailors blithely speed:</l>
<l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="20">Fair Honour shrinks from stain:</l>

lines.text: No guilty lusts the shrine of home defile:
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="21">No guilty lusts the shrine of home defile:</l>

lines.text: Cleansed is the hand without, the heart within:
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="22">Cleansed is the hand without, the heart within:</l>

lines.text: The father's features in his children smile
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="23">The father's features in his children smile</l>
<l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="24">Swift vengeance follows sin.</l>

lines.text: Who fears the Parthian or the Scythian horde,
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="25">Who fears the Parthian or the Scythian horde,</l>

lines.text: Or the rank growth that German forests yield,
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="26">Or the rank growth that German forests yield,</l>

lines.text: While Caesar lives? who trembles at the sword
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="27">While Caesar lives? who trembles at the sword</l>
<l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="28">The fierce Iberians wield?</l>

lines.text: In his own hills each labours down the day,
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="29">In his own hills each labours down the day,</l>

lines.text: Teaching the vine to clasp the widow'd tree:
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="30">Teaching the vine to clasp the widow'd tree:</l>

lines.text: Then to his cups again, where, feasting gay,
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="31">Then to his cups again, where, feasting gay,</l>

lines.text: He hails his god in thee.
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="32">He hails his god in thee.</l>

lines.text: A household power, adored with prayers and wine,
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="33">A household power, adored with prayers and wine,</l>

lines.text: Thou reign'st auspicious o'er his hour of ease:
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="34">Thou reign'st auspicious o'er his hour of ease:</l>

lines.text: Thus grateful Greece her Castor made divine,
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="35">Thus grateful <placeName key="tgn,1000074">Greece</placeName> her Castor made divine,</l>
<l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="36">And her great Hercules.</l>

lines.text: Ah! be it thine long holydays to give
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="37">Ah! be it thine long holydays to give</l>

lines.text: To thy Hesperia! thus, dear chief, we pray
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="38">To thy Hesperia! thus, dear chief, we pray</l>

lines.text: At sober sunrise; thus at mellow eve,
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="39">At sober sunrise; thus at mellow eve,</l>
<l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="40">When ocean hides the day.</l>

edition: John Conington; George Bell and Sons, London 1882

lines.text: Thou who didst make thy vengeful might
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="1">Thou who didst make thy vengeful might</l>
<l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="2">To Niobe and Tityos known,</l>

lines.text: And Peleus' son, when Troy's tall height
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="3">And Peleus' son, when <placeName key="perseus,Troy">Troy</placeName>'s tall height</l>
<l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="4">Was nigh his own,</l>

lines.text: Victorious else, for thee no peer,
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="5">Victorious else, for thee no peer,</l>

lines.text: Though, strong in his sea-parent's power,
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="6">Though, strong in his sea-parent's power,</l>

lines.text: He shook with that tremendous spear
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="7">He shook with that tremendous spear</l>
<l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="8">The Dardan tower.</l>

lines.text: He, like a pine by axes sped,
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="9">He, like a pine by axes sped,</l>

lines.text: Or cypress sway'd by angry gust,
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="10">Or cypress sway'd by angry gust,</l>

lines.text: Fell ruining, and laid his head
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="11">Fell ruining, and laid his head</l>
<l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="12">In Trojan dust.</l>

lines.text: Not his to lie in covert pent
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="13">Not his to lie in covert pent</l>

lines.text: Of the false steed, and sudden fall
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="14">Of the false steed, and sudden fall</l>
<l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="15">On Priam's ill-starr'd merriment</l>
<l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="16">In bower and hail:</l>

lines.text: His ruthless arm in broad bare day
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="17">His ruthless arm in broad bare day</l>

lines.text: The infant from the breast had torn,
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="18">The infant from the breast had torn,</l>

lines.text: Nay, given to flame, ah, well a way!
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="19">Nay, given to flame, ah, well a way!</l>
<l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="20">The babe unborn:</l>

lines.text: But, won by Venus' voice and thine,
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="21">But, won by Venus' voice and thine,</l>
<l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="22">Relenting Jove Aeneas will'd</l>
<l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="23">With other omens more benign</l>
<l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="24">New walls to build.</l>

lines.text: Sweet tuner of the Grecian lyre,
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="25">Sweet tuner of the Grecian lyre,</l>

lines.text: Whose locks are laved in Xanthus' dews,
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="26">Whose locks are laved in <placeName key="tgn,7002633">Xanthus</placeName>' dews,</l>
<l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="27">Blooming Agyieus! help, inspire</l>
<l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="28">My Daunian Muse!</l>
<l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="29">'Tis Phoebus, Phoebus gifts my tongue</l>

lines.text: With minstrel art and minstrel fires:
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="30">With minstrel art and minstrel fires:</l>

lines.text: Come, noble youths and maidens sprung
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="31">Come, noble youths and maidens sprung</l>
<l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="32">From noble sires,</l>

lines.text: Blest in your Dian's guardian smile,
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="33">Blest in your Dian's guardian smile,</l>

lines.text: Whose shafts the flying silvans stay,
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="34">Whose shafts the flying silvans stay,</l>

lines.text: Come, foot the Lesbian measure, while
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="35">Come, foot the Lesbian measure, while</l>
<l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="36">The lyre I play:</l>
<l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="37">Sing of <placeName key="tgn,2013536">Latona</placeName>'s glorious boy,</l>

lines.text: Sing of night's queen with crescent horn,
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="38">Sing of night's queen with crescent horn,</l>

lines.text: Who wings the fleeting months with joy,
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="39">Who wings the fleeting months with joy,</l>
<l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="40">And swells the corn.</l>

lines.text: And happy brides shall say, “'Twas mine,
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="41">And happy brides shall say, “'Twas mine,</l>

lines.text: When years the cyclic season brought,
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="42">When years the cyclic season brought,</l>

lines.text: To chant the festal hymn divine
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="43">To chant the festal hymn divine</l>
<l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="44">By <name>Horace</name> taught.”</l>

edition: John Conington; George Bell and Sons, London 1882

lines.text: The snow is fled: the trees their leaves put on,
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="1">The snow is fled: the trees their leaves put on,</l>
<l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="2">The fields their green:</l>

lines.text: Earth owns the change, and rivers lessening run
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="3">Earth owns the change, and rivers lessening run</l>
<l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="4">Their banks between.</l>

lines.text: Naked the Nymphs and Graces in the meads
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="5">Naked the Nymphs and Graces in the meads</l>
<l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="6">The dance essay:</l>

lines.text: “No 'scaping death” proclaims the year, that speeds
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="7">“No 'scaping death” proclaims the year, that speeds</l>
<l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="8">This sweet spring day.</l>

lines.text: Frosts yield to zephyrs; Summer drives out Spring,
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="9">Frosts yield to zephyrs; Summer drives out Spring,</l>
<l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="10">To vanish, when</l>

lines.text: Rich Autumn sheds his fruits; round wheels the ring,—
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="11">Rich Autumn sheds his fruits; round wheels the ring,—</l>
<l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="12">Winter again!</l>

lines.text: Yet the swift moons repair Heaven's detriment:
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="13">Yet the swift moons repair Heaven's detriment:</l>
<l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="14">We, soon as thrust</l>

lines.text: Where good Aeneas, Tullus, Ancus went,
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="15">Where good Aeneas, Tullus, Ancus went,</l>
<l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="16">What are we? dust.</l>

lines.text: Can Hope assure you one more day to live
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="17">Can Hope assure you one more day to live</l>
<l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="18">From powers above?</l>

lines.text: You rescue from your heir whate'er you give
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="19">You rescue from your heir whate'er you give</l>
<l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="20">The self you love.</l>

lines.text: When life is o'er, and Minos has rehearsed
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="21">When life is o'er, and Minos has rehearsed</l>
<l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="22">The grand last doom,</l>

lines.text: Not birth, nor eloquence, nor worth, shall burst
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="23">Not birth, nor eloquence, nor worth, shall burst</l>
<l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="24">Torquatus' tomb.</l>

lines.text: Not Dian's self can chaste Hippolytus
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="25">Not Dian's self can chaste Hippolytus</l>
<l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="26">To life recall,</l>

lines.text: Nor Theseus free his loved Pirithous
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="27">Nor Theseus free his loved Pirithous</l>
<l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="28">From Lethe's thrall.</l>

edition: John Conington; George Bell and Sons, London 1882

lines.text: Ah Censorinus! to my comrades true
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="1">Ah Censorinus! to my comrades true</l>

lines.text: Rich cups, rare bronzes, gladly would I send:
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="2">Rich cups, rare bronzes, gladly would I send:</l>

lines.text: Choice tripods from Olympia on each friend
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="3">Choice tripods from <placeName key="perseus,Olympia">Olympia</placeName> on each friend</l>

lines.text: Would I confer, choicer on none than you,
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="4">Would I confer, choicer on none than you,</l>

lines.text: Had but my fate such gems of art bestow'd
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="5">Had but my fate such gems of art bestow'd</l>

lines.text: As cunning Scopas or Parrhasius wrought,
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="6">As cunning Scopas or Parrhasius wrought,</l>

lines.text: This with the brush, that with the chisel taught
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="7">This with the brush, that with the chisel taught</l>

lines.text: To image now a mortal, now a god.
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="8">To image now a mortal, now a god.</l>

lines.text: But these are not my riches: your desire
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="9">But these are not my riches: your desire</l>

lines.text: Such luxury craves not, and your means disdain:
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="10">Such luxury craves not, and your means disdain:</l>

lines.text: A poet's strain you love; a poet's strain
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="11">A poet's strain you love; a poet's strain</l>

lines.text: Accept, and learn the value of the lyre.
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="12">Accept, and learn the value of the lyre.</l>

lines.text: Not public gravings on a marble base,
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="13">Not public gravings on a marble base,</l>

lines.text: Whence comes a second life to men of might
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="14">Whence comes a second life to men of might</l>

lines.text: E'en in the tomb: not Hannibal's swift flight,
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="15">E'en in the tomb: not Hannibal's swift flight,</l>

lines.text: Nor those fierce threats flung back into his face,
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="16">Nor those fierce threats flung back into his face,</l>

lines.text: Not impious Carthage in its last red blaze,
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="17">Not impious <placeName key="perseus,Carthage">Carthage</placeName> in its last red blaze,</l>

lines.text: In clearer light sets forth his spotless fame,
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="18">In clearer light sets forth his spotless fame,</l>

lines.text: Who from crush'd Afric took away—a name,
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="19">Who from crush'd Afric took away—a name,</l>
<l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="20">Than rude <placeName key="tgn,7007850">Calabria</placeName>'s tributary lays.</l>

lines.text: Let silence hide the good your hand has wrought,
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="21">Let silence hide the good your hand has wrought,</l>

lines.text: Farewell, reward! Had blank oblivion's power
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="22">Farewell, reward! Had blank oblivion's power</l>

lines.text: Dimm'd the bright deeds of Romulus, at this hour,
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="23">Dimm'd the bright deeds of Romulus, at this hour,</l>

lines.text: Despite his sire and mother, he were nought.
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="24">Despite his sire and mother, he were nought.</l>

lines.text: Thus Aeacus has 'scaped the Stygian wave,
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="25">Thus Aeacus has 'scaped the Stygian wave,</l>

lines.text: By grace of poets and their silver tongue,
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="26">By grace of poets and their silver tongue,</l>

lines.text: Henceforth to live the happy isles among.
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="27">Henceforth to live the happy isles among.</l>

lines.text: No, trust the Muse: she opes the good man's grave,
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="28">No, trust the Muse: she opes the good man's grave,</l>

lines.text: And lifts him to the gods. So Hercules,
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="29">And lifts him to the gods.  So Hercules,</l>

lines.text: His labours o'er, sits at the board of Jove:
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="30">His labours o'er, sits at the board of Jove:</l>

lines.text: So Tyndareus' offspring shine as stars above,
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="31">So Tyndareus' offspring shine as stars above,</l>

lines.text: Saving lorn vessels from the yawning seas:
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="32">Saving lorn vessels from the yawning seas:</l>

lines.text: So Bacchus, with the vine-wreath round his hair,
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="33">So Bacchus, with the vine-wreath round his hair,</l>

lines.text: Gives prosperous issue to his votary's prayer.
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="34">Gives prosperous issue to his votary's prayer.</l>

edition: John Conington; George Bell and Sons, London 1882

lines.text: Think not those strains can e'er expire,
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="1">Think not those strains can e'er expire,</l>
<l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="2">Which, cradled 'mid the echoing roar</l>
<l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="3">Of <placeName key="tgn,1128017">Aufidus</placeName>, to <placeName key="tgn,7003080">Latium</placeName>'s lyre</l>

lines.text: I sing with arts unknown before.
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="4">I sing with arts unknown before.</l>

lines.text: Though Homer fill the foremost throne,
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="5">Though Homer fill the foremost throne,</l>

lines.text: Yet grave Stesichorus still can please,
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="6">Yet grave Stesichorus still can please,</l>

lines.text: And fierce Alcaeus holds his own
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="7">And fierce Alcaeus holds his own</l>
<l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="8">With Pindar and Simonides.</l>

lines.text: The songs of Teos are not mute,
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="9">The songs of <placeName key="perseus,Teos">Teos</placeName> are not mute,</l>

lines.text: And Sappho's love is breathing still:
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="10">And Sappho's love is breathing still:</l>

lines.text: She told her secret to the lute,
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="11">She told her secret to the lute,</l>

lines.text: And yet its chords with passion thrill.
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="12">And yet its chords with passion thrill.</l>

lines.text: Not Sparta's queen alone was fired
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="13">Not <placeName key="perseus,Sparta">Sparta</placeName>'s queen alone was fired</l>

lines.text: By broider'd robe and braided tress,
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="14">By broider'd robe and braided tress,</l>

lines.text: And all the splendours that attired
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="15">And all the splendours that attired</l>
<l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="16">Her lover's guilty loveliness:</l>

lines.text: Not only Teucer to the field
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="17">Not only Teucer to the field</l>

<l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="18">His arrows brought, nor <placeName key="tgn,7002329">Ilion</placeName>
                     </l>
<l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="19">Beneath a single conqueror reel'd:</l>
<l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="20">Not <placeName key="tgn,7012056">Crete</placeName>'s majestic lord alone,</l>

lines.text: Or Sthenelus, earn'd the Muses' crown:
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="21">Or Sthenelus, earn'd the Muses' crown:</l>

lines.text: Not Hector first for child and wife,
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="22">Not Hector first for child and wife,</l>
<l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="23">Or brave Deiphobus, laid down</l>

lines.text: The burden of a manly life.
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="24">The burden of a manly life.</l>
<l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="25">Before Atrides men were brave:</l>

lines.text: But ah! oblivion, dark and long,
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="26">But ah! oblivion, dark and long,</l>

lines.text: Has lock'd them in a tearless grave,
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="27">Has lock'd them in a tearless grave,</l>
<l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="28">For lack of consecrating song.</l>

lines.text: 'Twixt worth and baseness, lapp'd in death,
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="29">'Twixt worth and baseness, lapp'd in death,</l>

lines.text: What difference? You shall ne'er be dumb,
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="30">What difference? You shall ne'er be dumb,</l>

lines.text: While strains of mine have voice and breath:
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="31">While strains of mine have voice and breath:</l>

lines.text: The dull neglect of days to come
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="32">The dull neglect of days to come</l>

lines.text: Those hard-won honours shall not blight:
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="33">Those hard-won honours shall not blight:</l>

lines.text: No, Lollius, no: a soul is yours,
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="34">No, Lollius, no: a soul is yours,</l>
<l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="35">Clear-sighted, keen, alike upright</l>

lines.text: When fortune smiles, and when she lowers:
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="36">When fortune smiles, and when she lowers:</l>

lines.text: To greed and rapine still severe,
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="37">To greed and rapine still severe,</l>

lines.text: Spurning the gain men find so sweet:
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="38">Spurning the gain men find so sweet:</l>

lines.text: A consul, not of one brief year,
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="39">A consul, not of one brief year,</l>

lines.text: But oft as on the judgment-seat
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="40">But oft as on the judgment-seat</l>

lines.text: You bend the expedient to the right,
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="41">You bend the expedient to the right,</l>

lines.text: Turn haughty eyes from bribes away,
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="42">Turn haughty eyes from bribes away,</l>
