lines.text: Or bear your banners through the fight,
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="43">Or bear your banners through the fight,</l>
<l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="44">Scattering the foeman's firm array.</l>
<l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="45">The lord of boundless revenues,</l>

lines.text: Salute not him as happy: no,
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="46">Salute not him as happy: no,</l>

lines.text: Call him the happy, who can use
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="47">Call him the happy, who can use</l>

lines.text: The bounty that the gods bestow,
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="48">The bounty that the gods bestow,</l>

lines.text: Can bear the load of poverty,
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="49">Can bear the load of poverty,</l>

lines.text: And tremble not at death, but sin:
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="50">And tremble not at death, but sin:</l>

lines.text: No recreant he when called to die
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="51">No recreant he when called to die</l>

lines.text: In cause of country or of kin.
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="52">In cause of country or of kin.</l>

edition: John Conington; George Bell and Sons, London 1882

lines.text: Here is a cask of Alban, more
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="1">Here is a cask of <placeName key="tgn,1031727">Alban</placeName>, more</l>

lines.text: Than nine years old: here grows for you
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="2">Than nine years old: here grows for you</l>

lines.text: Green parsley, Phyllis, and good store
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="3">Green parsley, Phyllis, and good store</l>
<l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="4">Of ivy too</l>

lines.text: (Wreathed ivy suits your hair, you know):
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="5">(Wreathed ivy suits your hair, you know):</l>

lines.text: The plate shines bright: the altar, strew'd
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="6">The plate shines bright: the altar, strew'd</l>

lines.text: With vervain, hungers for the flow
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="7">With vervain, hungers for the flow</l>
<l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="8">Of lambkin's blood.</l>

lines.text: There's stir among the serving folk;
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="9">There's stir among the serving folk;</l>

lines.text: They bustle, bustle, boy and girl;
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="10">They bustle, bustle, boy and girl;</l>

lines.text: The flickering flames send up the smoke
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="11">The flickering flames send up the smoke</l>
<l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="12">In many a curl.</l>

lines.text: But why, you ask, this special cheer?
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="13">But why, you ask, this special cheer?</l>

lines.text: We celebrate the feast of Ides,
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="14">We celebrate the feast of Ides,</l>

lines.text: Which April's month, to Venus dear,
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="15">Which April's month, to Venus dear,</l>
<l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="16">In twain divides.</l>
<l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="17">O, 'tis a day for reverence,</l>

lines.text: E'en my own birthday scarce so dear,
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="18">E'en my own birthday scarce so dear,</l>

lines.text: For my Maecenas counts from thence
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="19">For my Maecenas counts from thence</l>
<l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="20">Each added year.</l>
<l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="21">'Tis Telephus that you'd bewitch:</l>

lines.text: But he is of a high degree;
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="22">But he is of a high degree;</l>

lines.text: Bound to a lady fair and rich,
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="23">Bound to a lady fair and rich,</l>
<l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="24">He is not free.</l>

lines.text: O think of Phaethon half burn'd,
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="25">O think of Phaethon half burn'd,</l>
<l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="26">And moderate your passion's greed:</l>
<l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="27">Think how Bellerophon was spurn'd</l>
<l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="28">By his wing'd steed.</l>

lines.text: So learn to look for partners meet,
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="29">So learn to look for partners meet,</l>

lines.text: Shun lofty things, nor raise your aims
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="30">Shun lofty things, nor raise your aims</l>

lines.text: Above your fortune. Come then, sweet,
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="31">Above your fortune. Come then, sweet,</l>
<l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="32">My last of flames</l>
<l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="33">(For never shall another fair</l>

lines.text: Enslave me), learn a tune, to sing
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="34">Enslave me), learn a tune, to sing</l>

lines.text: With that dear voice: to music care
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="35">With that dear voice: to music care</l>
<l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="36">Shall yield its sting.</l>

edition: John Conington; George Bell and Sons, London 1882

lines.text: The gales of Thrace, that hush the unquiet sea,
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="1">The gales of <placeName key="tgn,7002756">Thrace</placeName>, that hush the unquiet sea,</l>

lines.text: Spring's comrades, on the bellying canvas blow:
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="2">Spring's comrades, on the bellying canvas blow:</l>

lines.text: Clogg'd earth and brawling streams alike are free
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="3">Clogg'd earth and brawling streams alike are free</l>
<l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="4">From winter's weight of snow.</l>

lines.text: Wailing her Itys in that sad, sad strain,
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="5">Wailing her Itys in that sad, sad strain,</l>

lines.text: Builds the poor bird, reproach to after time
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="6">Builds the poor bird, reproach to after time</l>

lines.text: Of Cecrops' house, for bloody vengeance ta'en
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="7">Of Cecrops' house, for bloody vengeance ta'en</l>
<l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="8">On foul barbaric crime.</l>

lines.text: The keepers of fat lambkins chant their loves
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="9">The keepers of fat lambkins chant their loves</l>

lines.text: To silvan reeds, all in the grassy lea,
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="10">To silvan reeds, all in the grassy lea,</l>

lines.text: And pleasure Him who tends the flocks and groves
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="11">And pleasure Him who tends the flocks and groves</l>
<l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="12">Of dark-leaved Arcady.</l>

lines.text: It is a thirsty season, Virgil mine:
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="13">It is a thirsty season, Virgil mine:</l>

lines.text: But would you taste the grape's Calenian juice,
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="14">But would you taste the grape's Calenian juice,</l>

lines.text: Client of noble youths, to earn your wine
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="15">Client of noble youths, to earn your wine</l>
<l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="16">Some nard you must produce.</l>

lines.text: A tiny box of nard shall bring to light
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="17">A tiny box of nard shall bring to light</l>

lines.text: The cask that in Sulpician cellar lies:
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="18">The cask that in Sulpician cellar lies:</l>

lines.text: O, it can give new hopes, so fresh and bright,
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="19">O, it can give new hopes, so fresh and bright,</l>
<l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="20">And gladden gloomy eyes.</l>

lines.text: You take the bait? then come without delay
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="21">You take the bait? then come without delay</l>

lines.text: And bring your ware: be sure, 'tis not my plan
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="22">And bring your ware: be sure, 'tis not my plan</l>

lines.text: To let you drain my liquor and not pay,
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="23">To let you drain my liquor and not pay,</l>
<l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="24">As might some wealthy man.</l>

lines.text: Come, quit those covetous thoughts, those knitted brows,
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="25">Come, quit those covetous thoughts, those knitted brows,</l>

lines.text: Think on the last black embers, while you may,
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="26">Think on the last black embers, while you may,</l>

lines.text: And be for once unwise. When time allows,
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="27">And be for once unwise.  When time allows,</l>
<l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="28">'Tis sweet the fool to play.</l>

edition: John Conington; George Bell and Sons, London 1882

lines.text: The gods have heard, the gods have heard my prayer;
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="1">The gods have heard, the gods have heard my prayer;</l>

lines.text: Yes, Lyce! you are growing old, and still
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="2">Yes, Lyce! you are growing old, and still</l>
<l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="3">You struggle to look fair;</l>

lines.text: You drink, and dance, and trill
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="4">You drink, and dance, and trill</l>

lines.text: Your songs to youthful Love, in accents weak
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="5">Your songs to youthful Love, in accents weak</l>

lines.text: With wine, and age, and passion. Youthful Love!
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="6">With wine, and age, and passion. Youthful Love!</l>
<l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="7">He dwells in <placeName key="tgn,5003424">Chia</placeName>'s cheek,</l>
<l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="8">And hears her harp-strings move.</l>

lines.text: Rude boy, he flies like lightning o'er the heath
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="9">Rude boy, he flies like lightning o'er the heath</l>

lines.text: Past wither'd trees like you; you're wrinkled now;
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="10">Past wither'd trees like you; you're wrinkled now;</l>

lines.text: The white has left your teeth
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="11">The white has left your teeth</l>
<l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="12">And settled on your brow.</l>

lines.text: Your Coan silks, your jewels bright as stars,
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="13">Your Coan silks, your jewels bright as stars,</l>

lines.text: Ah no! they bring not back the days of old,
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="14">Ah no! they bring not back the days of old,</l>
<l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="15">In public calendars</l>
<l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="16">By flying Time enroll'd.</l>

lines.text: Where now that beauty? where those movements? where
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="17">Where now that beauty? where those movements? where</l>

lines.text: That colour? what of her, of her is left,
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="18">That colour? what of her, of her is left,</l>
<l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="19">Who, breathing Love's own air,</l>
<l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="20">Me of myself bereft,</l>

lines.text: Who reign'd in Cinara's stead, a fair, fair face,
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="21">Who reign'd in Cinara's stead, a fair, fair face,</l>

lines.text: Queen of sweet arts? but Fate to Cinara gave
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="22">Queen of sweet arts? but Fate to Cinara gave</l>
<l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="23">A life of little space;</l>

lines.text: And now she cheats the grave
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="24">And now she cheats the grave</l>

lines.text: Of Lyce, spared to raven's length of days,
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="25">Of Lyce, spared to raven's length of days,</l>

lines.text: That youth may see, with laughter and disgust,
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="26">That youth may see, with laughter and disgust,</l>
<l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="27">A fire-brand, once ablaze,</l>
<l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="28">Now smouldering in grey dust.</l>

edition: John Conington; George Bell and Sons, London 1882

lines.text: What honours can a grateful Rome,
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="1">What honours can a grateful <placeName key="perseus,Rome">Rome</placeName>,</l>
<l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="2">A grateful senate, Caesar, give</l>

lines.text: To make thy worth through days to come
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="3">To make thy worth through days to come</l>
<l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="4">Emblazon'd on our records live,</l>
<l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="5">Mightiest of chieftains whomsoe'er</l>

lines.text: The sun beholds from heaven on high?
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="6">The sun beholds from heaven on high?</l>

lines.text: They know thee now, thy strength in war,
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="7">They know thee now, thy strength in war,</l>
<l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="8">Those unsubdued Vindelici.</l>

lines.text: Thine was the sword that Drusus drew,
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="9">Thine was the sword that Drusus drew,</l>

lines.text: When on the Breunian hordes he fell,
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="10">When on the Breunian hordes he fell,</l>

lines.text: And storm'd the fierce Genaunian crew
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="11">And storm'd the fierce Genaunian crew</l>
<l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="12">E'en in their Alpine citadel,</l>

lines.text: And paid them back their debt twice told
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="13">And paid them back their debt twice told</l>
<l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="14">'Twas then the elder Nero came</l>

lines.text: To conflict, and in ruin roll'd
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="15">To conflict, and in ruin roll'd</l>

lines.text: Stout Raetian kernes of giant frame.
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="16">Stout Raetian kernes of giant frame.</l>

lines.text: O, 'twas a gallant sight to see
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="17">O, 'twas a gallant sight to see</l>

lines.text: The shocks that beat upon the brave
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="18">The shocks that beat upon the brave</l>

lines.text: Who chose to perish and be free!
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="19">Who chose to perish and be free!</l>

lines.text: As south winds scourge the rebel wave
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="20">As south winds scourge the rebel wave</l>

lines.text: When through rent clouds the Pleiads weep,
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="21">When through rent clouds the Pleiads weep,</l>

lines.text: So keen his force to smite, and smite
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="22">So keen his force to smite, and smite</l>

lines.text: The foe, or make his charger leap
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="23">The foe, or make his charger leap</l>

lines.text: Through the red furnace of the fight.
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="24">Through the red furnace of the fight.</l>
<l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="25">Thus Daunia's ancient river fares,</l>
<l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="26">Proud <placeName key="tgn,1128017">Aufidus</placeName>, with bull-like horn,</l>

lines.text: When swoln with choler he prepares
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="27">When swoln with choler he prepares</l>

lines.text: A deluge for the fields of corn.
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="28">A deluge for the fields of corn.</l>
<l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="29">So Claudius charged and overthrew</l>
<l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="30">The grim barbarian's mail-clad host,</l>

lines.text: The foremost and the hindmost slew,
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="31">The foremost and the hindmost slew,</l>

lines.text: And conquer'd all, and nothing lost.
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="32">And conquer'd all, and nothing lost.</l>

lines.text: The force, the forethought, were thine own,
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="33">The force, the forethought, were thine own,</l>

lines.text: Thine own the gods. The selfsame day
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="34">Thine own the gods.  The selfsame day</l>

lines.text: When, port and palace open thrown,
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="35">When, port and palace open thrown,</l>

lines.text: Low at thy footstool Egypt lay,
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="36">Low at thy footstool <placeName key="tgn,7016833">Egypt</placeName> lay,</l>

lines.text: That selfsame day, three lustres gone,
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="37">That selfsame day, three lustres gone,</l>
<l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="38">Another victory to thine hand</l>

lines.text: Was given; another field was won
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="39">Was given; another field was won</l>

lines.text: By grace of Caesar's high command.
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="40">By grace of Caesar's high command.</l>

lines.text: Thee Spanish tribes, unused to yield,
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="41">Thee Spanish tribes, unused to yield,</l>

lines.text: Mede, Indian, Scyth that knows no home,
lines.xml:
<l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="42">
                        <placeName key="tgn,1045322">Mede</placeName>, Indian, Scyth that knows no home,</l>

lines.text: Acknowledge, sword at once and shield
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="43">Acknowledge, sword at once and shield</l>
<l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="44">Of <placeName key="tgn,1000080">Italy</placeName> and queenly <placeName key="perseus,Rome">Rome</placeName>.</l>

lines.text: Ister to thee, and Tanais fleet,
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="45">Ister to thee, and <placeName key="tgn,1123466">Tanais</placeName> fleet,</l>

lines.text: And Nile that will not tell his birth,
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="46">And <placeName key="tgn,1127805">Nile</placeName> that will not tell his birth,</l>

lines.text: To thee the monstrous seas that beat
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="47">To thee the monstrous seas that beat</l>

lines.text: On Britain's coast, the end of earth,
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="48">On <placeName key="tgn,7008653">Britain</placeName>'s coast, the end of earth,</l>

lines.text: To thee the proud Iberians bow,
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="49">To thee the proud Iberians bow,</l>

lines.text: And Gauls, that scorn from death to flee;
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="50">And Gauls, that scorn from death to flee;</l>

lines.text: The fierce Sygambrian bends his brow,
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="51">The fierce Sygambrian bends his brow,</l>

lines.text: And drops his arms to worship thee.
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="52">And drops his arms to worship thee.</l>

edition: John Conington; George Bell and Sons, London 1882

lines.text: Of battles fought I fain had told,
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="1">Of battles fought I fain had told,</l>

lines.text: And conquer'd towns, when Phoebus smote
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="2">And conquer'd towns, when Phoebus smote</l>
<l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="3">His harp-string: “Sooth, 'twere over-bold.</l>

lines.text: To tempt wide seas in that frail boat.”
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="4">To tempt wide seas in that frail boat.”</l>

lines.text: Thy age, great Caesar, has restored
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="5">Thy age, great Caesar, has restored</l>

lines.text: To squalid fields the plenteous grain,
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="6">To squalid fields the plenteous grain,</l>

lines.text: Given back to Rome's almighty Lord
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="7">Given back to <placeName key="perseus,Rome">Rome</placeName>'s almighty Lord</l>

lines.text: Our standards, torn from Parthian fane,
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="8">Our standards, torn from Parthian fane,</l>
<l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="9">Has closed Quirinian Janus' gate,</l>
<l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="10">Wild passion's erring walk controll'd,</l>

lines.text: Heal'd the foul plague-spot of the state,
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="11">Heal'd the foul plague-spot of the state,</l>

lines.text: And brought again the life of old,
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="12">And brought again the life of old,</l>

lines.text: Life, by whose healthful power increased
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="13">Life, by whose healthful power increased</l>

lines.text: The glorious name of Latium spread
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="14">The glorious name of <placeName key="tgn,7003080">Latium</placeName> spread</l>

lines.text: To where the sun illumes the east
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="15">To where the sun illumes the east</l>

lines.text: From where he seeks his western bed.
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="16">From where he seeks his western bed.</l>

lines.text: While Caesar rules, no civil strife
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="17">While Caesar rules, no civil strife</l>

lines.text: Shall break our rest, nor violence rude,
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="18">Shall break our rest, nor violence rude,</l>

lines.text: Nor rage, that whets the slaughtering knife
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="19">Nor rage, that whets the slaughtering knife</l>

lines.text: And plunges wretched towns in feud.
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="20">And plunges wretched towns in feud.</l>

lines.text: The sons of Danube shall not scorn
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="21">The sons of <placeName key="tgn,7012913">Danube</placeName> shall not scorn</l>

lines.text: The Julian edicts; no, nor they
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="22">The Julian edicts; no, nor they</l>
<l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="23">By <placeName key="tgn,1123466">Tanais</placeName>' distant river horn,</l>
<l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="24">Nor <placeName key="tgn,7000231">Persia</placeName>, <placeName key="tgn,6005315">Scythia</placeName>, or Cathay.</l>

lines.text: And we on feast and working-tide,
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="25">And we on feast and working-tide,</l>
<l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="26">While Bacchus' bounties freely flow,</l>

lines.text: Our wives and children at our side,
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="27">Our wives and children at our side,</l>

lines.text: First paying Heaven the prayers we owe,
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="28">First paying Heaven the prayers we owe,</l>

lines.text: Shall sing of chiefs whose deeds are done,
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="29">Shall sing of chiefs whose deeds are done,</l>

lines.text: As wont our sires, to flute or shell,
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="30">As wont our sires, to flute or shell,</l>

lines.text: And Troy, Anchises, and the son
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="31">And <placeName key="tgn,7002329">Troy</placeName>, Anchises, and the son</l>

lines.text: Of Venus on our tongues shall dwell.
lines.xml: <l xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="32">Of Venus on our tongues shall dwell.</l>
